en: O friends, do not praise anything else; do not suffer harm.
Praise only Indra, the bull, when the soma is pressed; recite your hymns repeatedly.
Praise him who strikes down the foe, the bull who never grows old, the subduer of peoples, like a cow.
The one who causes estrangement, the one who brings reconciliation, the one who performs both, the most generous, the one who possesses both [powers].
For although these people invoke you in various ways for aid,
O Indra, let this our prayer be yours, and may it be a source of strength for you in every way.
O Maghavan, the wise singers of the enemy among men vie with one another in their inspired hymns.
Approach us and bring hither strength in many forms for our closest protection.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, I would not give you away even for a great price.
Not for a thousand, nor for ten thousand, O wielder of the thunderbolt; not for a hundred, O lord of a hundredfold wealth.
You, O Indra, are more excellent to me than my father and more so than my unbeneficial brother. And you, O Vasu, delight my mother with your abundance of wealth and your gracious bounty.
Where are you? Where are you? For your mind is indeed in many places.
O warrior, stir yourself, you who create the battle-rage, O breaker of forts; the *gāyatrī* hymns have been sung forth.
Sing forth this *gāyatra* song for him, the beloved one who is the breaker of forts.
With those [horses] by which the wielder of the thunderbolt sat upon Kaṇva’s sacred grass and shattered the fortresses;
with those horses of yours which belong to groups of ten, hundreds, and thousands— those stallions that run swiftly— come to us for our praise.
I call today upon Indra, the one who inspires the *gāyatrī* hymn, the ever-yielding cow, the well-milking milch-cow, the other nourishment that is a broad stream and a ready gift.
When the Sun pierced Etaśa with his two swift, wind-winged steeds.
The Lord of a Hundred Powers bore Kutsa, the son of Arjuni, as he pursued the invincible Gandharva. He who, even without a bandage, before the joints were pierced,
Maghavan, the possessor of many riches, joined the broken joint together and restored what was shattered.
May we not be like outcasts, O Indra, nor like strangers to you.
Like forests abandoned by their owners, O wielder of the stone, we have been thought of as difficult to satisfy. We have indeed been thought slow and lacking in vigor, O slayer of Vṛtra.
O Hero, may we once more rejoice in your great bounty after our hymn of praise.
If Indra hears my hymn, may the swift drops of Soma,
having flowed through the filter, exhilarate him— the increasers of Tugra’s son.
Come today to this joint praise; come from your friend.
May the hymn of the liberal patrons favor you; I desire to offer you fair praise.
Press out the Soma with the stones; wash it in the waters.
Like men clothing themselves in garments, they have clothed themselves in cows; from their udders they have milked forth [the milk].
Now from the earth, or now from the luminous realm of the great heaven, grow strong with this body and my song; O you of noble wisdom, fill us with the things born [of your power].
For Indra, press the most intoxicating, choice Soma.
May Śakra cause it to swell, as he is urged on by every prayer like one seeking booty.
Let me not always beg you with my song while the Soma flows.
Like a restless wild beast, I have provoked him at the libations; who would not entreat the Lord?
Impelled by exhilaration, he is a fierce intoxicant with fierce power, the conqueror of all, shedding joy. For in his exhilaration, he indeed bestows gifts upon us.
At the dwelling of the worshipper, the God bestows many desirable things upon the mortal who offers oblations.
He grants gifts to the one who presses the juice and praises him—he who is celebrated by all and extolled by the pious.
O Indra, come hither and rejoice with wondrous bounty, O God!
Like a lake, your belly is filled with Soma-draughts for the drinking-feast— wide and expansive. May a thousand, may a hundred, yoked to your golden chariot—
tawny steeds with long manes, harnessed by prayer— bring you, O Indra, to drink the Soma.
Let your two bay steeds, with tails like peacocks’ feathers and white-backed, carry you upon your golden chariot to drink the exhilarating, swelling draught of the sweet soma-juice.
Drink of this pressed juice, O lover of songs, like one who drinks first.
This pressed juice of the refined, flavorful soma is prepared as a delightful draught for exhilaration.
He who alone by his wondrous power is great and fierce according to his holy ordinances—may he, the fair-cheeked one, come;
may he not stay away. May he come to our invocation and not pass us by.
With your weapons, you crushed the moving fortress of Śuṣṇa;
you followed after the light from of old, O Indra, when you became one to be invoked. I call upon you at the rising of the sun, and I call upon you at midday of heaven.
At the break of day and at the close of night, O Vasu, my hymns of praise have been turned toward you.
Praise him! Praise him! For these indeed are the most liberal among the wealthy patrons—Ninditāśva, Prapathin, Paramajyā, and Medhyātithi, the giver of riches.
When I mounted the chariot with faith, bringing the horses that long for the woods; then he who possesses the most excellent wealth takes notice of me—whatever cattle you have.
He who has granted me two bay steeds together with their golden skins.
May he, whose chariot resounds, surpass all blessings; may he whose chariot thunders come to us. Then Plāyoga, O Agni, subdued the others with ten thousand [men], he who is without equal.
Ten bright ones stood for me like reeds from a lake, O observer of men.
His massive [thigh] was seen from the front, boneless, hanging down;
the woman Śaśvatī, looking at him, said: "O noble man, you bear a most auspicious nourishment. O Vasu, drink this pressed juice; fill your belly completely.
We have offered [this] to you without fear.
Shaken by men, pressed with stones, purified through the sheep’s wool filter;
like a horse washed in the rivers, [the Soma is cleansed].
We have made this [Soma] sweet for you, mixing it with milk like barley;
O Indra, be present at this shared feast.
Indra alone is the drinker of Soma; Indra is the drinker of the pressed juice, the one who sustains all life.
[He stands] between the gods and mortals— him, the wide-extending one of kind heart, whom neither the pure, nor those of evil intent, nor the greedy can cause to shrink away.
When others seek him with cattle as hunters seek a wild beast,
they pursue him with milch-cows.
Let there be three pressed Soma draughts for Indra, the god.
In his own dwelling, for the one who drinks the pressed juice— three reservoirs drip, three ladles are well-filled,
upon a single support.
You are pure, established in many places, and mixed with milk in the midst;
you are most exhilarating with curd for the hero. These Soma juices, O Indra, are strong and pressed for us here.
The bright ones ask for the milk-mixture.
Mix this Soma with the milk-mixture, with the cake, and with those [bright ones] for Indra;
for I hear that you are wealthy.
Having drunk [the Soma], they fight within the hearts like those intoxicated by wine;
the naked ones groan like cows without udders.
O wealthy one, may the praiser of a bountiful patron such as you be rich indeed.
O Lord of the Bay Steeds, you have come before the famous [sacrifice].
The enemy who is not a liberal giver does not perceive even the hymn being recited,
nor the *gāyatra* chant being sung.
O Indra, do not deliver us over to the scorner, nor to the arrogant one. O Lord of Power, help us with your powers!
We, your friends, O Indra, seeking only this goal, are devoted to you.
The Kaṇvas praise you with hymns.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, I have never praised anything else at the newest work of the skillful; indeed, I have set my mind upon your hymn of praise alone.
The gods desire one who presses the soma; they do not long for sleep.
Being unwearied, they go toward him who is heedless. Come forth quickly with your strengths; do not be angry with us.
Like a great man with a young wife— let him not today, being ill-tempered, cause us distress at home like an unlovely son-in-law.
For we know the benevolence of this hero, which bestows much; he has won over the hearts of those born in the three worlds.
Pour forth [the soma] for him who is accompanied by Kaṇva; indeed, we do not know [anyone] more powerful than him.
The most glorious [gift] from Śatamūti—
press out the Soma for Indra, the hero, the powerful one, with the best [effort]; bring it, O men, so that he may drink.
He who is most familiar with the sacrificial altar, he shall bring to the singers, through his unswerving paths, strength consisting of horses;
to the praisers, strength consisting of cattle. O pressers, pour forth the most excellent [juice] for the exhilaration!
O hero, O brave one, press out the Soma!
May the slayer of Vṛtra, the drinker of the pressed juice, come quickly from afar to us; he of a hundredfold aid restrains himself for us.
May the two bay steeds, yoked by prayer and powerful, bring you here, O friend, who are renowned through songs and love songs.
Sweet are the Soma juices; come hither! The Soma juices are prepared; come hither!
O helmeted one, lord of men, wielder of power, come toward this feast together with the seers.
And may those praises which increase you for great bounty and manly valor strengthen you, O Indra, as they perform their work.
O you who are borne by songs, these hymns and those praises are for you; they have truly established your powers.
Thus indeed is he, the one of many deeds, the wielder of the thunderbolt, alone [the winner] of spoils.
Rising up, he bestows unimpaired gifts.
Lo! Indra, the much-invoked, slays Vṛtra with his right hand—he, the great one, by means of his mighty powers.
In whom all people, as well as great deeds and vast expanses, find delight; he, the exhilarating one, [rejoices] in the patrons.
Indra has performed all these deeds—he who is renowned far and wide.
The giver of booty to the wealthy patrons;
the bringer of the chariot seeking cattle, even from afar, whom he protects— the lord, for he is the bearer of your riches.
The sage is a winner with his steeds; the hero is a slayer of Vṛtra with his men; he is the true protector of the one who serves him.
O Priyamedhas, worship this Indra with a concentrated mind.
He who has truly drunk the Soma juices— the Lord of the Good, Gāthasravas, who desires glory and possesses many powers— him, the vigorous one,
the Kaṇvas have sung.
He who, powerful as a friend, gives even cows back from their tracks to men; those who have placed their desire in him—
thus, O wielder of the stone, [favor] Medhyātithi, the son of Kaṇva, who is rich in prayer.
Becoming a ram, he went toward the waters.
O Vibhindu, bestow gifts upon him; give him forty thousand, and eight thousand more.
And truly, those two who increase with milk, the two daughters of delight, have bestowed [their gifts] for the sake of procreation.
Drink of the flavorful pressed juice; O Indra, exhilarate yourself with our soma mixed with milk.
May our kinsman, the first to awaken, be for our prosperity; may your insights protect us.
May we, as prize-winners, abide in your favor; do not abandon us to the malice of the enemy.
Protect us with your wondrous aids; lead us toward your blessings.
O Lord of abundant wealth, may these songs of mine increase your strength; the wise ones, pure and bright as fire, have celebrated you with hymns of praise.
This one, empowered by a thousand seers, has spread himself out like the ocean.
True is that majesty of his; his power is praised at the sacrifices in the kingdom of the inspired poets.
Indra indeed we invoke for the service of the gods, Indra while the sacrifice proceeds, Indra when the battle is joined—we who long for the prize, Indra for the winning of wealth.
By his greatness Indra spread out the two worlds with his power; Indra caused the sun to shine.
In Indra all beings have found their support; in Indra the pressed drops find their rest.
O Indra, for the first draught, men come to you with hymns of praise.
The Ṛbhus, coming together, sang in unison; the Rudras praised that which was of old.
Indra’s manly power and strength increased through this, in the exhilaration of the pressed Soma by Viṣṇu. Today, as in former times, living men praise his greatness.
I beg that of you, O hero, that prayer for the sake of ancient mindfulness,
by which you helped the *yatins* and Bhṛgu when the prize was staked, and by which you protected Praskaṇva.
By which you released the ocean and the great waters— that, O Indra, is your manly power.
Immediately his greatness cannot be fully grasped, he whom the two worlds have acclaimed with song.
Be gracious to us, O Indra, for I entreat you for wealth and heroic strength.
Be gracious for the prize for him who desires to win it first; be gracious for our hymn, O Ancient One.
Be gracious to us in this, for you have protected Paura; O Indra, help the prayers of one who desires to win.
Be gracious, O Indra, as you protected Ruśama, Śyāvaka, Kṛpa, and Svarṇara.
What newest song of the *atasī* plants shall the mortal sing to you, the swift one?
Indeed, those who sing his praises have not attained his greatness or his sovereign power.
When do they praise him so as to win the gods? Who is the seer, who is the inspired poet that he honors?
O Indra, Maghavan, when will you come to the call of the one who presses the Soma? When will you come to the one who praises you?
Upward rise these most honey-sweet songs, these hymns of praise, like chariots seeking booty, ever-conquering, winning wealth, and providing inexhaustible aid.
Like the Kaṇvas, the Bhr̥gus, and the Sūryas, they have attained every desire.
Magnifying Indra with hymns of praise, the Āyus and Priyamedhas have raised their voices.
Yoke, O Indra, best slayer of Vṛtra, your two bay steeds from afar;
come hither, O Maghavan, for the drinking of Soma, O fierce one, with your noble companions.
For these singers of yours have yearned with their prayer, O Sage, for the winning of the prize; do thou, O Maghavan Indra, lover of songs, hear our call like a longing lover.
O Indra, thou didst hurl Vṛtra down from the lofty mountains.
From Nirarbuda, from Mrigaya, and from the illusory Parvata, you drove out the cattle.
The fires shone forth, the sun shone forth, and the Soma, the essence of Indra’s power, shone forth.
From the mid-air you blew away the great dragon; O Indra, you performed that manly deed.
The ruddy horse whom Indra gave to me— the Maruts and Pākasthāman Kaurayāṇa—
him who is by his very nature the most beautiful of all, as if running toward heaven;
that ruddy steed of mine, Pākasthāman’s gift, which is well-yoked and fills the girth-bands.
He has bestowed wealth that awakens;
he to whom ten other draft-horses yoke themselves as they carry the burden,
like birds returning to their nest at the house of Tugra.
The self is the father’s body; clothing is the giver of vigor;
ointment is the fourth part of the ruddy one. I have spoken to Pākasthāman, the liberal giver.
O Indra, when you are invoked by men from the east, the west, the north, or the south—
O Sima, you are many; urged by men, you are with Anu, O bold one, and with Turvaśa.
Or when, O Indra, you rejoice together with Ruma, Ruśama, Śyāvaka, and Kṛpa.
The Kaṇvas, bringing hymns of praise with their sacred prayers, draw you hither, O Indra; come!
As the thirsty buffalo goes to the waterless desert, so [come] to us at evening and at dawn; come quickly, and drink well among the Kaṇvas.
O Maghavan Indra, may these Soma drops exhilarate you for the sake of bestowing wealth upon the one who presses the juice.
From that [place], you drank the Soma pressed in the *camū* vessel; therein you took up supreme might. By force he displayed his power, and by his vigor he shattered the fury [of the foe].
O Indra, O youth, all those who sought battle against you were brought low like trees.
RV 8.4.6: He who offers praise to you is accompanied as if by a thousand; he makes his son a leader in heroic strength, and he worships you with words of homage.
RV 8.4.7: Let us not fear, let us not grow weary in your friendship, O Mighty One. We would behold Turvaśa and Yadu, for your deed, O Bull, is worthy of being gazed upon.
The bull has settled upon his left hip; his gift does not provoke anger.
The milch-cows are blended with honey from the bee-hive; come quickly, run hither, and drink!
O Indra, your friend is well-formed, possessing horses, a chariot, and cattle.

Sharing in strengthening nourishment, he is ever accompanied by vigor; radiant, he approaches the assembly. Like a thirsty antelope coming to a watering place, come hither and drink the Soma according to your desire. O Maghavan, raining down [bounty] day after day, you possess the most powerful strength.
O Adhvaryu, pour out the Soma; Indra thirsts for it.
He has now yoked his two vigorous bay steeds and the slayer of Vṛtra has arrived.
Even the man himself thinks he is a donor where you satisfy yourself with the Soma.
This is your appropriate food, sprinkled; come hither, hasten, and drink it!
O Adhvaryus, press the Soma for Indra, who stands upon his chariot.
The pressing-stones, as they pour out the libation, look toward the red sun, performing the service for the donor.
May the two vigorous bay steeds, the beloved ones, carry Indra toward the radiant sun during the rites.
May the seven coursers, the ornaments of the sacrifice, bring you hither to the libations.
We choose Pūṣan, the possessor of many riches, for our alliance.
O Śakra, invoked by many, teach us through our prayer for strength and for wealth, O deliverer!
Sharpen us as one whets a razor in its two hands; grant us riches, O deliverer!
With you, that wealth of the sun is easily found for us, when you impel a mortal man.
I desire you, O Pūṣan, for my aid; I desire to praise you, O glowing one.
I do not fear that, O Vasu, for it is not alien to you; I praise the *sāman* for Pajra.
O glowing one, immortal one, have the cows gone to some pasture? Our own wealth is constant.
O Pūṣan, be our protector, be auspicious for us, most bountiful for the winning of booty.
We have celebrated at the sacrifices of heaven the massive gift of a hundred horses from Kuruṅga,
and among the Turvaśas, we have meditated upon the gifts of the brilliant and fortunate king.
Through the inspired hymns of the victorious Kaṇva and the Priyamedhas who shine toward heaven,
the seer won sixty thousand cattle and drove forth their herds. Even the trees rejoiced when I arrived.
They eagerly partake of the cow; they eagerly partake of the horse.
Even from afar, as it were, the true one, red-hued, has manifested here; He has spread his radiance in every direction.
Like heroes, O wonder-workers, you accompany the Dawn on a mind-yoked chariot of broad splendor,
O Aśvins. To you two, O lords of ample wealth, this hymn of praise has been manifested.
Like a messenger, you have been summoned with our speech;
for our protection, we Kaṇvas praise the Aśvins, who are beloved by many, most gladdening, and possessors of abundant wealth.
Most bountiful, best at winning booty, impelling [the sacrifice], lords of splendor,
you who go to the house of the donor—
O gods, for the pious sacrificer, grant that which is highly wise and unfailing.
Sprinkle the pasture with clarified butter.
Hasten toward our hymn of praise swiftly with your rapid falcons; come hither, O Aśvins, with your horses.
With those [horses] by which you traverse the three distant realms, all the luminous spheres of heaven,
and the three seasons. And grant us nourishment rich in cattle, and booty that finds the day.
Open up the paths for us to win.
O Aśvins, bring to us wealth consisting of cattle, heroic sons, and excellent chariots; bring us nourishment accompanied by horses.
Increasing in strength, O Lords of Splendor, wonder-workers with golden paths,
drink the Soma-sweetness! Bestow upon us, O possessors of wealth, and upon our patrons, far-reaching prosperity.
Come quickly, O invincible ones, to the protection that goes forth; come swiftly to the prayer of the people that has been offered; do not neglect others.
O Aśvins, drink of this lovely, exhilarating draught, of the honeyed juice offered to you, O wise ones.
Bring hither to us wealth consisting of hundreds and thousands.
[He is] rich in food, the sustainer of all.
For indeed, in many places, the wise call upon you both, O Heroes; come, O Aśvins, with the singers of praise!
The people, having spread the sacrificial grass, bearing oblations, and having prepared everything well,
invoke you both, O Aśvins. May this our praise today be the most effective and closest to you both.
O Aśvins,
let it be for you both; O you who move among the people, drink from that skin-bag of honey which has been set out for you.
With that, O you who possess abundant wealth, bring us well-being for our cattle, our offspring, and our kine;
bring us plenteous nourishment. And bring us celestial nourishment, and the rivers, O you who find the days.
You rain down like the opening of two doors. When, O Heroes, did the son of Tugra worship you, abandoned in the ocean,
when your chariot flew forth with winged steeds?
O Nāsatyas, you bestowed constant succor upon Kaṇva when he was confined within his dwelling;
with those most recent aids, accompanied by excellent praises, come hither to us.
Or when I call upon you, O possessors of raining wealth—
just as you protected Kaṇva, Priyamedha,
Upastuta, Atri, and Śiñjāra, O Aśvins.
Just as [you helped] Aṃśu in the winning of wealth, Agastya in the winning of cattle, and Sobhari in the contests for booty—
O Aśvins, possessors of rain-like wealth, such is your aid, or even more than this.
Praising you, we implore your favor.
O Aśvins, mount your chariot with its golden seat and golden reins, for it reaches unto the heavens.
Golden is your supporting pole, golden the axle,
and both wheels are golden. With that [chariot], O you who possess abundant wealth, come to us even from afar.
Come to this my fair praise. O Aśvins, you who are immortal, bring hither from afar many offerings of the Dāsa people that we may eat.
Come to us with splendors, with glories, and with wealth, O Aśvins; come, O Nāsatyas, who possess manifold radiance.
May the dappled-winged birds, laden with leaves, carry you both hither.
Toward the people who perform the sacrifice well; sing after the chariot that rolls along with its nourishment,
whose wheel is never obstructed.
On a golden chariot with horses that run swiftly at the touch of a hand, O Nāsatyas, you who are swift as thought, you two, O lords of wealth,
enjoy the wakeful wild beast.
May those two sprinkle us with food and wealth.
O Aśvins, may you two recognize me as a recipient of new gifts,
just as Kaśu, the son of Cedi, gave a hundred camels and ten thousand cattle.
He who bestowed upon me ten kings resembling gold— beneath the feet of the Cedi king are the people, the folk all around like leather straps.
Let no one go by that path by which these Cedis travel.
No other patron rises superior to him, a man who bestows more abundant gifts.
Great is Indra by his might, like Parjanya when he possesses the rain;
he has grown strong through the hymns of Vatsa.
When the bearers, the inspired singers, bring forward the offspring of *ṛta*, fulfilling it with the vehicle of *ṛta*.
When the Kaṇvas have made Indra the accomplisher of the sacrifice through their hymns of praise.
He who calls his weapon "kinsman"— at his wrath all the tribes, all the peoples,
bow down together like rivers unto the ocean.
His vigor blazed forth when Indra, as if with a leather shield, brought the two worlds together;
indeed, he shattered Vṛtra, the furious one, with his hundred-knotted thunderbolt.
He split the head with the *vṛṣṇi* [thunderbolt].
We praise these prayers aloud before the inspired poets;
they are like the flashing flames of Agni.
Though dwelling in secret, the radiant prayers themselves have come forth;
the Kaṇvas [have come] with the stream of Truth.
O Indra, may we attain that wealth consisting of cattle and horses.
For the sake of first reflecting upon the sacred word (*brahman*),
I have indeed received from my father the wisdom of the Eternal Order (*ṛta*);
I have been born like Sūrya.
With an ancient hymn of thought, I adorn my songs like Kaṇva,
by which Indra gains his strength.
Those ṛṣis who have not praised you, O Indra, and those who have praised you— [all these I honor].
Grow strong for me, you who are well-praised!
When his wrath roared along its path, shattering Vṛtra limb by limb,
he drove the waters toward the ocean.
O Indra, you brought down your enduring thunderbolt upon the Dasyu Śuṣṇa; O fierce one, you are renowned as the bull.
Neither the heavens nor the mid-air regions equal Indra in might, the wielder of the thunderbolt.
The earths did not expand [to contain him]. O Indra, you who lay upon the great waters as they were being propped up—
him you struck down upon his feet.
He who has firmly grasped these two great worlds, heaven and earth, which face one another— to him, O Indra,
you have hidden [the darkness] with glooms. O Indra, those Yatis and those Bhr̥gus who have praised you— [to them you have granted this].
O fierce one, hear my call!
O Indra, let these dappled cows yield for you butter and milk-mixtures,
swelling with the nectar of Truth.
O Indra, those who, through their own power, have brought forth the embryo,
have encompassed it like the sun with its heat. O Lord of Might, the Kaṇvas have magnified you with their hymn.
The pressed drops, the *indavas*, [seek] you. O Indra, wielder of the stone, under your guidance and your praise,
the sacrifice is to be extended far and wide.
O Indra, bring us great nourishment; burst open for us the fortress rich in cattle, and grant us offspring and heroic strength.
And also that wealth of swift horses which, O Indra, exists among the Nahuṣī tribes.
At the forefront, he has shone upon the people; you have extended [your light] toward the enclosure like the sun, visible nearby—
O Indra, when you show us mercy.
When indeed, O Indra, you, the most powerful one, rule over the peoples— great and boundless in your might—
then the tribes bearing oblations address you for their protection.
With his drops,
he who possesses wide-reaching speed was born as a sage through inspired thought, in the shelter of the mountains and at the confluence of the rivers.
From there, the wise one looks down upon the ocean from the heights, from where the flowing wave stirs.
Then they behold the light of the ancient seed, the morning radiance.
When it is kindled high in heaven,
O Indra, all the Kaṇvas increase your thought and your manly power; and so too, O mightiest one, your virile strength.
O Indra, take pleasure in this well-fashioned hymn of mine; protect me well!
And further increase my inspired thought.
Furthermore, O wielder of the thunderbolt, we offer these prayers to you, O magnified one.
We, the sages, have fashioned [the hymn] for our long life;
the Kaṇvas have sung toward Indra with a hymn that seeks his favor, like waters flowing down a slope.
Hymns have magnified Indra, as rivers swell the ocean—
him whose wrath is unsurpassed and who is undecaying.
Come to us from afar with your two beloved bay horses.
Drink this pressed juice, O Indra!
Thee indeed, O greatest slayer of Vṛtra, do the people who have spread the sacrificial grass invoke for the winning of booty.
Both worlds follow you, as the two wheels follow the steed Etaśa;
the pressed drops of Soma follow you.
Rejoice well, O Indra, you who are rich in men, at Śaryaṇāvat.
Rejoice in the hymns of Vivasvat;
increasing toward heaven, the bull, wielder of the thunderbolt,
has bellowed— the slayer of Vṛtra, the greatest drinker of Soma.
For the seer was indeed his first-born, the sole lord by his might;
O Indra, you bestow wealth upon us. Toward our pressed juices, we with smooth-backed steeds hasten toward the food.
Let the hundred bay steeds carry him away. The Kaṇvas have magnified this ancient prayer, which overflows with honey and clarified butter, by means of their hymn of praise.
Among the great ones, let the mortal choose Indra at the sacrifice;
let him who desires to win choose Indra for his protection.
O you who are praised by many, may your two bay steeds, lauded by the Priyamedhas, turn hither toward us.
They have brought [the gifts] for the drinking of Soma.
From Tirindira I have received a hundred, and from Parśu a thousand,
as gifts from the Yadus.
Three hundred steeds and ten thousand cattle were given to Pajra Sāman;
the preeminent one reached up to heaven, bestowing camels yoked in teams of four.
By your fame, O Yadus, you surpass the people.
When the inspired singer has poured forth the *triṣṭubh* hymn as nourishment for you, O Maruts,
you shine forth across the mountains.
When, O bright ones, you who possess great power have indeed determined your course,
the mountains have bowed down. Roaring with the winds, the sons of Pṛśni have raised themselves up.
They milk the swelling nourishment.
The Maruts sow the mist and cause the mountains to tremble when they go on their course with the winds.
When the mountain and the rivers have bent down before your march, before your ordinance,
and before your great impetuous might; we invoke you by night for our protection, and we invoke you by day.
When the sacrifice is being prepared for you—
upward those of ruddy hue, brilliant in their courses,
roar with the swelling of heaven.
They release the path for the sun to travel by their might; they have spread themselves out with their rays.
O Maruts, O Ṛbhukṣans, accept this my song, this hymn of praise!
Accept this my invocation.
The dappled cows have milked three lakes of honey for the wielder of the thunderbolt: a well, a water-skin, and a cask.
O Maruts, when we, seeking your favor, call upon you from heaven, come hither to us! For you, O bounteous Rudras, lords of the Ribhus, abide in our home.
And in the exhilaration of the wise ones,
O Maruts, send down from heaven to us wealth that distills joy, abounding in food and providing all sustenance.
When you, O brilliant ones, have determined your course over the mountains, as it were,
you exhilarate yourselves with the pressed drops. Let a mortal man beg for the favor of these [Maruts] even for so much as this.
Through the hymns of the invincible one—
those who, like sparks, blow through both worlds with showers of rain, milking the inexhaustible spring.
Up they rise with their roars, up with their chariots, up with the winds,
and up with their hymns of praise— the sons of Pṛśni.
With that [aid] by which you helped Turvaśa and Yadu, and by which you helped Kaṇva who won the prize of wealth.
May we meditate well upon his wealth.
O bounteous ones, may these refreshments of yours swell like clarified butter;
may they increase through the hymns of Kāṇva.
Where now do you rejoice, O bounteous ones, for whom the sacrificial grass has been trimmed?
Which priest honors you?
For indeed, it is not as it was before, when you were honored with hymns by those who had trimmed the sacrificial grass.
You quicken the hosts of Truth.
Together they have brought together the great waters, together the two worlds, and together the sun; they have fashioned the thunderbolt joint by joint.
They have rent Vṛtra limb from limb and split the mountain peaks asunder, performing manly deeds of heroism. They have reinforced the strength and the resolve of Trita as he fought.
They followed after Indra in the conquest of Vṛtra;
lightning in their hands, they reached toward the heavens; golden helmets upon their heads, the radiant ones have adorned themselves for glory.
When Uśanas came from afar to the opening of the bull,
he roared like heaven out of fear.
Come to us for the giving of the sacrifice, with horses whose hooves are adorned with gold.
O gods, come hither!
When the spotted deer and the ruddy horse draw as the leader at their chariot, the brilliant ones go forth, letting the waters flow.
To the Sushoma, to the Sharyanavat, to the Arjika, and to the Pastyavat—
there the heroes went with their downward-turning wheels.
When, O Maruts, will you come to the inspired singer who thus invokes you?
With your mercies, [help] the one who implores you. When now, O you who are dear to many, have you abandoned Indra? Who among you can claim the status of a friend?
O Kaṇvas, let us indeed praise Agni with the Maruts who hold the thunderbolt in their hands, those who possess golden axes, for our great strength.
Let us truly praise the vigorous and most worshipful ones for new and auspicious prosperity.
May I turn hither those who possess variegated steeds. Even the mountains bow down, thinking themselves to be mere heaps of earth;
even the rocky peaks submit.
Moving crosswise, they carry [the offerings] as they fly through the mid-air;
as bestowers, they grant vital strength to the one who praises them.
For Agni has been born as the first, like the Sun with his radiance according to the sacred meter.
They have spread themselves out with their rays.
O Aśvins, come to us with all your aids;
O wonder-workers on golden paths, drink the Soma-sweetness.
Come now, O Aśvins, on your chariot with a sun-bright skin; you who enjoy [the offerings], adorned with gold, you two seers of profound intellect.
Come from the realm of Nahuṣa, come from the mid-air, by means of our well-fashioned hymns.
Drink the honeyed mead, O Aśvins, pressed at the libation of the Kaṇvas. Come to us from heaven, come from the mid-air, you who are dear.
Here, the son of Kaṇva has pressed for you the Soma-mead.
O Aśvins, having heard us, come to us for the drinking of the Soma;
Svāhā! O sages, you who increase the hymn of praise, O heroes, [come] with your inspired thoughts.
For whatever aid the seers of old invoked from you, O heroes—

Come, O Aśvins, arrive at this my excellent hymn of praise! Even from the luminous realm of heaven, come to us, you who find the light! You who are mindful of Vatsa through our prayers, and who hear our invocation through our hymns of praise.
Why do others sit around us with their hymns, O Aśvins?
Vatsa, the son of Kaṇva, the seer, has magnified you both with his songs.
The inspired singer has invoked you here for protection with hymns, O Aśvins.
Free from blemish, the greatest slayers of Vṛtra, may you both be sources of bliss for us.
When the maiden mounted your chariot, O lords of ample wealth,
you Aśvins reached all our prayers.
From here, O Aśvins, come on your chariot adorned with a thousand ornaments.
Vatsa, the seer among poets, has recited a honey-sweet hymn to you both.
O you who are greatly gladdened, possessors of many riches, you are the discoverers of wealth.
O Aśvins, bearers of the sacrifice, may you both respond favorably to this hymn of mine.
O Aśvins, bestow upon us all gifts that are beyond reproach. O you who are true to the seasons, do not deliver us over to the scorn of our enemies.
Whether you are far away, or whether you are in the sky above,
come from there, O Aśvins, on your chariot adorned with a thousand ornaments. O Nāsatyas, the seer Vatsa has magnified you both with his songs.
For him, provide food that has a thousand adornments and drips with ghee.
O Aśvins, you two bestow upon him strength that drips with ghee,
he who has praised you for the sake of favor and seeks wealth, O Lords of Bounty.

Come to us, O destroyers of enemies, to this hymn of ours, O you who enjoy many things! O heroes, grant us great glory and these gifts for our protection. The Priyamedhas have invoked you both with all your aids.
O Aśvins, you who reign over the sacrifices at the invocations of the journey,
come to us, O Aśvins, you who are sources of bliss and bringers of prosperity.
Vatsa, the praiser, has magnified you both with his prayers and songs.
With those [powers] by which you protected Kaṇva and Medhātithi, with which you [protected] Vaśa Daśavraja,
and with which you protected Gośarya— with those, O Heroes, protect us.
With those [powers], O Heroes, you protected Trasadasyu in the winning of the prize.
With those aids, O Aśvins, protect us for the winning of booty.
May our hymns of praise, well-fashioned songs, exalt you both, O Aśvins.
You who are the greatest slayers of Vṛtra in many places—be such to us as those who are much desired.
The three steps of the Aśvins are manifest, yet they remain hidden in the secret place beyond.
O Sages, come hither from among the living along the paths of Eternal Order.
Now, O Aśvins, come for the protection of Vatsa.
Grant him a wide, secure dwelling free from predators; drive away those who are hostile.
Whatever manly strength exists in the mid-air, whatever in heaven, and whatever among the five tribes of men—bestow all that, O Aśvins.
O Aśvins, just as the sages who have fully grasped your wondrous deeds,
so too do you take heed of Kaṇva.
This hot offering, O Aśvins, is poured out for you with a hymn of praise.
This Soma is honey-sweet, O lords of ample wealth, by which you two take notice of Vṛtra.
Whatever [power] you have established in the waters, in the tree, or in the plants, O performers of many wonders,
with that, O Aśvins, protect me.
O Nāsatyas, whether you hasten forth or whether, O Gods, you practice healing, this Vatsa here does not find you through his prayers alone; for you go to him who possesses the oblation.
Now indeed, the seer has conceived a hymn of praise for the Aśvins with skillful art.
Pour out the most honey-sweet Soma and the hot oblation for Atharvan. Now indeed, O Aśvins, mount your chariot that rolls swiftly;
may these hymns of mine cause you to hasten hither like a cloud.

Whatever we may have stirred you up today with hymns, O Nāsatyas, or whatever with our songs, O Aśvins— take heed of Kaṇva’s son. Or whether Kakṣīvat, or the seer Vyaśva, or Dīrghatamas has invoked you.

When Pṛthī Vainya [invoked] you both at the sacrificial seats, O Aśvins, you took notice of him. Come as protectors of our shelter, be our protectors from afar; be the protectors of our moving world and the protectors of our bodies.
Come for the sake of our household, our offspring, and our progeny.
O Aśvins, whether you travel in the same chariot with Indra, or whether you dwell in the same abode with Vāyu;
whether you are in harmony with the Ādityas and the Ṛbhus, or whether you stand in the wide strides of Viṣṇu— whatever it be, O Aśvins, if today I should invoke you for the winning of booty.
Whatever aid of the Aśvins is most excellent for conquering in battles—that is their power.
Come now, O Aśvins, for these oblations have been prepared for you;
these Soma-draughts are here among the Turvaśas, and likewise among the Kaṇvas for you both.

O Nāsatyas, whatever healing medicine exists for you in the distance or near at hand— with that, O wise ones, grant protection now to Vimada and to Vatsa. I have awakened together with the divine speech of the Aśvins.
Turn away the divine thought [from us], turn away the bounty from mortals.
O Uṣas, awaken the Aśvins; O great goddess Sūnṛtā, awaken them.
Awaken the two Hotṛs of the sacrifice in succession, and awaken high renown for our exhilaration.
O Uṣas, when you come with your radiance, you shine together with Sūrya.
Here comes the chariot of the Aśvins, traveling its circuit that protects men.
When the pressed stalks have been drunk, they yield their milk like cows from their udders.
Or when the voices have resounded, the god-fearing ones have called forth the Aśvins— for glory, for power, for protection that overcomes men,
and for skill, O ye two wise ones.

O Aśvins, when you now sit upon the father’s seat with your prayers, or when you are there with your riches, O you who are worthy of praise; whether you are in the far-reaching dwelling, or in the luminous realm of heaven,
or in the ocean, in the fashioned house— from there, O Aśvins, come hither!
Or when you have prepared the sacrifice for Manu, take heed of this Kaṇva as well.
I invoke Bṛhaspati, all the gods, Indra and Viṣṇu, and the Aśvins who possess swift horses. I now call upon those two Aśvins of wondrous deeds, who are ready to be grasped.
Those two whose friendship is to be esteemed among the gods,
under whose protection the wise patrons stand during the sacrifice while the sun has not yet risen— those two,
the mindful ones of the sacrifice and the rite, drink the Soma-mead with their inherent powers.
O Aśvins, whether you are in the west today or in the east, O lords of wealth;
whether with Druhyu, Anu, Turvaśa, or Yadu—I call upon you both, so come to me. Whether you fly through the mid-air, O enjoyers of much, or whether you range across these two worlds.
Or when you mount the chariot by means of your self-sustaining powers (*svadhā*), from there come hither, O Aśvins!
O Agni, you are the guardian of vows (*vratapā*), a god among mortals;
you are to be praised at the sacrifices.
You are worthy of praise in the assemblies, O victorious one; O Agni, you are the charioteer of the sacrifices.
As such, O Jātavedas, drive away our enemies from us.
O Agni, drive away the godless hostilities.
O Jātavedas, you do not attend even the sacrifice of a mortal enemy that is close at hand.
We mortals meditate upon your many names, O immortal one, we inspired singers upon you, Jātavedas.
Inspired singers [meditate] on the inspired one for protection; mortals [meditate] on the god for aid.
We invoke Agni with our songs.
May Vatsa draw your mind away even from your highest dwelling-place,
O Agni, with a song that yearns for you.
For you are present in many places, the lord over all the tribes.
In the battles we invoke you. In the battles, seeking booty, we invoke Agni for protection.
In the contests for booty, [we call upon] him whose gifts are manifold.
For you are the ancient one, worthy of praise at the sacrifices; as the Hotṛ-priest, you sit, both old and new. O Agni, satisfy your own body and win for us prosperity through sacrifice.
O Indra, that exhilaration which is the greatest drinker of Soma, O most powerful one, which is conscious—
that by which you strike down the devouring demon, for that we pray. That by which [you struck] Daśagva, Adhrigu, Vepayan, and Svarṇara—
We implore that [power] by which you protected the ocean;
we implore that [power] by which you urged on the Sindhu and the great waters like chariots, so that the path of *ṛta* may be traversed.
O wielder of the stone, accept this hymn for our protection, purified like clarified butter—by which power you have grown mighty even now.
O lover of songs, take pleasure in this; it swells like the ocean.
O Indra, you have grown great through all your aids. That god who has granted us a boon for friendship from afar—
you have grown great, spreading [your fame] like rain from heaven.
His banners have grown strong, and the thunderbolt is in his two hands,
when, like the sun, he caused the two worlds to swell. O blameless Lord of the Good, when you, having grown great, [slew] a thousand buffaloes.
From the very beginning, your great Indra-power has increased.
Indra, with the rays of the sun, burns down the one who acts with violence.
Like Agni conquering the forests, he has grown ever stronger.
This newest prayer of yours, timely and full of devotion, goes forth;
serving you, much-beloved, it measures out its course. The embryo of the sacrifice, seeking the gods, purifies the ritual power (kratú) in due succession.
RV 8.12.11.2: He has grown strong through the hymns of Indra;
he measures out [the sacrifice]. RV 8.12.12.1: Indra, the winner, has spread the friendship for the drinking of Soma.
RV 8.12.12.2: Like a sharp axe, he measures out [the reward] for the one who presses the juice.
Whom the inspired poets, the Āyus who bring hymns of praise, have gladdened;
he has swelled like clarified butter in their mouth when the Truth is uttered. And Aditi has brought forth this hymn for Indra, the self-ruling lord.
O you whose aids are praised by many, when the bearer of the *ṛta* has sung forth for help and for glory;
O God, your two bay steeds do not turn back from the *ṛta*.

Whether, O Indra, you rejoice in Soma with Viṣṇu, or with Trita Āptya, or whether, O Śakra, you rejoice among the Maruts with the flowing drops; or whether, O powerful one, you rejoice in the distance beyond the sea— RV_08.012.16.1 {04} yat somam indra viṣṇavi yad vā gha trita āptye RV_08.012.16.2 {04} yad vā marutsu mandase sam indubhiḥ RV_08.012.17.1 {04} yad vā śakra parāvati samudre adhi mandase
Rejoice in our pressed juice together with the drops, O Indra!
Whether you are the strengthener of the presser, O Lord of the True, or whether you take delight in his hymn of praise, rejoice together with the drops.
To praise each god for your protection, we shall sing of Indra after Indra.
Thus, for the sake of the sacrifice and for victory, they have pervaded [the world].
We honor with sacrifices him who is borne by sacrifices, and with Soma-drinks him who is the greatest drinker of Soma.
With oblations they have magnified Indra;
they have attained his great guidances and his many praises.
All treasures have been attained for the donor.
The gods placed Indra at their head to slay Vṛtra;
the voices of praise have shouted for Indra, for his peerless might. We [praise] the great one with greatness through our hymns, him who hears our invocation.
We praise him with hymns for his equal might;
neither the two worlds nor the mid-air regions can contain the wielder of the thunderbolt,
at whose onset the equal-mighty one blazes forth.
When, O Indra, the gods placed you at their head in the battle for booty,
then your two beloved bay horses carried you forward.
When, O wielder of the thunderbolt, you slew Vṛtra who obstructed the rivers with your might.
From the very beginning, yours...
When Viṣṇu strode out his three steps by his might, from the very beginning, yours...
When your two beloved bay steeds grew in strength day by day,
from that moment all the worlds submitted to you. When the hosts of Maruts were made subject to you, O Indra.
Come hither to you... When you established yonder sun, that bright light, in heaven—
then indeed did we come to you...
O Indra, this well-wrought hymn of praise is brought forth for you by the inspired singer with his meditations;
it carries him across, like a kinswoman at the station, toward the sacrifice. When they have sung together in unison within his beloved abode.
At the navel of the sacrifice, the milkings are for the rite.
O Indra, grant us great heroism, good horses, and good cattle,
like a Hotar-priest at the rite for the first thought.
When the Soma juices have been pressed, Indra purifies his praiseworthy power of will;
he has found the increase of the skillful one, for he is great. He is the increaser in the first firmament, in the dwelling place of the gods.
Easy to cross over, most glorious, winner of the waters—
him I invoke for the winning of booty, Indra the impetuous, for the sake of battle.
Be our closest friend for our welfare and for our increase.
O Indra, lover of songs, this gift from the one who presses the soma flows for you;
rejoicing in this sacred grass (*barhis*), you shine forth.
Now, O Indra, grant us that which we, pressing the soma, implore of you.
Bring us manifold wealth that finds the light of heaven,
so that your worshipper, O far-seeing one, may cause his songs to flourish exceedingly. Like branches, they grow upward when you take pleasure in them.
As of old, give birth to songs; hear the call of the singer. In every exhilaration, you have grown great for the doer of good deeds.
His joyful blessings play like waters flowing down a slope.
By this prayer, he who is called the Lord of Heaven—
and he who is called the sole sovereign Lord of the peoples— rejoices at the pressed juice, [invoked] by those seeking aid who increase their homage.
Praise the renowned and wise one, whose two bay steeds are ever-victorious;
they go to the house of the worshipper who bows in homage.
O thou of great power, hastening with thy dappled horses—
Come to the sacrifice with your swift steeds, for fuel has been prepared for you.
O Indra, most powerful Lord of the virtuous, bestow wealth upon those who sing your praises; grant immortal fame and abundance to our patrons.
We invoke you at the rising of the sun; we invoke you at midday of the day.
O Indra, being pleased, come to us with your horses.
Come hither, run forth, and rejoice in the pressed soma mixed with milk.
Spin out the ancient thread, as is known. O Śakra,
O slayer of Vṛtra, whether you are in the distance or nearby,
or if you are in the ocean, you are the protector of the soma-juice.
May our songs magnify Indra; may the pressed Soma drops magnify Indra.
The people, bearing oblations, have found delight in Indra.
Him indeed do the sages, seeking aid, [magnify] with their swift-flowing protections.
The two worlds have strengthened Indra like branches.
At the Trikadruka rites, the gods performed the sacrifice that brings consciousness; may our songs of praise strengthen him who ever increases.
When the praiser, devoted to you, offers hymns at the proper times, he is called pure and purifying; he is the wonderful one. That mighty power of Rudra is manifest in the ancient abodes.
Where the wise have placed their minds, there let [the Soma] flow.
If you choose my friendship, drink of this juice,
by which we may overcome all enemies.
O Indra, lover of songs, when shall your praiser become most peaceful?
When will you bestow upon us wealth in cattle and horses?
And your two well-praised, vigorous bay steeds draw your chariot.
We implore that most intoxicating [Soma] of the ageless one. We implore that one praised by many, the mighty one, with ancient aids;
may he sit down doubly upon the beloved sacrificial grass.
Grow strong, O you who are well-praised by many, with those aids extolled by the seers;
milk forth for us swelling nourishment and protect us.
O Indra, wielder of the stone, you are indeed our protector for him who praises you thus.
I send forth my prayer to you, yoked by the mind, according to the eternal Law. Here,
harnessing those two bay steeds that share in the feast and bring abundant wealth, O Indra, call out to us for the drinking of the Soma.
Let those Rudras who accompany you respond with their roar, they who share in your splendor;
and let the Marut-clans come toward the offerings. These his victorious charges take delight in the station that is in heaven.
They have established him at the navel of the sacrifice, as is well known. He, for long-lasting vision, while the forward-moving rite proceeds,
measures out the sacrifice step by step, looking around.
O Indra, your chariot is a bull, and your two bay steeds are bulls.
O Śatakratu, you are a bull; your call is a bull.
The pressing-stone is a bull, the exhilaration is a bull, and this pressed Soma is a bull.
The sacrifice is a bull; you, O restrainer, further it. The invocation is a bull.
As a bull, I call upon you, the bull, O wielder of the thunderbolt, with your wondrous aids. For you have favored the hymn of praise; the invocation is a bull.
O Indra, if I were the sole lord of wealth just as you are, my praiser would be a possessor of cattle. O Lord of Might, I would bestow upon that wise man and I would desire to give to him.
If I were the lord of cattle...
O Indra, your *sūnṛtā* is a cow for the sacrificer who presses the soma;
swelling with milk, she yields both cow and horse.
There is no restrainer of your bounty, O Indra, neither god nor mortal,
when you, being praised, desire to bestow wealth.
The sacrifice magnified Indra when he spread out the earth.
Having fashioned a crest upon the sky—
for you who have grown great and have won all treasures— we choose your protection, O Indra.
In the exhilaration of Soma, Indra extended across the mid-air and the luminous realms when he split Vala asunder;
revealing those cows that were hidden in the cave, he drove them out for the Aṅgirases.
He has driven Vala downward.
By Indra, the luminous realms of heaven were made firm and strengthened—
stable, so that they may not be pushed back.
Like a wave of waters, O Indra, the hymn of praise rushes forward with speed;
your exhilarations have shone forth.
For you, O Indra, are the one who increases the hymn of praise, the one who increases the song of glory.
And he brings prosperity to his worshippers. May the two long-maned bay steeds carry Indra to the Soma-drinking,
to the sacrifice of the bounteous giver.
With the foam of the waters, O Indra, you struck off the head of Namuci,
when you conquered all rival hosts.
O Indra, by means of your wondrous powers, you [overthrew] those who sought to creep upward and desired to scale heaven.
You have shaken down the Dasyus;
O Indra, you have scattered the assembly of those who do not press the Soma in every direction,
becoming the superior drinker of Soma.
Sing forth to him who is invoked by many and praised by many;
with songs, seek to win Indra, the powerful one.
He whose great might is twofold supports both heaven and earth.
With bull-like vigor, you [overcame] the mountains, the plains, and the waters; O Indra,
much-praised one, you alone rule as king and strike down the Vṛtras,
so that we may attain victories and glory.
We sing of that exhilarating draught of yours, the bull-strong, victorious in battles,
the world-maker, O wielder of the stone, who possesses the beauty of tawny steeds—
by which you found the lights for Āyu and for Manu.
Rejoicing in this sacred grass (*barhis*), you shine forth.
Even today, those who recite hymns praise you according to the ancient custom.
Day by day, win the waters that have the bull as their lord.
That great power of yours, O Indra, your impetuous strength, and your wisdom—
the Dhiṣaṇā sharpens your choice-worthy thunderbolt.
O Indra, heaven increases your manly might, and earth increases your fame.
The waters and the mountains urge you on; Viṣṇu, the lofty abode, and Mitra and Varuṇa sing your praise;
the host of Maruts exults after you.
You, O Indra, were born as the most bounteous bull among men;
you truly possess all things that bring good offspring. Truly, O much-praised one, you alone shatter the Vṛtras.
None other than Indra impels a greater deed.
When, O Indra, men invoke you from various sides for aid,
conquer the light of heaven here with our heroes.
Be ready for our great dwelling, entering into all forms;
gladden Indra, the Lord of Might, for victory. Praise with new songs Indra, the sovereign ruler of the peoples.
The man who is the conqueror of men, the most bountiful, in whom all hymns of praise and all glorious deeds find delight, like the waters in the ocean.
I seek to win him over with beautiful praise— the eldest king, the doer of deeds in battle,
the possessor of great strength for the sake of winning prizes.
He whose exhilarations are unimpaired, profound, vast, and rescuing.
Full of joy in the battle for heroes; him indeed they invoke for the sake of a superior word when the spoils have been set out—
those whose Indra is their ally are victorious.
Men honor him with mighty deeds and with their sacred works;
he is Indra, the creator of wide space.
Indra is the priest, Indra is the seer, Indra is invoked by many.
Great with his mighty powers, he is worthy of praise, worthy of invocation, the true hero, the one of many deeds; though he is alone, he is all-conquering.
The people, the inhabitants of the earth, magnify that Indra with hymns of praise, with Sāmans, and with Gāyatrī chants—
him who leads us toward greater wealth and creates light in battles.
He who has overcome his enemies in battle—
may that Indra, the much-invoked, being our protector, carry us safely across all hostilities by means of his ship.
As such, O Indra, favor us with spoils; grant us a path and lead us toward happiness.
Come hither, for we have pressed the juice for you; O Indra, drink this Soma!
This is my sacrificial grass, my seat.
O Indra, may your two long-maned bay horses, yoked by prayer, bring you hither;
hear our sacred invocations.
O Indra, drinker of Soma, we who possess the Soma and have pressed it— your companions and priests—
we call upon you. Come to us, who have pressed the juice, and attend to our beautiful hymns of praise.
Drink well, O fair-cheeked one, of the soma-juice!
I pour it into your two flanks; let it flow through all your limbs. Seize the sweetness with your tongue.
May it be sweet for your enjoyment, honeyed for your body;
may the Soma be a blessing to your heart.
O you who are far-seeing, here he comes, encompassing you like women surrounding a man.
O Soma, flow forth to Indra. With his powerful neck, his belly of fatness, and his strong arms, in the exhilaration of the plant,
Indra smites down the Vṛtras.
O Indra, go forth at the head; you are the lord of all by your might.
O slayer of Vṛtra, strike down the Vṛtras.
Let your hook be long, with which you bestow wealth.
For the sacrificer who presses the juice.
This Soma of yours, O Indra, is purified upon the sacred grass; come hither, hasten to it, and drink!
O Śācigu, for you who are honored for your power, this [soma] has been pressed for your delight;
O Ākhaṇḍala, you are invoked.
That which is yours, O grandson of the bull-horned one, the great-grandson, the Kuṇḍapāyya—
In him they have fixed their minds. O Vāstoṣpati, you are a firm pillar, a shelter for those who offer Soma.
Drapsa is the breaker of eternal fortresses; Indra is the friend of the sages.
Pṛdākusānu, the worshipful seeker of cattle, being alone, has overcome the many.
With force, he leads the impetuous horse forward; he seizes Indra for the drinking of the Soma.
Truly, let the mortal man now beg this favor from them.
In the impelling power of the Ādityas, there is that which is unprecedented.
For the path of these Ādityas is unassailable; their guardians are undeceived, increasing our well-being on the easy way.
May Savitar, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman grant us that wide-spreading protection which we implore.
O divine Aditi, together with the gods, come hither, O you whose sustenance is unimpaired.
Together with the wise patrons who are dear to many and provide excellent protection—
For they are the sons of Aditi, who know how to ward off hostilities; They are the wide-ruling ones, free from malice, even from distress.
May Aditi protect our cattle by day; may Aditi, free from duplicity, protect us by night.
May Aditi, ever-increasing, guard us from distress. And may that Aditi come to us with her aid during the day.
May she, with her healing power, grant us bliss and drive away our enemies.
And may those two divine physicians, the Aśvins, bring us well-being; may they ward off from here all affliction and drive away our enemies.
May Agni bring us peace with his fires; may Sūrya shine auspiciously upon us.
May the wind blow auspiciously, driving away misfortune and our enemies.
Drive away disease, drive away the adversary, and drive away ill-will.
O Ādityas, keep us away from distress. O Ādityas, keep the arrow away from us, and keep off the curse; O possessors of all wealth, drive our enemies far apart.
O Ādityas, grant us that protection which releases even the sinner from his sin, O bounteous givers. Whatever mortal, through demonic intent, seeks to harm us—
May the person who seeks to harm us with his own evil deeds be harmed; may he reach that mortal enemy of ill intent,
he who is hostile toward us and double-tongued.
O Gods, you are with the simple-hearted; you know the mortal within his heart, O Vasus, both the double-tongued and the single-minded.
We choose for ourselves the protection of the mountains and likewise that of the waters.
O Heaven and Earth, drive away from us the evil we have committed. O Vasus, with your auspicious protection, ferry us across all difficulties as if by your ship.
For our offspring and for ourselves, O Ādityas of great power, grant us that long life so that we may live.
O Ādityas, you who are most mighty, bestow this upon us.
For the sacrifice is within your favor; O Ādityas, be gracious.
In you indeed we find our kinship; we belong to you.
We implore the great protection of the Maruts, the divine savior Aśvins, Mitra, and Varuṇa for our well-being.
O Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa, grant us, like heroes, that sinless, praiseworthy, and threefold-sheltering protection, O Maruts. For we are indeed men, O Ādityas, who have death as our kinsman.
May you further extend our life-span for us to live. Praise him, the one who brings light to men; the gods have established him as the divine messenger. They have conveyed the oblation to the gods.
O sage, praise Agni, the giver of abundant wealth, whose radiance is manifold, the controller;
O Sobhari, praise him, the ancient one, for this Soma-sacrifice and for the rite. We have chosen you, the best of sacrificers, the immortal god among the gods, the invoker.
The skillful performer of this sacrifice— Agni, the Son of Strength, the fortunate one of splendid luster, whose flame is most excellent— may he, through his worship,
win for us the favor of Mitra, Varuṇa, and the Waters in heaven.
The mortal who has worshipped Agni with fuel, with oblations, and with sacred knowledge;
who, performing the rite well, has honored him with reverence—
his swift coursers gallop forth, and his glory is most resplendent.
No distress caused by the gods from any quarter, nor that wrought by mortals, shall reach us.
O Son of Strength, Lord of Power, may we be well-provided with fires through your fires;
you, rich in heroes, are well-disposed toward us.
Praising him like a friendly guest, Agni is to be known like a chariot;
in you abide secure and successful dwellings—you are the king of riches.
O Agni, that mortal who truly performs the sacrifice is fortunate and worthy of praise.
May he be a winner through his prayers— he for whose sacrifice you stand upright, O Lord of heroes;
he succeeds. He is a winner with his swift horses, he with his praisers, and he is a winner of the prize with his heroes.
In whose house Agni, the possessor of all desirable things, accepts the hymn with pleasure, or who, as a swift worker, zealously offers the oblations;
or [who honors] the sage who praises you, O Son of Strength, among the gifts of the most prompt one.
O Vasu, make the speech of the one who has found [thee] superior to the gods and proximate to mortals.
He who seeks to win over Agni— the one of great skill— with oblations of sacrificial food or with salutations, with a song [praising] him whose radiance is like that of a prize-winning steed.
The mortal who, with fuel and with fervor, worships Aditi through his sacred rites—
may he, blessed by his prayers, surpass all people with his splendors,
as one crosses over waters. O Agni, bring that glory which shall overcome every devouring demon in our dwelling.

The wrath of the evil-minded person; that by which Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman perceive, by which the Nāsatyas and Bhaga perceive— that we, through your power, O Indra, being the best finders of the path and protected by you, may worship.
O Agni, they indeed were wise, those inspired singers who established you, the one with the gaze of a man;
O God, the inspired ones [established] you, the one of good intent.
They, O fortunate one, have prepared for you the altar, they have prepared for you the oblation, and they have prepared the pressing of the soma in heaven.
With those strengths they have won great wealth—those who have directed their desire toward you.
May Agni be auspicious to us when invoked; auspicious be the gift, O fortunate one, and auspicious the sacrifice.
And may our praises be auspicious.
Form an auspicious mind for the conquest of Vṛtra, by which you may prevail in battles. Relax the many firm bows of those who defy us; may we overcome them through your aids.
I praise with song him who is beneficial to mankind, whom the gods appointed as their messenger and steward.

To Agni, the most excellent sacrificer, the bearer of oblations— to him with sharp teeth, the youthful, the radiant— sing forth a song of joy. He who, when offered oblations of clarified butter, fashions heroic power through his bounteous gifts.
When Agni, invoked with offerings of clarified butter, brandishes his axe now upward and now downward,
he is like an Asura putting on his robe.
He, the god established by Manu, has brought forth the oblations with his fragrant mouth.
The immortal god, the Hotṛ-priest of the fair sacrifice, distributes desirable boons.
O Agni, son of strength, invoked with oblations, if you were mortal and I were immortal, O you of Mitra-like greatness!
O Vasu, I would not deliver you over to calumny, nor to misfortune, O Excellent One.
Let my praiser not be in want, nor ill-fated, O Agni, nor suffer through sin.
Like a son well-nourished in his father’s house, let our oblation go forth to the gods.
O Agni, may I ever be accompanied by your most immediate aids, according to your pleasure, O Vasu;
for as a mortal, I am always [under the care] of the god. Through your wisdom, O Agni, through your gifts, and through your praises, may I obtain [wealth].
RV 8.19.29: O Vasu, they call you my providence; O Agni, take delight in giving.
RV 8.19.30: O Agni, he prospers through your aids, which bring heroic sons and bear away prizes—he whose friendship you have chosen.
Your dark-blue drop, lowing at the proper season, kindled, O bounteous one, has been taken up.
You are the beloved of the great Dawns; you rule over the nights and the dawns.
We, the Sobharis, have come for protection to him who possesses a thousand testicles and is a most excellent helper.
The sovereign lord of Trasadasyu—
O Agni, you to whom other fires are subordinate like branches;
like inspired songs, I gather your splendors from among the people, increasing your princely powers.
O Ādityas, free from guile, you lead that mortal across to the further shore—
ye all who are bountiful givers to every patron. O Kings, you who subdue the peoples, [lead] whoever dwells among men.
May we, O Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman, be the charioteers of your eternal Law (ṛta).
Trasadasyu, the son of Purukutsa, has given me fifty brides;
he is the most bountiful noble, the lord of the virtuous.
And at the ford of the Suvāstu, on the bank of the Prayiyu and Vayiyu rivers, Śyāva became the leader of three times seventy [cows], the lord of the Vasus who were being bestowed.
Come hither; do not fail us! O you who are ever-moving, do not stand still, for you are of one mind.
O Maruts, you who bend even the firm things, O R̥bhukṣans with your strong fellies, O Rudras with your brilliant splendors—
come today with food to our sacrifice, you who are much-desired and seek the offerings of Sobhari.
For we know the fierce might of the sons of Rudra, the Maruts, who are full of vigor; [we know it] of Viṣṇu, the swift one, and of the bounteous givers.
The islands fly asunder; distress stands still; they have joined both heaven and earth together.
The steeds with beautiful bits have sped across the desert wastes when you, O self-luminous ones, moved forth.
Even the immovable things roar at your onset—the mountains and the lord of the forest;
the earth trembles at your marches.
To give way to your coming, O Maruts, the vast heaven has yielded itself as a higher path, so that the heroes may display their powers upon their bodies—the powers born of the strength of their arms.
Following their own nature, the men are resplendent; they are mighty, impetuous, and bull-like in appearance.
They carry [the chariot], their forms unyielding.
The arrow of the Sobharis is anointed with the products of the cow upon the golden seat of the chariot.
O kinsmen of the cow, well-born and great, come now for our nourishment and enjoyment, that we may touch you.
O Maruts, you who are adorned with raindrops, bring forth your offerings for your vigorous host,
for the host that has vigorous steeds. O Maruts, come on your chariot drawn by vigorous horses, possessing vigorous power, and having a vigorous nave.
Like winged falcons, come swiftly, O heroes, to enjoy our oblations.
Their golden ornaments shine equally upon their arms,
and their spears flash brilliantly.
Those fierce ones, the bulls with fierce arms, have not striven against one another in their bodies.
Firm are the bows and weapons upon your chariots; upon your faces are the glories.
They whose name is as far-spreading as the ocean, and whose brilliance is terrifying, are for the enjoyment of all people.
Like birds, [they possess] the ancestral power.
Worship those Maruts; praise them! For of those roaring ones, there is no last one, as among the spokes of a wheel; such is their bounty, such is their greatness.
Fortunate was he among your aids, O Maruts, in former dawns, and he shall be so even now.
Or he, O heroes, to whose oblations you come as swift steeds for the sake of partaking them.
May your splendors and your gains of booty, O shakers, reach us with favor.
Just as the sons of Rudra, the youthful ones, desire from the divine Asura, the Ordainer of heaven, so shall it be fulfilled.
The Maruts, who are worthy of praise and are bounteous givers, who move among us as munificent lords— from them, O youths, turn toward us with a more gracious heart.
O Sobhari, with a most new song, sing forth to the youthful, purifying, and vigorous ones.
Sing! Like one tending cattle, sing to those who are victorious like boxers, who are to be invoked among all the Hotṛ-priests in every battle.
Pay homage with song to the Maruts, who are like radiant bulls and most renowned.
Even the cows, O Maruts, are of one mind; by common descent you are kinsmen. They lick one another’s humps.
Even a mortal, O dancers with golden ornaments upon your breasts, attains brotherhood with you.
O Maruts, come hither, for your friendship is ever constant and secure.
O bounteous Maruts, bring us a portion of the healing medicine of the Maruts;
you are our friends and our steeds.

With those aids wherewith you protect the Sindhu, wherewith you overcome [the foe], and wherewith you show favor to Akri-vi— O bringers of bliss, may your auspicious protections be a source of joy to us, keeping those who hate us at bay. O Maruts, who possess the beautiful sacrificial grass, whatever [power] is in the Sindhu, whatever is in the Asiknī, and whatever is in the oceans— [with that come to us].

The medicine that is in the mountains—seeing it all, you carry it within your bodies; with that, speak for us! O Maruts, heal the injury upon the earth of our sick man; restore what has been dislocated.

Seeking your aid, we call upon you, O matchless one, like those carrying a heavy load, for the sake of booty— we call upon you, the wondrous one. For our protection in this rite, let your youthful and fierce power come to us— you who are bold.
We friends have chosen you alone, O Indra, as our protector and winner of the spoil.
Come hither to these Soma-drops, O Lord of horses, Lord of cattle, Lord of the fertile fields!
Drink the Soma, O Lord of Soma!
For we, the friendless ones, O Indra, have drawn you hither—you who possess many friends—as inspired singers.
Come with all those forms of yours, O Bull, for the drinking of the Soma.
Sitting like birds at the exhilarating, speech-inspiring mead mixed with milk, they revel.
We roar aloud toward you, O Indra;
we address you with this homage. Why do you hesitate even for a moment?
O Lord of the Bay Steeds, our desires exist; you are the giver, and we exist—our prayers exist.
O Indra, we have indeed become recipients of your newest aid; for we have not known such abundance from you before, O wielder of the stone.
We know your friendship, O Hero, and your bounty; those things of yours, O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, we now implore.
And so, O Vasu, sharpen us for this very battle rich in cattle,
O fair-cheeked one! Him who brought this and that wealth to us in the past— him, Indra, I praise for you, O friends, for our protection.
The Lord of the good, the master of bay horses, the subduer of peoples—he indeed is the one who has gladdened us.
May that Maghavan bestow upon us, his worshippers, hundreds of cattle and horses.
O Bull, with you as our ally, we shall indeed speak back to the one who snarls at us.

In the assembly of the cattle-owning folk, O much-invoked Indra, may we, as doers, conquer those who do evil; may we overcome the malicious ones. With our men, may we slay Vṛtra and may we prosper. O Indra, further our prayers.
O Indra, by your very birth you have from of old been without a rival, without kin, and without a friend;
yet through battle you seek companionship. You find no wealthy man for friendship; those who drink wine hold you in contempt.
When you raise the roar of the flood, then indeed you are invoked like a father.
O Indra, let us not sit with you at the pressed juice like fools who have not attained full age, as companions of one such as you.
O giver of cattle, O Indra, may we not fail to obtain your bounty; may we not be deprived of your gifts.
Even the firm things of the enemy, seize them and bring them hither; for your gifts cannot be frustrated. Indeed, it is Indra who bestows this wealth, or the blessed Sarasvatī who grants riches.
O Citra, you alone are for the donor.
Citra indeed is the king; others are merely kings who dwell along the Sarasvatī.
Like Parjanya with his rain, he has spread abroad, bestowing thousands and tens of thousands.
I invoke that most wondrous chariot today for our protection,
O Aśvins, you who are easy to call upon and whose paths are red, which you mounted for the sake of Sūryā.
It is the chariot of ancient life, easy to invoke, much desired, the foremost in spoils of war, and preeminent.

O Sobhari, with your hymns of praise, we call upon the Aśvins—who are accompanied by favor, who possess benevolence, and who are without equal in the assembly—to be present here. With our salutations, we bring those two gods, who exist in many places, hither for our protection; they are the ones who go to the house of the donor.

One wheel of your chariot revolves; the other seeks out the food. O Lords of Splendor, may your favor hasten toward us like a milch-cow. That chariot of yours, O Aśvins, which has three seats and golden reins—
He adorns heaven and earth; renowned for this, O Nāsatyas, come hither!
Bestowing gifts upon Manu, you plough the ancient grain in the sky with the wolf.
As such, O Aśvins, Lords of Splendor, we shall praise you today with our hymns of devotion.
Come to us, O lords of wealth, by the paths of Truth, by which you, O bulls,
quickened Tr̥kṣi and Trasadasyu for great dominion. This Soma, O heroes, lords of bull-like wealth, has been pressed for you with stones.
Come for the drinking of the Soma; drink in the house of the donor.
Mount, O Aśvins, upon the chariot, upon the golden seat, O possessors of bovine wealth. Yoke your abundant nourishments.

With those aids wherewith you helped Paktha, wherewith you helped Adhrigu, and wherewith you helped Babhru when he was deprived of his companions— with those aids, O Aśvins, come to us quickly and swiftly, and heal that which is diseased.
When we call upon the Aśvins at this very time of day, O ye who are irresistible, even as we who are ourselves irresistible.
We, desiring to sing praises with our songs—

come hither with those [songs], O Bulls, to my call, which provides all nourishment and contains all that is desirable; O Heroes, most generous with food and most abundant in being, come hither with those [songs] by which you strengthened Krivi.
Praising them, I address those very Aśvins at the passing of the days;
we seek them with our prostrations.
Those two lords of splendor, Rudravartanī, [we invoke] at evening and at dawn upon their journey.
O possessors of wealth, O Rudras, do not reveal us to the hostile mortal. For our well-being,
I call upon the Aśvins at dawn with their auspicious chariot— the two who bring victory— just as Sobhari calls upon his father.
O bulls, swift as thought, distilling exhilaration, come with your aids that move quickly;
even from afar, be present for our protection with your many ancient succors, O you who provide manifold nourishment.
O Aśvins, O heroes, drinkers of the sweet draught, come to our dwelling rich in horses.
O wonder-workers, [grant us wealth] consisting of cattle and gold;
[grant us] a good lineage, great heroic power, and excellent desirable things that are unassailable by the Rakṣases.
On this approach of yours, O lords of ample wealth, may we obtain all precious things from you.

Praise him who is worthy of invocation; worship Jātavedas, whose smoke wanders abroad and whose radiance is ungraspable— Agni, the giver of gifts, with your song, O Viśvamanas, you who belong to all people.
And I praise the rival chariots of those whose assault is worthy of song, so that food and strength may be seized;
the priest finds wealth through their close assistance.
The flame of this one who shines brightly has risen up,
ageless, from him whose jaws are glowing, whose light is beautiful, and whose glory is in his troop.
Arise, O you of fair sacrifice, being praised with divine grace!
Shining brightly with great splendor, O Agni, come hither with excellent praises as you are offered the oblations in due order,
just as you have become the messenger, the bearer of the sacrificial offerings.
I invoke for you Agni, the ancient one, the Hotṛ-priest of the peoples;
him I laud with this speech, him indeed I praise.
Him of wondrous power, whom they bring to perfection through sacrifices and with their creative form.
Like a friend well-placed among the people, [he dwells] in the observer of Truth.
O seekers of Truth, with song you have approached him who observes Truth, the accomplisher of the sacrifice, at the place of homage; they have indeed delighted in him.
May our well-ordered sacrifices go toward him, the best of the Aṅgirases,
who is the most glorious Hotṛ among the people.
O Agni, those kindling logs of thine, undecaying, produce great light.
Like stallions seeking strength,
O Lord of power, grant us wealth and heroic might;
protect us in battles for our offspring and progeny.
Or when the Lord of the People, Agni, is sharpened and well-pleased among the human clans, he drives away all the *rakṣas* demons.
O hero, O Lord of the People, Agni, listen with favor to this new hymn of mine!
Burn down the guileful, burning Rākṣasas! No mortal enemy shall prevail through his magic against him who has given offerings to Agni with sacrificial gifts.
The seer Ukṣaṇyu, seeking horses, gratified you, the finder of wealth;
we kindle you for great riches.
Uśanas Kāvya established you as the Hotṛ priest.
I have sacrificed to you, Jātavedas, for the sake of Manu;
for all the gods, acting in unison, have made you their messenger. O God, through your readiness to hear, you have become the first one worthy of sacrifice.

Let the mortal hero indeed make this immortal one his messenger— him who is purifying, whose path is black, and who traverses the vast space. With ladles uplifted, let us invoke him who is of beautiful luster and radiant brilliance.
Agni, the ageless and ancient one, worthy of praise among the people— The mortal who provides him with oblations through the giving of offerings,
He bestows abundant nourishment and glory accompanied by heroic sons.
To Agni Jātavedas, the first and foremost in sacrifices,
let the ladle full of oblation go forth with reverence.
With these most excellent hymns, we shall worship Agni like Vyaśva.
