With most bountiful hymns, [worship] him of brilliant luster.
Now indeed, O seer Vyaśva, praise with songs of praise, like Sthūrayūpa,
Agni who is to be tamed.
The inspired singers implore for protection the ancient Agni, the guest of men and the son of the lords of the forest.
He overcomes all great adversaries and [approaches] the oblations of men.
O Agni, sit down upon the sacred grass with reverence.
Grant us many desirable things; grant us wealth sought by many—wealth consisting of heroic sons, abundant progeny, and glory.
O Agni, you are the bestower; impel the gift toward Suṣāman and his people.
O Most Youthful One, O Vasu, grant bounty forever to everyone.
For you are truly a mighty conqueror; you are our source of food accompanied by cattle.
O Agni, open up the attainment of great wealth.
O Agni, you are glorious; bring hither Mitra and Varuṇa, the two sovereign kings who uphold the cosmic order and possess purified will.
O friends, let us learn the sacred prayer for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt;
I praise him, the most heroic and bold,
for he is renowned for his power as the slayer of Vṛtra by virtue of his deed against Vṛtra.
O Hero, with your bounties you bestow gifts beyond those of other wealthy patrons.
Thus praised, bring us wealth of most wondrous fame—
wealth that, O Lord of Bay Horses, grants riches even in the very midst of scarcity.
O Indra, disclose the secret treasure and that which is dear to men;
O bold one, being praised, bring it hither with courage.
No obstructors can restrain either your left hand or your right.
O Lord of the Bay Steeds, there is no obstacle for you in the raids for cattle.
O Wielder of the Stone, I enclose you with my songs as one encloses a stall with cows. Fulfill the desire and the mind of the singer.
O most excellent slayer of Vṛtra, with your wisdom grant us all things for us who are all-minded.
O fierce one, O Vasu, come hither as our leader.
O hero, slayer of Vṛtra, may we know this newest work of yours.
O Vasu, invoked by many, [bestow] upon us desirable wealth.
O Indra, O Dancer, for as your power is indeed unassailable, so too, O much-invoked one, is your gift to the donor unimpaired.
O most magnificent one, most manly Indra, pour forth for great bounty!
O Maghavan, though you are firm, be even firmer for the granting of wealth!
O wielder of the stone, our prayers have never gone elsewhere than to you.
O Maghavan, grant us that through your aids!
For truly, O Dancer, I find no one other than you for the granting of wealth—
for riches, for glory, and for power, O Lover of Song.
Pour out [the soma] for Indra; he drinks the honeyed mead.
He shall impel us with bounty by his greatness. I have addressed the Lord of the two bay steeds, the skillful one who bestows abundance.
Now, truly, hear the one who praises you, the son of Aśva.
For indeed, O Lord, even in the past no hero was ever born greater than you;
none is equal to you in wealth, nor in such deeds, nor in glory.
Come, O Adhvaryu, pour out for us the most intoxicating of the sweet juices,
for thus is the Hero praised, he who ever increases our prosperity.
O Indra, driver of the bay steeds, no one surpasses your ancient praise.
We have celebrated him with our strength, as if with songs of praise. Seeking glory, we invoke you, O Lord of spoils,
who is to be magnified by sacrifices that do not fail.
Come now, O friends, let us praise Indra, the hero worthy of hymns, who alone surpasses all the tribes.
To him who does not withhold the cattle, who seeks the kine, the celestial one, let us speak wondrous speech.
Declare that he is sweeter than ghee and honey;
his heroic powers are immeasurable, and his bounty cannot be surpassed.
His sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) surpasses everything, like light.
Praise Indra like Vyaśva—him who is waveless, the possessor of booty, the controller;
him who, bestowing the wealth of the noble one, grants it to the donor.
Thus now, O son of Vyaśva, praise him—the tenth, the new.
The wise one, worthy of praise among those who move; for you know, O wielder of the thunderbolt, how to avoid the snares of destruction,
day after day, like one who purifies himself from pitfalls.

O Indra, bring that [wealth] for us, by which you, O most wondrous one, struck down for Kutsa in the past; urge it toward us now. We entreat you now, O most wondrous one, for new [gifts] for the sake of winning.
As such, may you overcome all our adversaries.
You who deliver from the devouring of the wolf and from distress within the seven rivers— O you of many heroic deeds, humble the Dāsa.
As you brought wealth to Varo Suṣāman for his gains,
O blessed one, rich in steeds, to the Vyaśvas; so let the sacrificial fee of Nārya come to the Soma-pressing Vyaśvas.
And may there be abundant bounty, consisting of hundreds and thousands!
If one who has sacrificed should ask thee, "O thou of wondrous deeds, where art thou?"— this powerful one, having taken refuge here, dwells by the Gomatī river.
Those two guardians of the universe, the gods among gods worthy of sacrifice,
the upholders of *ṛta*, whose skill is born of their own power— you worship them. Like two charioteers, they are Mitra and Varuṇa, who is of excellent wisdom, joined together in their lineage.
From of old, well-born, their offspring are steadfast in their vows;
Aditi, the observer of Truth, brought forth those two all-knowing ones, the great mothers, for the sake of divine power with exceeding majesty.
Great are Mitra and Varuṇa, sovereign gods and lords of power; upholding the cosmic order, they proclaim the lofty Law.
They are the grandsons of great strength, the sons of Dakṣa, possessed of excellent wisdom.
O you who grant wide-reaching gifts, you dwell upon the dwelling-places of nourishment.
You two have gathered together the gifts of heaven and the nourishments of the earth; let your rainfalls come hither, accompanied by clouds.
They who look down from the lofty heaven like herds of cattle, the two sovereign kings, observers of *ṛta*, established for the sake of homage;
the two observers of *ṛta*, of noble will, have sat down for universal sovereignty.
Firm in their vows, the two Kṣatriyas have attained sovereign power. Finding the path even for the eye with unblinking vision, though closing their eyes, they perceive with keen insight.
May the goddess Aditi protect us; may the Nāsatyas protect us;
may the Maruts of increased strength protect us. O bounteous ones, protect our ship by day and by night.
May we, unharmed, be united with those who protect us. May we, unharmed, serve the non-slaying Viṣṇu, the giver of good gifts.
O self-moving Sindhu, hear us for our first thought.
We choose that desirable, most excellent, and well-guarded boon which Mitra, Varuṇa, and Aryaman protect for us. And may Sindhu, the lord of waters, the Maruts, and the Aśvins grant that to us.
Indra, Viṣṇu, and the bountiful ones, acting in harmony—
For they, the eager heroes, indeed strike down the hostile assault of any man, Like a sharp flood, they who are impetuous.
This one alone thus gazes far and wide as the lord of the people;
we follow his sacred laws.
We follow his ancient, familiar ordinances of sovereign rule.
The far-famed ordinances of Mitra and Varuṇa—
he who measured out the ends of heaven and earth with his ray has filled both world-halves with his greatness.
Up has risen yonder Sūrya, the light of heaven, for our protection—
bright like Agni when kindled and offered oblations.
He who dwells in the far-reaching distance is master of speech and of wealth consisting of cattle.
For he is the lord over the granting of wholesome food;
therefore, O Sūrya, I address you and both worlds, heaven and earth, at evening and at dawn.
Rise up always for us among those who enjoy your bounty.
At the sacrifice of Ukṣaṇyāyana we won a swift, silver chariot harnessed with bay horses at the sacrifice of Harayāṇa;
and at the sacrifice of Suṣāmaṇ we won a chariot yoked with steeds. These two bay stallions of mine are the bestowers of wealth.
And now, for the sake of those who perform deeds, [I call] the two who carry heroes,
who possess reins and whips; may the inspired singers, with their newest hymn,
be present together with the two great, prize-winning, swift steeds.
I call hither your chariot for joint praise among the patrons—
O you of unassailable skill, O bulls, O possessors of bull-like wealth!
You two, O Nāsatyas, [came] for Varo Suṣāman’s great lineage.
As you have [helped] with aids, O bulls, O possessors of bull-like wealth— such as you two we invoke today with oblations, O lords of powerful steeds.
You who seek to provide abundant nourishment, protect us through the nights.
O Aśvins, heroes, let your most swift and renowned chariot come hither;
behold the hymns of the zealous one for the sake of glory.
O Aśvins, possessors of bull-like wealth, even though you are far away, take heed of us.
For you two, O Rudras, shall carry us across our enemies;
for you two, O wonder-workers, fly swiftly around all that is human, O lords of splendor, stirring the prayer and honey-colored with your speed.
Come to us, O Aśvins, together with wealth that nourishes all;
come, O bounteous lords, endowed with heroic sons, unshakable. Come to me, O Nāsatyas, to receive this offering of mine.
O Gods, most worthy of being honored by the gods today—
For we, like Vyaśva, call upon you both while offering oblations;
Come hither now, O Sages, with your gracious favors.
O Aśvins, O seer, praise them; will they not hear your call?
May they drive away the Paṇis who are closer at hand.
O Heroes, listen to Vyaśva and take heed of this my prayer.
May Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman, acting in harmony,
O wise ones, grant me day by day what has been given by you and brought by you through the patron-sages, O bulls. Bestow these gifts upon me.

He who is encompassed by your sacrifices like a bride upon her wedding garment— him the Aśvins, being honored, have made beautiful for splendor. He who takes thought of you, the most wide-extending protectors of men.
O Aśvins, come around our dwelling-place, seeking us;
O you who possess bull-like wealth, come well to our path that leads to the heroes.
Like two seekers of the sacrifice, you have carried it forward through our song.
The most effective of all invocations, this hymn, as a messenger calling you,
O Heroes, has been sent to you both, O Aśvins. When you rejoice in that ocean of heaven, in the dwelling-place of nourishment;
O immortal ones, hear my cry!
And this Śvetayāvarī river is the most swift of all rivers for you two— the Sindhu, whose path is golden.
O Aśvins, with this well-praised hymn and with pure devotion, you who travel in splendor, come hither. Yoke, O Vasu, your chariot that overcomes all; harness the steeds that bring prosperity.
O Vāyu, drink our honeyed mead; come to our libations!
O Vāyu, Lord of Truth, wondrous son-in-law of Tvaṣṭṛ, we choose your protections.
We pray to the son-in-law of Tvaṣṭṛ, the lord of wealth; we, the people who have pressed the soma, seek glory from you, O Vāyu. O Vāyu, come from heaven auspiciously; bring us excellent horses.
Carry [us] on your great, broad-winged chariot; for we invoke you, the most beautiful in form, in the assemblies of men—
like a pressing-stone with a horse's back, through your generosity.
As such, O divine Vāyu, gladdened in your mind as the foremost one, grant us strength, waters, and inspired thoughts.
Agni is the chief priest at the hymn of praise; the pressing-stones and the sacred grass are at the sacrifice.
With a *ṛc*-verse I seek the Maruts, Brahmaṇaspati, and the gods for desirable aid.
I sing to the cattle, to the earth, to the trees, to Dawn and Night, and to the plants.
And may you all, O Vasus, possessors of all wealth, be the furtherers of our prayers.
May our sacrifice proceed forth to the gods through Agni as its ancient leader—
to the Ādityas, to Varuṇa whose laws are firm, and to the Maruts who shine over all. For all you possessors of all wealth, destroyers of enemies, have indeed become the increasers of man.
O you who possess all knowledge, come with your unharmed protections, and grant us a dwelling free from the wolf.
Come to us today, all of one mind and in full accord; O Maruts, O Goddess Aditi, come with our hymn and song to this great seat and home.
O Maruts, come toward our dear offerings, those consisting of horses; O Mitra, proceed to them!
May Indra, Varuṇa, and the Ādityas, the swift heroes, sit upon our sacrificial grass. We, having spread the *barhis* grass and prepared the sacrificial food, offer it to you in due order.
O Varuṇa, we who have pressed the Soma call upon you, like Manu, with our fires well-kindled. O Maruts, Viṣṇu, Aśvins, and Pūṣan, come forth with a thought directed toward me!
Let Indra come first with those seeking to win; he is the bull, the slayer of Vṛtra, who is celebrated by our songs.
O guileless gods, extend to us a flawless protection, such that no one, O Vasus, may assail this shelter from afar or even from near at hand.
For there is kinship with you, O gods who destroy the foe; there is also fellowship with you.
Proclaim for us toward our former prosperity; quickly [proclaim] for new favor!
For now indeed I have sent forth this hymn of praise to you, for the sharing of wealth—O possessors of all knowledge, I, the worshiper, have sent it forth as if toward another.
Up has risen for you that Savitṛ, the excellent leader, the one to be chosen, standing erect.
The bipeds and the quadrupeds, seeking their goals, have settled down, as have the birds ready to fly.
For your protection, we call upon god after god; for our aid, we call upon god after god.
Let us invoke each god for the winning of booty, praising them with divine prayer.
For all the gods, being of one mind toward Manu, have granted their gifts together.
May they be our protectors today and in the future, and may they find wide space for our offspring.
I proclaim before you, O guileless ones, this assembly of hymns of praise.
No harm, O Varuṇa and Mitra, reaches that mortal who honors your divine ordinances. He who offers gifts according to your will extends his dwelling and increases his great provisions.
He is born again through offspring according to the cosmic law; unharmed, he prospers in every way.
Without conflict, he finds battles; by easy paths he travels his journeys—he whom Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuṇa, acting in concert and with one accord, protect as their kin.
Even on level ground, you provide him a place to rest; even in difficult terrain, you make it easy for him to traverse.
May this very thunderbolt fall far away from him, perishing in its own course.
When the sun rises today, O lords of dear dominion, may he establish the cosmic order (*ṛta*).
O all-knowing ones, whether at sunset or at dawn, or at midday of the sky,
or at the arrival of evening, O Asuras, grant protection to the one who follows the *ṛta* and to the donor;
may we, O Vasus, possessors of all wealth, abide in the midst of that [protection] of yours.
Whatever good you bestow today upon Manu when the sun has risen, at midday, or at the setting of the light—
O possessors of all wealth, you who have offered oblations for the sake of the wise one—
we choose that same abundant protection from you, O sovereign kings, as a son chooses his father.
May we, O Ādityas, obtain that oblation as we offer it, by which we may attain greater prosperity.
The thirty-three gods who have sat upon the sacrificial grass, knowing the great friendship, have taken their seats.
Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, and the Agnis who bestow gifts together— may they, accompanied by their wives and consecrated with the cry of *vaṣaṭ*,
be our guardians from the west, from above, and likewise from below.
With their entire host, from the front,
let it be as the gods desire; none shall diminish this of theirs,
not even a hostile mortal.
The seven carry seven spears; seven are their splendors; they have assumed seven glories.
One is brown, manifold, noble, and youthful; he anoints himself with golden [ornaments].
One has sat down in the womb, radiant and wise among the gods.
One bears an iron axe in his hand, steadfast among the gods. One bears the thunderbolt placed in his hand; with it, he strikes down the Vṛtras.
One bears a sharp weapon in his hand; he is pure, fierce, and possesses healing medicines.
Another has nourished the paths like a thief; he knows the hidden treasures.
The wide-striding one has taken three steps where the gods rejoice.
The two move with three [wheels] together with one; they dwell as if on a journey. The two have made for themselves a seat near heaven, sovereign kings who drink the clarified butter.
Some, chanting, conceived the great *sāman*; by it they caused the sun to shine.
For among you, O gods, there is no one who is small, nor any who is a child;
all of you are indeed great. Thus shall you be praised, O destroyers of enemies, you who are thirty and three.
The gods worthy of sacrifice belong to Manu;
as such, protect us, aid us, and speak for us.
Do not lead us far away from the paternal path of Manu into distant realms.
O all you gods who are here, and you Vaiśvānaras,
grant us wide-reaching protection for our cattle and our horses.
Whoever sacrifices, sacrifices repeatedly, presses the Soma, and cooks the oblation—
The prayer has pleased Indra. He who offers him the sacrificial cake and the pressed Soma mixed with milk—
that Śakra has delivered him from distress.
His radiant chariot, impelled by the gods, has grown great;
he conquers all who act with hostility.
In his house dwells a prolific and inexhaustible abundance day after day.
The *iḷā* yields milk like a cow; O gods, those who, being of one mind as husband and wife, press and wash [the soma] with the constant mixture.
They have partaken of the sacrificial food from here; turning toward the sacred grass, they have taken their seats. They do not falter in the contests for booty;
they do not forget the favor of the gods, nor do they shrink from it.
May they win great renown while seeking it. Possessing sons and daughters, may they enjoy the full span of life;
both of them are adorned with golden ornaments.
May the two who enjoy the oblation and possess bestowed wealth grant us favor for the sake of the sacred law.
May they strike down the hairy *samudha* and perform service among the gods.
We choose the protection of the mountains and of the rivers.
May they come together with Viṣṇu.
May Pūṣan, Wealth, and Bhaga come; may he who bestows all blessings bring well-being. May the wide path lead to well-being.
The unassailable Aramati, with her mind, [is united] with every god;
she has attained the non-hostility of the Ādityas.
Just as Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa are our guardians, so may they be.
The paths of Truth are easy to traverse.
With my song, I praise Agni, the ancient god of your treasures—
the one who is much beloved, whom we serve like Mitra, the establisher of our domain.
Swift is the chariot of the one who favors the gods, like a hero in any battle whatsoever;
he who, as a sacrificer, strives to win the mind of the gods, shall surpass those who do not sacrifice.
O sacrificer, you shall not come to harm; neither shall the presser of the soma, nor the one devoted to the gods.
He who [controls] the mind of the gods...
No one shall reach him by deed, nor shall he be left behind; he shall not be left behind.
He who [controls] the mind of the gods...
Therein lies great heroic power, and there too that wealth of horses,
for he who fulfills the will of the gods. The Kaṇvas have proclaimed the deeds of the impetuous Indra with a song.
Proclaim, while intoxicated by Soma,
[the deeds] of him who, fierce, slew Sṛbinda, Anarśani, Pipru, and the Dāsa Ahīśuva, and released the waters.
You have struck down the dwelling-place and the lofty height of Arbuda;
you performed that manly deed, O Indra.
Boldly, as if from a mountain, you have hurled [the bolt] against the one who hears you.
I invoke the fair-cheeked one for protection.
May he, being exhilarated by the Soma-pressers, burst open the pen of cattle and horses for us,
O hero, as if shattering a fortress.
If you take pleasure in my pressed juice or find delight in my hymn of praise, come from afar by your own power!
O Indra, lover of songs, we indeed belong to you as your praisers.
O Soma-drinker, quicken us!
And bring us food, O bounteous one, bestowing it unceasingly;
for great is your wealth, O Maghavan.
And make us possessors of cattle, of gold, and of horses;
may we grasp them firmly with our invocations.
We invoke Bṛhaduktha, whose hands are swift, for our protection.

He who, even in the midst of battle, being the wise slayer of Vṛtra and possessor of many riches, brings about the first [victory] for his singers to aid them— may he act effectively for our protection.
May he, the powerful Śakra, who brings gifts from nearby, be able to help us;
may Indra with all his aids [protect us].
He who is the great vessel of riches, the easy passage for the one who presses the soma, the friend of the sacrificer.
Sing forth to that Indra,
who comes as a mighty and steadfast one, who wins glory in battles,
and who rules over abundance by his power.
There is no restrainer of his powers, of his true gifts;
there is no one who can say, "He has not given.
Indeed, there is now no debt for the zealous priests who press the soma.
Soma has been drunk by the peerless one.
Praise him; sing unto him who is worthy of praise; recite hymns to him who is worthy of praise; offer sacred prayer to him who is worthy of praise.
May the praiseworthy Indra, the unimpeded one who increases the prosperity of the sacrificer, shatter hundreds and thousands [of foes].
Go forth indeed according to your own power, following the invocations of the peoples.
O Indra, drink of the pressed juices!
Drink of those mixed with their own milk, and of that which was with Tugrya;
and this, O Indra, is yours.
Pass by the one who utters wrath while pressing [the juice] at the end; drink this offered libation that has been pressed. Go beyond the three distant realms; go beyond the five peoples.
O Indra,
let my prayers look toward you; may my songs hold you fast, as the sun sends forth its ray, like waters flowing together toward the lowland.
O Adhvaryu, pour out the Soma for the hero with the handsome jaws;
bring the pressed juice for his drinking.
He who split the water-holding mountain and sent the rivers flowing downward.
He who held the cooked food among the cattle; he, O worthy of praise, slew Vṛtra, Aurṇavābha, and Ahīśuva,
and pierced Arbuda with frost.
Sing forth the god-given prayer for your fierce, impetuous, unconquerable, and victorious one. He who, in the exhilaration of the Soma plant, presides over all sacred ordinances.
Indra takes heed among the gods.
Here are those two bay steeds, companions at the feast, with golden manes; let them carry him toward the prepared food.
O you who are praised by many, may the two bay steeds, lauded by the Priyamedhas,
bring you hither to drink the Soma. We indeed, having pressed the juice and trimmed the sacred grass, call upon you as waters flow.
O Vṛtra-slayer, at the outpourings of the filter, the praisers sit around thee.
O Vasu, when the Soma is pressed, the men who recite hymns sing to thee alone.
When, O Indra, thirsty for the pressed juice, wilt thou come to our home, like a bellowing bull?
O bold one, with the Kaṇvas, boldly strike out thousandfold booty. O Maghavan, O far-seeing one, we quickly implore you for that golden-hued wealth consisting of cattle.
Drink from the soma-juice at the exhilaration for Indra, O Medhyātithi.
He who is joined with the two bay steeds at the pressed juice, the wielder of the thunderbolt, whose chariot is golden;
he who is excellent on the left and excellent on the right, the lord praised as one of perfect wisdom;
he who is the source of thousands, the possessor of hundreds of riches, Indra, who is the shatterer of fortresses.
He who is bold, he who is unrestrained, he who rests upon his beard—possessing far-reaching splendor, the shaker, much-praised, mighty in his will like a bull.
Who knows him as he drinks beside the pressed juice? What vital power does he bestow?

He who, exhilarated by the soma-juice, shatters the fortresses with his might—the fair-cheeked one—like a wild elephant in its rutting season, he has assumed his course in many places. No one can hold you back; come to the pressed juice! You move as a great one through your own power.

He who is fierce, unsubdued, firm, and prepared for battle—if Maghavan Indra hears the call of the singer, he will not stay away but shall come. Truly, you are such a bull; with the speed of a bull, come to us, unobstructed.
For you are heard of as a fierce bull in the distance, and as a bull renowned nearby.
Bulls are your reins; the golden whip is a bull.
O Maghavan, the chariot is a bull, the two bay steeds are bulls; you, O Satakratu, are a bull.
O Bull, let the presser press for you; O Bull, O Ṛjīpin, bring [the Soma].
The Bull has flowed toward the Bulls in the rivers, for you, O driver of the tawny steeds.
Come here, O Indra, most powerful one, to drink the sweet Soma juice.
May this Maghavan, the one of excellent wisdom, not fail to hear our songs, our prayers, and our hymns. Let the bay steeds, yoked to the chariot, carry you, who stand upon the car,
across even the enemy’s libations, O Vṛtra-slayer, O Śatakratu, [and those] of others.
O Most Great One, accept today our most intimate hymn of praise!
May our libations be most soothing for your exhilaration, O celestial Soma-drinker! For neither you nor I take pleasure in the instruction of another.
The hero who brought us here—
even Indra himself has said that the mind of a woman is ungovernable, and her resolve is fickle.
Even the two steeds, exhilarated by the soma, draw the chariot as a pair;
thus indeed is the bull superior. Look downward, not upward; bring your feet closer together.
Let them not see your two testicles; for you have become a Brahmin through a woman. Come hither, O Indra, with your bay steeds to the beautiful hymn of Kaṇva.
You who rule from yonder heaven, you who went to heaven, O you whose wealth is light!

May the pressing-stone, speaking here as it holds the Soma, draw you hither with its sound from yonder heaven. Here, as the rim of these [stones] shakes the stalks, it is like a wolf shaking out the entrails.
From yonder sky...
The Kaṇvas call upon you here for protection and for the winning of booty.
From yonder sky...
I offer for you, the bull, the first draught of the pressed juices,
as from yonder heaven.
Come hither with us, O you who possess abundant wisdom, for our protection on every side.
From yonder sky...
Come to us, O most mighty one, with a thousandfold stream, O lord of a hundred bounties,
from yonder sky...
May the Hotṛ priest, established by Manu and worthy of praise among the gods, bring you hither from yonder heaven. ...
May your two bay steeds, dripping with exhilaration, carry you hither like two wings carrying a falcon.
From yonder sky...
Come hither from afar, O Noble One; Svāhā! for the drinking of the Soma.
From yonder sky...
Come to us, having heard our call; take delight here in our hymns.
From that very heaven...
Come well to us with those who are like you, O you whose horses are gathered together.
From that yonder heaven... Come hither from the mountains, from the summit of the ocean;
from that yonder heaven...
O Hero, burst open for us thousands of cattle and horses;
[open the doors] of yonder heaven. Bring to us by the thousands, tens of thousands, and hundreds.
From yonder sky...
When Indra and I received a thousand of Vasurocis,
the most powerful herd of horses.
Those steeds, brown as the wind in speed, ruddy and swift-gliding,
shine like suns;
they are among the gifts of Pārāvata, with wheels that roll swiftly.
Standing in the midst of the forest,
O Aśvins, drink the Soma together with Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Viṣṇu, the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus; being of one accord, together with Uṣas and Sūrya, drink the Soma, O Aśvins.
With all prayers, with the world, O possessors of vigor, with heaven, earth, and the mountains, being together;
with the Dawn, being in harmony; with all the gods, the three times eleven, here with the waters, the Maruts, and the Bhṛgus, being together.
In harmony with Uṣas...
[enjoy the sacrifice, be mindful of my invocation; O two gods, come here to all the libations.
In harmony with Uṣas and with Sūrya, O Aśvins, bring us nourishment.
May you two enjoy the hymn of praise like a youth with a maiden; O two gods, come here to all the libations at this sacrifice.
Being of one mind with Dawn and with Sūrya, grant us nourishment...
Enjoy our songs; enjoy the sacrifice; O two gods, come here to all the libations at this sacrifice.
In harmony with the Dawn and with Sūrya, [bring] nourishment...
Like two *hāridrava* birds you fly toward the forest; like two buffalo, you descend to the pressed Soma.
In harmony with the Dawn and with Sūrya, O Aśvins, travel your circuit three times.
Like two swans you fly; like travelers on the road, you come down to the pressed Soma like two buffaloes.
Being of one accord with Uṣas and Sūrya, [you come] three times...
Like two hawks you fly for the giving of the oblation; you come down to the pressed Soma like two buffaloes.
In harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya, thrice...
drink and be satisfied, and come hither; bestow progeny and bestow wealth. In harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya, O Aśvins, bestow vigor upon us.
Conquer and be praised; protect us and bestow progeny, and bestow wealth.
Being of one mind with Uṣas and Sūrya, grant us vigor...
Slay the enemies and strive for our friends; bestow progeny and bestow wealth.
In harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya, come to us with nourishment...
Accompanied by Mitra and Varuṇa, and by Dharma, and by the Maruts, come to the call of the singer.
In harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya, and with the Ādityas, O Aśvins, come hither.
Accompanied by the Aṅgirases and by Viṣṇu, and accompanied by the Maruts, come to the invocation of the singer.
Being of one accord with Uṣas and Sūrya, and with the Ādityas...
Accompanied by the Ṛbhus, O Bulls, and accompanied by Vāja and the Maruts, come to the invocation of the singer.
In harmony with the Dawn and with Sūrya, and with the Ādityas...
Quicken the sacred prayer and quicken our thoughts; slay the demons and drive away diseases.
In harmony with the Dawn and with Sūrya, O Aśvins, [protect] the one who presses the Soma.
Quicken the ruling power and quicken the men; slay the demons and drive away diseases.
In harmony with the Dawn and with Sūrya, [drink] the Soma...
Quicken the milch-cows and quicken the people; slay the demons and drive away diseases.
In harmony with Uṣas and with Sūrya, [drink] the Soma...
Like those of Atri, hear the ancient praise of Śyāvāśva, who presses the juice, O you who flow with exhilaration;
In harmony with Uṣas and with Sūrya, O Aśvins, [hear] that which has come across the day.
Like creating emanations, come to the well-fashioned hymns of Śyāvāśva who presses the juice, O you who flow with exhilaration;
O Aśvins, being of one accord with Uṣas and Sūrya, come to the sacrifices of Śyāvāśva who presses the juice, O you who flow with exhilaration.
Like holding the reins, come to the sacrifices of Śyāvāśva who presses the juice, O you who flow with exhilaration.
In harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya, O Aśvins...
Drive your chariot hither; drink the honeyed soma-sweetness.
Come, O Aśvins; arrive! Seeking your aid, I call upon you. Bestow treasures upon the donor.
When the sacrifice has been set forth with an invocation of homage, O Heroes, come for the drinking of the exhilarating draught. ... Come hither!
Satisfy yourselves, O Gods, with the pressed soma-juice consecrated by the cry of *svāhā*.
Come hither...
You shall be the protector of the one who presses the juice and has strewn the sacrificial grass; drink the Soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu!
That portion which they have set apart for you—you, the conqueror of all hostile armies, the wide-striding one, the winner of the waters—come with the Maruts, O Indra, Lord of the virtuous.
Protect the singer, O Maghavan; protect yourself. Drink the Soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu!
That portion which is yours... With nourishment you aid the gods, with vigor you aid yourself. Drink the Soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu!
That portion which is yours...
[O Indra,] the progenitor of heaven, the progenitor of earth, drink the Soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu!
That portion which is yours...
You are the progenitor of horses, the progenitor of cattle; drink the *soma* for exhilaration, O Śatakratu!
That portion which is yours...
O wielder of the stone, make the hymn of the Atris great; drink the *soma* for exhilaration, O Śatakratu!
The portion which is yours...
Listen likewise to Śyāvāśva as he presses the juice, just as you listened to Atri when he performed his rites;
you alone, O Indra, protected Trasadasyu in the struggle for men, strengthening his sacred prayers.
In the battles against Vṛtra, you protected this prayer; O Indra, Lord of Might, with all your aids, protect the one who presses the Soma.
O Slayer of Vṛtra, wielder of the thunderbolt, drink of the Soma at the midday libation—O blameless one!
O fierce Indra, Lord of Might, overcoming hostile armies with all your aids, [protect us].
Of the midday [pressing]...
O sole king of this world, you rule with all your aids, O Indra, Lord of Might!
Of the midday [pressing]...
O Indra, Lord of Might, you alone, with all your protections, drive away those who possess cattle.
[Of the midday pressing...
O Indra, Lord of Might, you rule over both security and exertion, with all your protections.
Of the midday [pressing]...
For the sake of the ruling power (*kṣatra*), you have helped us; you have protected us, O Lord of Might (*śacīpati*), with all your aids, O Indra.
Of the midday [pressing]...
Listen likewise to the chanting of Śyāvāśva, just as you listened to Atri while he was performing his rites.
O Indra, you alone protected Trasadasyu, increasing his princely powers in the struggle for men.
For you two are the officiating priests of the sacrifice, winners in contests and in ritual acts.
O Indra and Agni, take heed of this!
O bounteous ones, who travel in your chariot, slayers of Vṛtra, unconquered— O Indra and Agni, take heed of this!
The men have milked this exhilarating mead for you both with the pressing-stones;
O Indra and Agni, take heed of it! May you two, praised together, enjoy the sacrifice for the sake of the rite and the pressed Soma.
O Indra and Agni, O heroes, come hither!
Be pleased with these libations, by which you carry away the oblations. O Indra and Agni, O heroes, come hither!
O Indra and Agni, Heroes, enjoy this my well-wrought praise that follows the path of the *gāyatrī*; come hither with the gods who move at dawn, O you whose wealth is noble.
O Indra and Agni, come for the drinking of the Soma!
O Indra and Agni, hear the invocation of Śyāvāśva as he presses the juice, and that of the Atris; come for the drinking of the Soma!
Thus I call upon you both for aid, just as the wise have called,
O Indra and Agni, for the drinking of the Soma.
I choose the protection of Indra and Agni, who are accompanied by Sarasvatī.
By means of whom the *gāyatra* is sung;
I shall praise Agni, the one worthy of hymns; I shall worship Agni with *īḷā*.
May Agni anoint the gods for us, for as a seer he moves between both assemblies on his mission as messenger. May all others, the base ones, be destroyed!
O Agni, through our newest speech, we place within our bodies the praise of these [men].
May the hostilities of the stingy ones, all the enmities of the enemy, be driven far away. Let the godless ones perish; let all others be destroyed.
O Agni, we offer these prayers to you like clarified butter poured into your mouth.

Make yourself known among the gods, for you are the ancient, auspicious messenger of Vivasvat. Let all others who are hostile perish! Agni bestows that very vital strength upon us, according as each one prays for it. He, the oblation of vigor, bestows upon the Vasus health, prosperity, and joy for every invocation of the gods. Let all others who are hostile perish!
Agni has distinguished himself by his most powerful and wondrous deed;

he is the Hotṛ-priest of all people, encompassed by sacrificial gifts. He bestows what is to be offered. May all others, the base ones, perish! Agni knows the births of the gods; Agni knows the secret of mortals.
Agni is the giver of wealth; Agni opens the doors when he is invoked with a new oblation. Let all others perish, even those who are near!
Agni dwells among the gods and among the clans worthy of sacrifice.
With joy he nourishes many poetic insights, like the earth nourishing all things; he is the god among gods, worthy of worship. Let all others perish, even those who are near!

The Agni who dwells among the seven human tribes, who rests within all the rivers—to him we have come, to the one with three abodes, the greatest slayer of Dasyus for Mandhātṛ, the ancient Agni at the sacrifices. May all others perish!
Agni, the sage, inhabits the three triple realms in the assembly; may he, the inspired priest and consecrated messenger, worship and satisfy here the three times eleven gods. May all others perish!
O Agni, you alone rule over wealth among us mortals and among the gods, O Primordial One.
The waters, flowing around with their own banks, go about you; let all those others who are enemies be destroyed.
O Indra and Agni, may you two, as conquerors, bestow excellent wealth upon us.
By which we may overcome even the firm and the solid in battles—like Agni through the woods, like the wind—let all those who are hostile perish!
For we do not conceal you two; rather, we worship this Indra, the most powerful hero among men.
May he come to us at any time with his steed for the winning of booty, may he come for the winning of wisdom! Let all those who are hostile perish!
For Indra and Agni dwell upon the midst of our offerings;

they are the two sages who, when questioned with wisdom by one seeking their friendship, bestow their thought upon the man. May all those who are otherwise perish! Praise Indra and Agni with a song of sacrifice like that of Nabhāka.
In whose lap this entire world, this vast heaven, and this earth hold their treasures—may all the others, the insignificant ones, perish!
Sing forth sacred hymns like Nabhaka to Indra and Agni;
they who have opened the ocean with its sevenfold bottom and its downward-opening gates by their sovereign might—Indra rules through his power. May all the others, the insignificant ones, perish!
Tear it away as of old, like the tangled mass of a creeping vine; strike down the power of the Dāsa. May we share out that accumulated wealth of his with Indra; may all our enemies be destroyed.
O Indra and Agni, when these people invoke you with songs throughout their lives...

With our own men, may we overcome those who attack us; may we conquer those who seek to conquer us. May all the others perish! When the two white ones rise from heaven with their radiant beams, the rivers flow forth according to the law of Indra and Agni—those which they released from their bond. May all the others perish!
Numerous, O Indra, are your aids; numerous indeed are your praises, O Son of the Mighty One, Lord of the Bay Steeds.
May those riches of the hero come to us without fail, so that our prayers may be fulfilled.
Let all the others perish! Sharpen him with well-fashioned hymns—the fierce warrior who is worthy of praise.

And he who by his might shall shatter even the eggs of Śuṣṇa, who shall win the water-bringing waters—he, let the others, all alike, perish! Sharpen him for the well-performed sacrifice, the true hero, the one who comes at the proper time; and he who by his power shall shatter the eggs of Śuṣṇa, who shall win the water-bringing waters—he, let the others, all alike, perish!
Thus, for Indra and Agni, a newer hymn has been spoken like that of the fathers, like that of Mandhātṛ, and like that of Aṅgiras.
With your triple-layered protection, guard us; may we be masters of riches.
To this Varuṇa, for his great power, and to the Maruts, the most wise, sing forth a song of praise.
He who, like a herdsman watching over his cattle, protects the thoughts of men—let all others who are base be destroyed!

Him indeed we celebrate with a song in common, with the hymns of our ancestors, and with the praises of Nābhāka—he who dwells at the source of the rivers, he whose brotherhood consists of seven sisters, he who is the central one; let all others who are base be destroyed!
He has embraced the nights; by his creative power he has established the suns; he is visible throughout the entire world.
The three dawns have increased his power according to his law; all others, however, have perished.

He who established the peaks of the earth, he who is visible upon it—he is the measurer of the ancient station, that which belongs to Varuṇa’s herd; for he is the guardian of the secret place. All others, however, have perished.

He who is the upholder of the worlds, who knows the secret and hidden names of the dawns—he, the seer, nourishes many poetic forms like the sky; let all the others perish, even those who are near. In him all poetic insights are established as if upon a nave.

Worship Trita with swift zeal, as one would drive cattle into a pen; they have harnessed their horses for the yoking. Let all others perish! He who dwells among these, who knows all their births, and who touches all the domains of Varuṇa within his own home—all the gods follow his law. Let all others perish!
He, the secret ocean, rises up as it were to the four heavens when he has deposited the sacrificial formula (*yajus*) within these [worlds].

With his flaming foot, he has trampled the magic illusions and ascended to the firmament. May all those others who are hostile perish! He whose white, far-seeing [rays] are established over the three earths—

RV_08.041.09.2 They two have thrice measured out the higher [realms], the firm seat of Varuṇa; he rules over the seven; let all the others, the base ones, perish! RV_08.041.10.1 He who has made the white [days] his upper garment and the black [nights] his undergarment according to his laws;
RV_08.041.10.2 He has measured out the ancient abode; with a pillar he has propped apart the two worlds, as the Unborn supported the sky; let all the others, the base ones, perish!
The Asura, the all-knowing, propped up the sky; he measured out the breadth of the earth.
As sovereign lord, he took his seat over all worlds—all these are the ordinances of Varuṇa.
Thus praise the lofty Varuṇa; pay homage to the wise guardian of immortality.
May he grant us a triple-layered shelter; may Heaven and Earth protect us in their lap. O God Varuṇa, sharpen this prayer of the one who strives, and sharpen our will and skill.
May we board a well-paddled ship by which we may cross over all difficulties.
O Aśvins, the inspired singers with their prayers have caused the pressing-stones to move for you both;
O Nāsatyas, come for the drinking of the Soma! May all others perish!
Just as the sage Triśoka has repeatedly invoked you both, O Aśvins, with his songs...
O Nāsatyas, for the drinking of the Soma—let all others who are base perish!
Thus have I called you for aid, just as the wise sages have called;
O Nāsatyas, for the drinking of the Soma—let all others who are base perish!
These songs and hymns of praise rise up toward Agni, the inspired sage, the ordainer, the priest whose sacrifices are never thwarted.
To you, O Jātavedas, who are observant of all people and take delight in these offerings— [to you they rise].
O Agni, I produce a fair hymn of praise.
Indeed, O Agni, your sharp flames are like glimmers of light; with your teeth you devour the forests.
The bay steeds, smoke-bannered and wind-swift, strive toward heaven; the fires advance separately.
These very fires, kindled separately, have now become visible all at once.
Like the banners of the dawns,
the dark dust rises from the feet of Jātavedas as he advances when Agni spreads across the earth.
Making the plants his food and devouring them, Agni does not grow weary, even as he repeatedly consumes those that are young.
With his tongues he has truly bent them down; he has become ablaze with his radiance.
Agni shines in the forests; O Agni, your seat is in the waters. You cause the good plants to grow, and being in their womb, you are born again.
O Agni, that flame of yours shines forth when offered with clarified butter; it kisses the sacrificial ladles at its mouth.
[To him] who feeds on bulls and feeds on heifers, whose back is the *soma*, the ordainer.
Let us worship Agni with hymns of praise. And we, O Agni, of most excellent wisdom, invoke you with reverence and with fuel, O Hotṛ-priest.
Moreover, O pure Agni, invoked with oblations, we invoke you as did Bhṛgu, as did Manu, and as did Aṅgiras.
For you, O Agni, are a sage by means of fire, a sage by means of a sage, being yourself a true being.
As a friend, you are kindled by your friend. As such, O Agni, grant thousandfold wealth to the inspired singer who offers oblations, and grant him nourishment accompanied by heroic sons.
O Agni, brother, born of strength, with ruddy horses and pure vows,
accept this hymn of praise from me.
And you, O Agni, when praised by me, [come] like a lowing cow toward one who welcomes her.
Like cows to their stall,
they have come to you; O best of Aṅgirases, all those people dwelling in secure homes have turned themselves toward you individually, O Agni, out of desire.
The wise, the thoughtful, the inspired singers have urged Agni with their prayers and hymns to sit at the feast.
O Agni, we who perform the sacrifice urge you, the prize-winner, in our races.
They praise the bearer, the invoker.
For in many places you are the same; you are the lord over all the tribes. We invoke you in the battles.
Praise him who, when invoked and fed with clarified butter, blazes forth—
may he hear this our call. We invoke you, Jātavedas, who hears us.
O Agni, strike away our enemies.
I praise this Agni, the wonderful king of the people, the overseer of the sacred laws; may he indeed hear us.
We urge Agni, who stirs all life, like a prize-winning youth set to the race, even as we urge a steed for victory.
Slaying the obstructors, driving away our enemies, and burning up the Rākṣasas forever.
O Agni,
shine with your sharpened flame! O Agni, best of the Aṅgirases, whom the people kindle like Manu, take heed of this my word.
O Agni, whether you are born of heaven or born of the waters, O you who are strengthened by might—
we invoke you with our songs. For all these people and all well-settled communities here separately offer worship unto you.
They urge the milk-stream forward for him to consume.
O Agni, may we, through our well-directed thoughts, be those who behold men throughout all days, and may we cross over all difficulties.
We implore with our joyful hearts Agni, the delightful one, beloved by many, fierce, and possessing purifying luster.
O Agni, you who are rich in light, like the sun emitting rays, spread yourself abroad.
Boldly you strike down the darkness.
We beg of you, O powerful one, that gift of yours which never fails—
that precious wealth, O Agni, which comes from you.
Worship Agni with fuel; awaken the guest with offerings of clarified butter.
Pour the oblations into him. O Agni, take pleasure in my hymn of praise; grow strong through this prayer of mine.
Accept our hymns with favor. I place Agni at the forefront as my messenger; I address him who carries the oblations.
May he seat the gods here.
Your lofty flames, O shining Agni, rise up when you are kindled; your bright rays stream forth.
Let my ladles, dripping with clarified butter, approach you, O beloved one.
O Agni, enjoy our oblations.
I praise Agni—the delightful invoker, the officiating priest, of wondrous luster and radiant light; may he indeed hear us.
The ancient Hotṛ, worthy of praise, the beloved Agni of prophetic insight,
the glory of the sacrifices— O best of Aṅgirases, accepting these oblations in their proper sequence, ... [he has come].
O Agni, lead the sacrifice according to the seasons; O kindled one, O truthful one, O brightly shining one, bring here the divine host, you who are wise.
We implore the inspired sage, the guileless invoker, whose banner is smoke, the radiant one, the signal of sacrifices.
O Agni, protect us; O God, ward off those who would harm us.
Shatter our enemies,
O you who are born of strength! Agni, adorning his own body with an ancient hymn,
the Seer has grown mighty through the inspired singer.
I invoke Agni, the Son of Strength, whose radiance is purifying,
at this well-performed sacrifice.
O Agni, you who are great like Mitra, with your bright luster— [May you grant us favor.]
May you sit with the gods upon the sacred grass.
The mortal who serves the god Agni within his own home—
for him he shines forth wealth.
Agni is the head of heaven, the summit, the lord of this earth;
he quickens the seeds of the waters.
O Agni, your pure, bright, and radiant flames rise upward.
Your lights are flames; for you, O Agni, Lord of Heaven, rule over the gift of desirable wealth. May I be your praiser under your protection.
O Agni, the wise impel you with their thoughts;
may our songs increase you.
[O you who are] unerring, self-dependent, the messenger, and ever the singer.
We choose the friendship of Agni.
Agni is the one of the most pure vows; he is the pure sage, the pure seer. Pure, he shines when offered oblations.
And may my meditations and songs strengthen you at all times; O Agni, be mindful of our friendship.
O Agni, if I were you, or if you indeed were I...
May your blessings here be realized; for you, O Agni, are the Vasu, the lord of wealth, and the possessor of radiant light. May we abide in your benevolent favor.
O Agni, to you who are firm in your vows, our songs flow forth like rivers to the ocean, lowing like cows.
To the youthful lord of the people, the sage, the all-eater, the one of many impulses.
I adorn Agni with hymns of thought. To him,
the charioteer of sacrifices, the sharp-toothed and firm, we would offer nourishment with songs of praise— to Agni.
O Agni, let this singer be under your protection, O Truthful One; have mercy on him, O Purifier.
For he is wise, sitting at the feast like a vigilant sage.
O Agni, you shine in the sky.
O Sage Agni, before the calamities and before the oppressors,
prolong our life, O Vasu.
Truly, those who kindle Agni and spread the sacrificial grass in due order—
those whose friend is the youthful Indra— for them the fuel is great, their praise is abundant, and the sacrificial post is wide.
Those whose youthful Indra is their friend— Even without fighting, the hero drives through the encircling host with his warriors,
They whose youthful Indra is their friend.
The Vṛtra-slayer took up his bow; as soon as he was born, he questioned his mother:
"Who are the fierce ones? Who indeed are renowned?
Śavasī answered him: "The mountain shall fight against you like a swift steed."
He who has declared enmity toward you—listen to him, O Maghavan; whatever he desires, you fulfill it. Whatever you make firm, that remains firm.
When Indra, the instigator of battle, goes forth to the fray seeking good horses, he is the best of charioteers among charioteers.
O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, scatter all assailants in every direction; strike them down on all sides.
May you be our most glorious one.
May Indra place our chariot at the front for the sake of victory— a chariot which no deceivers can harm.

May we avoid your enemies; O Śakra, you are ready to give. May we go, O Indra, to one who possesses cattle. Even if we proceed slowly, O wielder of the stone, may we be possessed of horses and a hundredfold wealth.
Desiring to speak, they are free from distress.
For upward indeed do your hundreds and thousands of bountiful gifts rise day after day; you bestow them upon those who sing your praises.
For we know you, O Indra, as the winner of wealth, who breaks even what is firm,
like one who tears down a dwelling.
O Sage, may the drops exhilarate you, the preeminent one, O Bold One.
When we beg you for the niggardly Pani...
That wealthy man who, being stingy, has withheld [the gift] from us for the sake of bestowing wealth— bring to us the knowledge of him!
These Soma-offering friends of yours, O Indra, look toward you, as those seeking prosperity gaze upon their cattle.
And we call upon you, who are deafless and have ears that hear, for our protection.
From afar we call you hither;
if you would hear this invocation, then make it one that cannot be disregarded, and be our closest kinsman.
Whatever distress we have experienced while wandering, O Indra, you have surely known; therefore, be a giver of cattle to us.
O Lord of Might, we have embraced you as the aged embrace a staff for support.
We desire you in our assembly.
Sing a hymn of praise to Indra, the hero of many exploits;
no one can withstand him in battle.
O Bull, at this pressing, I pour out the pressed juice for you to drink;
satisfy yourself and enjoy the exhilaration.
Let not the foolish, greedy, nor the mockers deceive you.
Do not favor those who hate prayer.
Here, let the waters rich in milk exhilarate you for great bounty; drink like a wild buffalo at a lake.
Those ancient and new deeds which the slayer of Vṛtra has performed in the distance— proclaim them well in the assemblies.
Indra drank the pressed juice from the brown plant at the thousand-armed [sacrifice].
Therein he displayed his manly power;
that was true for Turvaśa and Yadu, as he, being conscious, made manifest what is beyond reproach.
He pervaded everything in the act of conquest.
I praise your common [deed], the savior of men, the piercer of wealth consisting of cattle—
R̥bhukṣan, who strengthened Tugra’s son amidst the hymns and is not to be turned back.
To Indra, at the pressed Soma—
him who for Triśoka cut apart the broad mountain, parting its womb, so that he might find a path for the cattle to go forth.
Whatever you intend or contemplate while exhilarated, and whatever you wish to bestow—O Lord, do not do that; have mercy!
For even a small deed committed against one such as you is heard of upon the earth.
May your mind, O Indra, come hither.
Truly yours are those fair glories and your high praises, in that you, O Indra, show us mercy.
Do not slay us for one offense, nor for two, nor even for three; O Hero, do not slay us for many.
For we are indeed afraid of one like you, O fierce one, who shatters all who oppose you.
From him, the wondrous subduer of enemies— O Lord of abundant wealth, may I not suffer the loss of a friend nor the loss of a son;
let your mind be turned back toward us.
O men, what friend indeed, unprovoked, has ever spoken thus to his friend: "Who is it that seeks to abandon us?
Thus, O bull, when the soma is pressed, you who are insatiable have turned away many [enemies].
Like a gambler moving through the depths,
I seize for you these two bay steeds yoked by our word, drawn by a well-rolling chariot, so that you may grant them to those who offer prayers.
Shatter all our enemies; strike down those who oppress us and destroy our adversaries.
Bring us that desirable wealth.
O Indra, whatever has been carried away into the stronghold, into the firm place, or into the mountain fastness—bring it back.
Then bring that desirable wealth; may all mankind know of your gift of abundance. Then bring that desirable wealth.
O Indra, Lord of abundant wealth, O leader, we belong to one such as you, the driver of the bay steeds.
For we know you, O wielder of the stone, to be the true giver of nourishment;
we know you to be the giver of riches.
O you of a hundred aids, O Śatakratu, whose greatness the poets celebrate with their songs—
that mortal indeed has a good leader whom the Maruts and Aryaman [favor].
Mitra protects those who are free from malice.
Possessing wealth in cattle and horses, along with great heroic power, he, impelled by the Ādityas, prospers; he is ever enriched with much-desired riches.
We beg that Indra for his bounty—the powerful one, the fearless;
we beg him, the lord of wealth.
For in him are all protections and all fearlessnesses found together.
Let the bay steeds, the possessors of much wealth, bring him hither—the pressed juice—for exhilaration.
That exhilaration of yours which is most excellent, O Indra, which is the greatest slayer of Vṛtra; which wins the light with heroes, and which is invincible in battles.
He who is invincible, O possessor of all boons, who is worthy of renown and the conqueror in battles—O most powerful Vasu, come to our libations; may we reach a stall filled with cattle.
As of old, grant us wealth in cattle, in horses, and in chariots.
O Most Magnificent One, grant us wide space!
For, O Hero, I find no end to your bounty; indeed, you have always bestowed it upon us.
O Maghavan, wielder of the stone, favor our prayers even now; with your strengths, you have protected us.
He who is lofty, the friend who makes [all] heard, he, praised by many, knows all generations.
All human generations, with uplifted ladles, invoke that powerful Indra.
May he, the possessor of much wealth, the slayer of Vṛtra, the liberal lord, stand before us as our protector in the battles for booty.
Sing with song to your hero during the exhilarations of the soma-juice—to the one of great wisdom, to Indra by name, the famous and powerful, just as the word [describes him].
He has bestowed wealth upon his own person; he has given riches; O much-invoked one, he has given a prize-winning steed in the contests for booty.
Now indeed,
he who rules over all treasures, even as he who is victorious through his wondrous form—
now indeed, he pities us.
We praise you greatly for your great bounty—for the one who comes readily, who goes forth, and who moves swiftly.
With sacrifices and songs, you worship the Maruts, who are followed by all men; let him sing to you with reverence and song.
They who cause [the clouds] to fall with their courses upon the ridges of the mountains—of them [I sing].

The sacrifice of those who roar loudly, the favor of those who roar with great might—at the rite, O Indra, bring us the breaking force of the evil-minded. O most powerful one, impelling our thought, bring us wealth that is worthy of alliance; impelling our thought, bring us the highest [wealth].
O winner, O excellent winner, O fierce one, O wonderful and most wise one, O giver of true joy!
O sovereign ruler, by thy might, [bring] the victorious Bhujyu, the subduer, the foremost in battles.
May he come who, as a god, has accepted such a gift and taken possession of the fulfillment.
Just as Vaśa Aśvya took [the cattle] at the dawning of this [night] for Pṛthuśravas Kānīta—
sixty thousand of the horse-herds, ten thousand seated in the wagon, twenty hundred camels,
ten hundred dark-brown mares, ten hundred ruddy ones, and ten thousand cows.
Ten dark-brown steeds, winners of wealth, swift and eager for the prize,
have turned the felly downward with their speed.
These are the gifts of Pr̥thuśravas, the son of Kānīta, who is bountiful in his generosity.
Giving a golden chariot, the most generous patron has become preeminent; he has achieved the highest renown.
O Vāyu, come to us for our great expansion, for the sacrifice, and for splendor!
For we have performed much for you to give, indeed, so that you may grant us great bounty this very day.
He who travels with horses at dawn, thrice seven times seventy [steeds]—
for him, O Soma-drinkers, pure and drinkers of the purified, come with these Soma-pressing Soma-offerers for the sake of giving.
He who himself has gladdened me here, the wonderful one, for the sake of bestowing gifts.
Against Araṭva Akṣa and Huṣa, who perform good deeds, [Indra], the one of excellent wisdom, acts as the doer of even better deeds.

He who is the self-ruler over the wondrous and praiseworthy, O Vāyu, you who are bathed in ghee—this very thing has now been sent forth, impelled by horses, impelled by dust, and impelled by dogs. This indeed is it.
Then, for the impetuous one, sixty thousand dear [gifts] were brought;
they came like a herd of stallions, like a herd of cattle— my stallions have come to me.
And when he bellowed for a hundred camels in the troop of Caratha;
and twenty hundred among the Śvitnas; a hundred the seer Tarukṣa received from the Dāsa Balbūtha.
These people here, O Vāyu, rejoice in thee; protected by Indra they rejoice, protected by the gods.
And now this great woman, turning toward Vaśa Aśvya, is led forth adorned with golden ornaments.

Great is the help of you, the great ones, O Varuṇa and Mitra, for the donor. O Ādityas, whomsoever you protect from malice, no misfortune shall reach him; for yours are the unerring aids, yours are the well-bestowing aids. O gods, O Ādityas, you know how to drive away all evils.
Like birds spreading their wings above, grant us protection; your aids are unfailing, your aids are well-bestowed.
Spread out that protection for us, as birds extend their wings;
O possessors of all wealth, we meditate upon all your secure shelters; your aids are unfailing, your aids are well-bestowed.
To whomsoever the wise ones have granted a dwelling and a means of life—O Ādityas, we truly know that you rule over all the wealth of Manu; unerring are your aids, well-aiding are your aids.
May they carry us around, avoiding evils as chariot-drivers avoid difficult paths.
May we abide in the protection of Indra and under the shelter of the Ādityas. Your aids are unfailing; your aids are well-aiding.
The person who is deprived of what has been given by you suffers in distress.
O Gods, O Ādityas, that which you have bestowed upon us is abundant. Your aids are unfailing; your aids are well-aiding.
Neither fierce abandonment nor heavy weight shall strike him down, O Ādityas, for whom you have granted far-reaching protection; for yours are the faultless aids, yours are the well-aiding aids.
O Gods, we belong to you, like warriors beneath their armor.
May you deliver us from great sin; may you deliver us from small. Yours are the aids that are free from harm; yours are the aids that are well-bestowing.
May Aditi deliver us; may Aditi grant us protection.
She is the mother of wealthy Mitra, of Aryaman, and of Varuṇa. Yours are the aids that are free from harm; yours are the aids that are well-bestowing.
O Gods, that shelter which is a refuge, that which is auspicious and free from disease, that triple-layered protection—grant all that to us! Your aids are unfailing; your aids are well-bestowed.
O Ādityas, look down upon us, as a spy looks over the riverbanks!
RV_08.047.11.2 As one leads a horse to a good ford, so lead us along a pleasant path; for yours are the aids that are free from danger, yours are the well-aiding aids.
RV_08.047.12.1 Here there is no blessing for the one who possesses demons, nor for the one who seeks to harm; nor even for the one who approaches with malice.
RV_08.047.12.2 But there is blessing for the cow and for the milch-cow, and for the hero who strives for glory; for yours are the aids that are free from danger, yours are the well-aiding aids.
O Gods, whatever evil deed there is, whether it be manifest or hidden—O Trita Āptya, place all that far away from us! Your aids are free from harm; your aids are truly effective.
And whatever ill dream is among our cattle, or whatever [evil] is in us, O Daughter of Heaven...
To Trita Āptya, carry that away at dawn; for yours are the aids that fail not, your aids are truly effective.
Whether she makes herself a golden ornament or a garland, O Daughter of Heaven—to Trita Āptya we entrust all evil dreaming; for yours are the aids that fail not, your aids are truly effective.
To Trita who has approached that food, that work, and that portion— and to Dvita, carry away the evil dream! Swift are your aids; well-aiding are your aids!
Just as we pay back a sixteenth part, just as an eighth, so do we pay back the debt.
RV_08.047.17.2 Thus we transfer all evil dreaming to Āptya; unerring are your aids, truly effective are your aids.
RV_08.047.18.1 We have conquered today, we have attained [our goal], and we have become sinless.
O Uṣas, may that evil dream from which we were afraid depart; unerring are your aids, truly effective are your aids.
I, the wise one, have partaken of the sweet food of the bird, the well-praised [soma] that finds widest space.
It is that which all the gods and mortals approach, calling it honey. And you shall go within as Aditi, the warder-off of divine wrath.
O Indu, enjoying the friendship of Indra, may you carry us toward riches like a draft-animal pulling at the yoke.
We have drunk the Soma, we have become immortal; we have reached the light, we have found the gods.
What can hostility now do to us? And what, O Immortal One, can the malice of a mortal do?
Be gracious to our heart when drunk, O Indu; O Soma, be as kind as a father to his son. Like a friend to a friend, O wise one of wide renown, prolong our life that we may live, O Soma.
These glorious, space-expanding draughts, once drunk, have bound me together at my joints, as straps bind a chariot.
May they protect me from the slipping of my conduct, and may the drops preserve me from lameness.
Like fire churned forth, kindle me; grant us vision and make us more prosperous.
For then, O Soma, in your exhilaration, I consider myself like a wealthy man; go forth toward nourishment.
With an eager mind, may we partake of your pressed juice, as if it were ancestral wealth. O King Soma, prolong our lives, as the sun lengthens the days.
O King Soma, be gracious unto us for our well-being; we are your devotees—know this.
Indu, our skill and our wrath are stirred; do not surrender us to the will of the enemy.
For you, O Soma, are the guardian of our bodies; as one who beholds men, you have settled within every limb.
If we should violate your sacred laws, O benevolent friend, be gracious to us for our welfare.
May I be united with the friend whose heart is soft, so that he, O Lord of the Bay Horses, being drunk, may not harm me.
This Soma which has been placed within us—for its sake, O Indra, I lengthen my life.
Those ailments have departed, the diseases have vanished; the female spirits of darkness have fled away.
Soma, the far-reaching one, has mounted upon us; we have gone to where they prolong our life.
O Fathers, that drop (*indu*), the immortal, which, when drunk, has entered into the hearts of us mortals— To that Soma let us do worship with an oblation; may we abide in his grace and mercy.
O Soma, you who are in harmony with the Fathers have spread yourself across heaven and earth. To you, O Indu, we pay worship with this oblation; may we be masters of riches.
O protecting gods, speak for us! Let neither sleep nor idle chatter hold power over us.
May we, ever dear to Soma, with heroic sons, promote the assembly.
O Soma, you are the bestower of vital strength upon us from every side; you, the beholder of men, have found the light through the people.
O Indu, being of one mind with us, protect us with your aids from behind and also from the front.
Sing forth to Indra, the bestower of great wealth, according to his known nature—he, the Maghavan rich in many treasures, who bestows gifts upon his singers as if by the thousands.
Like one with a hundred hosts, he advances boldly; he slays the Vṛtras for the sake of the donor.
Like streams from a mountain, the gifts of him who nourishes many have overflowed.
O Indra, lover of songs, may the pressed drops, the exhilarating juices, fill you for the sake of bounty—
just as waters fill a lake that must be praised, O hero, wielder of the thunderbolt.
Drink this most sweet draught of honey, which is faultless, furthering, and eloquent.
When you have drunk it and are exhilarated, scatter gifts upon us of your own accord, boldly as if toward small game.
Run toward our hymn of praise, like a horse urged on by its drivers.
O Indra, the milch-cows provide the sacrificial food for you; among the Kaṇvas, the gifts flow forth.

Like a fierce hero, we have approached you with reverence—you, the pervasive one whose wealth is inexhaustible. Like water poured from a vessel, O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, our prayers flow toward you, O Indra.
Whether it be now, or at the sacrifice, or upon the earth—

come from there to our sacrifice with your swift steeds, O great and fierce one, with your fierce ones! Those agile bay horses of yours, which are fleet and impetuous like the winds— [with them come].
With those [powers] by which you encompass the offspring of Manu, and with those by which you behold the entire world of light—
for so much of this, O Indra, we implore you, for the sake of your favor consisting of cattle—
just as you, O Maghavan, protected Medhyātithi and Nīpātithi in the struggle for wealth.
As you were for Kaṇva, O Maghavan, for Trasadasyu, as for Paktha Daśavraja, as for Gośarya Ṛjiśvan— you were present— so, O Indra, grant us wealth in cattle and gold.
Sing forth for our aid to the far-famed Śakra, the bestower of excellent gifts.
He who bestows desirable wealth upon the one who presses the Soma and praises him, as if with a thousandfold gift.
The hundred-pointed missiles of this Indra are invincible; his great impetuous powers are mighty.
Like a mountain, he overflows for the sake of the bounteous patrons when the pressed juices have exhilarated him.
When the pressed drops have exhilarated him for his beloved [soma],
my libation has been set down like waters, O Vasu, like milch-cows for the donor. For you,
the peerless one who is invoked for aid, the thoughts flow forth like honey.
O Vasu, the Soma drops, calling upon you, have been set before your praises.
To our Soma, O performer of the fair sacrifice, he hastens like a racing steed.
O giver of sweetness, those songs of praise which are sweet to you—you find pleasure in the invocation of the Paura.
Forward [I call] the fierce hero, the discerning one, the winner of wealth, the lord of great bounty.
O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, like a well that overflows with water, you ever cause the giver to swell with riches through your possession of treasures.
Whether it be now in the far distance, or upon the earth, or in heaven—
Yoking thy bay steeds, O Indra, the Great One, come hither with thy lofty ones, O Lofty One.
Thy bay steeds, the chariot-borne and tireless, surpass even the wind in their vigor.
With them thou didst strike down the Dasyu from the men, and with them thou encompassest the sun.
O Vasu, O Hero, may we know you as such a one in your newest form,

just as you protected Etaśa in the decisive contest for wealth, and as you protected Vaśa at Daśavraja; just as you did, O Maghavan, for Kaṇva at the sacrifice and the rite, and for Dīrghanītha in his home.
O wielder of the stone, as you desired to win the prize of cattle at Gośarya, so grant me the wealth of the herd, resplendent with gold.
As you, O Indra, drank the pressed soma with Manu Sāṃvaraṇi, so drink it now.
O Maghavan, together with Nīpātithi, Medhyātithi, Puṣṭigu, and Śruṣṭigu.
Pārṣadvāṇa restored Praskaṇva, who was worn out and lying cast away;
protected by you, the seer sought to win thousands of cattle from the Dasyu Vṛka.
He who does not fail before hymns, the wise one who impels the seers—
Speak toward that Indra with a newest hymn, as one who desires to overcome for the sake of enjoyment. He to whom they have chanted the seven-headed, three-layered hymn in the highest station—
he, having roared through all these worlds, brought forth manly power from the beginning.
We invoke that Indra who is the giver of riches to us;
for we know his most recent favor, may we go to a stall filled with cattle.
O Vasu, he to whom you grant gifts attains the increase of wealth.
We, having pressed the soma, call upon you, O Maghavan Indra, lover of songs.
Never are you barren, O Indra; you never fail the one who offers oblations.
Ever more and more, O Maghavan, is your divine bounty increased.
He who has reached out with his might against Krivi, striking down Śuṣṇa with his weapons;
when he propped up and spread out that heaven, the earthly one was born from the beginning.
He whose every Aryan and Dāsa is a servant guarding his treasure, a subduer.
Even from the noble Ruśama Parīru, that wealth is being driven toward you.
The inspired singers have quickly sung their hymn, dripping with clarity and flowing with sweetness.
For us, wealth and manly strength have spread abroad; for us, the pressed drops of Soma flow.
Just as you drank the pressed Soma, O Śakra, at the sacrifice of Manu Vivasvat;
Just as you took pleasure in the hymn at Trita’s rite, O Indra, and rejoiced together with Āyu;
At the pressing by Pṛṣadhra, Medhya, and Mātariśvan, O Indra, you were exhilarated.
As [you drank] the Soma, O Daśaśipra, Daśoṇya, Syūmaraśmi, and Ṛjūnas;
he who established the hymns as his own, who boldly drank the Soma,
for whom Viṣṇu strode out three steps according to the ordinances of Mitra.

O Indra, Lord of a hundred powers, you who take pleasure in our hymns and in the prize-winning contest for booty—such as you are, we, seeking glory, call upon you as milkers call a cow that yields abundance.
He who is our giver is our father; he is the great one, the gracious lord who exercises sovereign power.
Coming hither, may the fierce Maghavan, possessor of many treasures, grant us cattle and horses.
O Vasu, he for whom you provide wealth to give away prospers with the increase of riches.
Seeking wealth, we invoke Indra, the lord of wealth and the lord of a hundred powers, with our hymns of praise.
Never do you neglect; you protect both races of beings. O Āditya, your fourth invocation is your Indra-power; your immortality is established in heaven.
For whichever worshipper you, O bounteous Indra, lover of songs, grant your aid—O Helper, you grant it to him.

O Vasu, hear our songs and our fair praise; hear our invocation like that of Kaṇva. The ancient hymn has been recited; speak the sacred prayer to Indra. Many lofty verses of Truth have been sung aloud; the inspirations of the singer have been released.
Indra has shaken together vast riches, together the two worlds, and together the sun.
Together the bright, pure Soma juices, mixed with milk, have exhilarated Indra.
You, the highest among the wealthy patrons and the eldest among the bulls.
O Maghavan Indra, we seek you, the best breaker of forts, the winner of cattle, the lord of wealth— you who,
growing stronger day by day, did violence to Āyu, Kutsa, and Atithigva; as such, we, seeking booty, invoke you, the lord of bay steeds, the possessor of a hundred powers.
May all the mountains pour out for us the essence of the honeyed juice—those drops which are pressed among the people in distant lands and those which are pressed nearby.
Slay all our enemies and drive them away; let all win wealth.
Even among the remnants, the exhilarating stalks are yours, where you satisfy yourself with Soma.
O Indra, come nearer with your aids that bring well-disposed wisdom;
come, O most auspicious one, with your most auspicious protections, O most gracious one, with your most gracious succors.
Make him a conqueror, a true lord, one who observes all people, and grant him a share among the progeny.
Further those who, uttering hymns of praise, purify their will according to your power. May we be yours, those who are most effective for your aid, in the battles for you.
Through our priestly offices and invocations of the gods, we consider ourselves as having won the prize.
For I, O Lord of the Bay Steeds, seeking strength, ever go to the contest with my prayers and your protections;
for you alone, O most divine one, do I seek at the head of the churners, yearning for horses and kine.
O Indra, the poets celebrate this heroic power of yours with their songs;
chanting aloud, they have increased their strength, dripping with clarity, as the Pauras have approached you with their prayers.
Those who, through their good deeds, approach Indra for protection, in whose pressed juices you take delight—[for them you are the helper].
As you were exhilarated at Saṃvarta, as you were at Kṛśa, so, O Indra, be exhilarated with us.
O all you gods, being of one accord, come hither unto us. May the Vasus and Rudras come to us for our protection; may the Maruts hear our call.
May Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī, and the seven rivers protect my invocation. May the waters, the wind, the mountains, the lord of the forest, and the earth hear my call.
O Indra, most bountiful one, whatever wealth you possess as a liberal giver—
Through him, be our companion at the feast for our prosperity; O Vṛtra-slayer, O Bhaga, come for the sake of giving.
O Lord of the field, O Lord of men, you indeed, O wise one, bring us strength.
Having won through the invocations of the Hotṛ-priests and the feasts of the gods, they have become renowned far and wide.
O Indra, the Aryas possess blessings and the life-span of men;
come to us, O Maghavan, for our protection, and milk forth swelling nourishment for us.
O Indra, may we honor you with hymns of praise; you, O Śatakratu, belong to us.
Bestow upon Praskaṇva a great, solid, enduring, and modest gift that is beyond reproach.
The many heroic deeds of Indra have been revealed as he approaches;
O Dasyave-vṛka, this is your gift.
A hundred white bulls shine like stars in the sky;
by their greatness, they have propped up the heavens as if with pillars.
A hundred bamboos, a hundred dogs, and a hundred tanned skins.
A hundred are my *balbaja*-grass tufts; four hundred are the ruddy ones.
O descendants of Kaṇva, you are well-disposed toward the gods; moving about at every stage of life, do not falter like horses.
From the very beginning they have celebrated the great glory of the sevenfold, the perfect one;
the dark mare, rushing along the paths, cannot be overtaken even by the eye.
O Dasyave-vṛka, your gift has appeared, which inspires no shame.
His power is as vast as the sky in its breadth.
Dasyave-vṛka, the son of Pūtakratu, bestowed ten thousand [cows] upon me from his own wealth.
A hundred donkeys for me, a hundred woolly ewes,
a hundred slaves, and even garlands;
there too, it was clearly brought forth for Pūtakratā.
Like a stallion of the herd, Agni has been perceived; he is the wise bearer of oblations, he whose chariot brings prosperity.
Agni, with his bright radiance, has shone forth loftily like the Sun; the Sun has shone in heaven.
O Gods, joined with your ancient wisdom and your powerful chariot, O worshipful ones, come hither with your mighty powers, O Nāsatyas; drink this third libation.
The thirty-three gods, the truthful ones, have beheld you, the two truthful ones, standing before the Truth.
Rejoicing in our sacrifice and our libation, O Aśvins, you whose fire is radiant, drink the Soma!
O Aśvins, that deed of yours is worthy of praise: the bull [of the sacrifice] belongs to heaven, the mid-air, and the earth.
Come to all those thousand praises uttered in the quest for cattle, so that you may drink.
This portion has been set out for you two, O worshipful ones; come hither to these songs, O Nāsatyas!
Drink the honeyed Soma among us, and protect the donor with your powers.
Him whom the officiating priests, acting in harmony and arranging him in many ways, bring as this sacrifice.
When a learned Brāhmaṇa is engaged in the rite, what indeed is the shared understanding of the sacrificer therein?
