Agni is but one, though kindled in many ways; the Sun is one, pervading all things.
The Dawn is but one, yet she illumines this entire world; indeed, this whole universe has become one.

The luminous, ensign-bearing, triple-wheeled chariot, easy to mount and providing many boons—him whose yoking brought forth the goddesses of wondrous wealth, him I invoke for you both to drink the empty [vessel]. These portions of yours flow forth, O Indra and Varuṇa; at the libations, we call upon you both for the sake of greatness.
At every sacrifice you hasten to the libations, when you bestow your aid upon the sacrificer who presses the Soma.
The obstructing plants and waters stood still; O Indra and Varuṇa, they attained your greatness.
Those two who have sped across the path on the far side of the firmament—no enemy at all dares to challenge them.

O Indra and Varuṇa, that is true: for you, the seven voices of Kr̥śa milk forth a wave of sweetness. With those [voices], O Lords of Splendor, protect the donor who guards you unharmed with his thoughts.
Dropping ghee, Soma-like, quick-giving, the seven sisters [dwell] in the seat of Order.
O Indra and Varuṇa, with those [streams] of yours that drip with clarity, bestow them upon the sacrificer and grant him aid.
For great good fortune, we have proclaimed the true majesty and Indra-like power belonging to those two radiant ones.
O Indra and Varuṇa, lords of splendor, protect us who drip with clarity by means of the three sevens.
O Indra and Varuṇa, when in the beginning you bestowed upon the seers inspired thought, the wisdom of speech, and sacred revelation; when the wise,
performing the sacrifice, beheld through fervor those stations which they created— O Indra and Varuṇa, bestow upon the sacrificers a state of graciousness free from pride and an abundance of wealth.
Bestow upon us progeny, nourishment, and prosperity; prolong our life for the sake of long-lived existence.
O Agni, come hither with the fires; we choose you as the Hotṛ-priest.
Let the extended ladle, filled with oblation, anoint you, the most excellent sacrificer, so that you may sit upon the sacrificial grass.
For toward you, O Aṅgiras, Son of Strength, the ladles move at the sacrifice. We pray to Agni, the Son of Vigor, whose hair is ghee—the foremost in sacrifices.
O Agni, you are a seer, a disposer, a purifying Hotṛ worthy of worship.
Pleasant, most worthy of sacrifice at the rites, to be praised by the inspired singers with pure hymns—O radiant one!
O most youthful one, bring here the guileless gods for the feast of the desiring [worshipper], you who are eternal.
O Vasu, come toward the well-prepared offerings; rejoice, being well-disposed through our prayers.
O Agni, you alone are far-extending, O protector, O seer of Truth; the inspired poets, O kindled and radiant one, seek to win you over, they who are the ordainers.
Shine forth, O most brilliant one; beam out for the people, grant joy to the singer—for you are great.
May the wise patrons, who overcome enemies and maintain the sacred fires, be under the protection of the gods for me. O Agni, just as you consume upon the earth even one whose mind is grown arrogant,
so do you burn him who seeks to harm us, the ill-minded one, O god of great luster.
Do not deliver us over to the mortal enemy, nor to the sorcerer, nor to the one who utters evil speech.
O most youthful one, protect us with your tireless, crossing, and auspicious guardians.
Protect us, O Agni, with your first [form], and protect us also with your second.
Protect us with your three songs, O Lord of Strength; protect us with your four, O Vasu.
Protect us from every malicious demon; grant us aid in the contests for booty.
For we approach you alone as our closest kinsman for the service of the gods, that we may prosper.

O Agni, O Purifier, grant us wealth that increases our vigor and is worthy of praise; and bestow upon us, O Supreme Lord, that which is much-desired through your excellent guidance and most glorious self-splendor—
by means of which we may overcome the defiant in battle, crossing over the threats of the enemy.
As such, O Lord of Might, increase us with your nourishment; quicken our thoughts that find wealth.
Like a sharpening bull brandishing his horns, Agni’s flames are keen;
they are not to be defied, for he, the son of strength, has powerful jaws.
For your jaws, O Bull Agni, cannot be withstood when you spread yourself abroad.
As our Hotṛ-priest, make our oblation well-offered; win for us many desirable things.
You lie within the woods; mortals kindle you from your two mothers.

Unwearied, you carry the oblations of the preparer of the sacrifice; from then on, you reign among the gods. The seven priests laud you, O Agni, the one who is easy to invoke and free from guile. You cleave the rock with your heat and your flame; O Agni, stand forth above all people.
We who have trimmed the sacred grass invoke Agni after Agni, the unrestrained one;
we whose offerings are prepared call upon Agni, the Hotṛ of all peoples, throughout the eternal ages.
O Agni, he who is wise attends to you with his thought for protection, providing a secure dwelling.
With your impelling power, bring us wealth in many forms, most near for our protection.
O Agni, singer, lord of the people, you who burn away the demons— O God, you are the great master of the house who never departs, the guardian of heaven, dwelling in the home.
Let not the destructive spirit enter us, O Lord of glowing wealth; let not the sorcery of those who practice sorcery reach us.
Drive away hunger beyond the cattle-pasture, O Agni, and repel the demonic spirits.
May Indra hear both [our prayers] and this our speech from afar.
May the most powerful Maghavan come with his constant favor, through our prayer, to drink the Soma.
For the two worlds have fashioned him as the self-ruling bull for the sake of strength. Moreover, you sit as the first among those who are supreme, for your mind is set upon the Soma.
O Indra, Lord of many riches, pour forth [the draught] of the pressed soma-juice!
For we know you, O Lord of the bay horses, as the conqueror in battles, the one who daunts even the undaunted.
O Maghavan of unfailing truth, let this be so according to your will, O Indra, by your power of mind.
May we win booty through your favor, O fair-cheeked one, as we hasten swiftly toward you, O wielder of the stone.
Be gracious to us, O Lord of Power, Indra, with all your aids.
For we follow you, O Hero, like Bhaga—the glorious finder of wealth.
The leader of the horse, the performer of many deeds for the cattle, is a golden fountain, O God.
For no one can diminish the gift in you; whatever I ask of you, bring that here.
Come indeed to the singer and find fortune for the sake of bestowing wealth.
Pour forth, O Maghavan, for the sake of winning cattle; pour forth, O Indra, for the sake of winning horses.
You bestow upon us as a gift many thousands and hundreds of herds.
We have brought hither Indra, the shatterer of forts, with our inspired words, singing for his protection.
Whether it be a non-sage or a sage who has fashioned this speech for you, O Indra—let him gladden you with his devotion, O Lord of a hundred powers; may he, O impetuous one, be free from harm.
May the fierce-armed Purandara, the crusher of foes, hear my call.
Seeking wealth, we invoke Indra, the lord of wealth and possessor of a hundred powers, with our hymns of praise.
We do not consider ourselves sinners, nor are we indolent, nor are we dull-witted;
for if only we could make the bull Indra our companion at the pressed soma.
We have harnessed the fierce one, the conqueror in battles, the debt-claimer, the invincible. He knows even the most zealous [foe]; as the best of charioteers, he wins the prize when he reaches it.
O Indra, from whatever we fear, from that grant us security.
O Maghavan, may that power of yours be effective for us through your aids; strike away our enemies and our adversaries.
For you, O Lord of Wealth, are the master of great bounty for the one who serves you;
as such, O Maghavan Indra, lover of songs, we, having pressed the soma, call upon you.
O Indra, you are the one to be praised, the slayer of Vṛtra, our supreme protector;
may he guard our last [rank], may he guard our middle, and may he protect us from behind and from the front.
O Indra, do thou protect us from behind, from below, from above, and from the front—from every side.
Keep divine fear far from us; keep the godless weapons far away.
O Indra, protect us today and today, tomorrow and tomorrow, and in the future as well.
And you, Lord of the Good, shall guard all our singers by day and by night throughout the days.
The breaker-down, the hero, Maghavan, the possessor of abundant wealth, is united for the sake of heroic power.
O Śatakratu, both your arms are virile, which have grasped the thunderbolt.
Bring forth a hymn of praise to him, that which he shall delight in.
With hymns, the Soma-pressers increase Indra’s majestic vigor; auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
Unyoked, peerless among men, alone he has driven forth the peoples; he has grown far beyond all created beings by his might. Auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
Even with a steed that is not yet harnessed, the giver of quickening gifts desires to win;
Indra, that deed of yours is to be proclaimed as you perform your heroic exploits—blessed are the gifts of Indra.
Come hither, O Indra, so that we may offer to you the sacred prayers that increase your strength.
O most powerful one, with those [gifts] for which you take pleasure, prosperity is brought here to the seeker of glory; auspicious indeed are Indra’s gifts.
O Indra, when you, being bold yourself, make the mind of even the bold man bold, as he honors you with strong Soma juices and waits upon you with prostrations—auspicious indeed are Indra’s gifts.
The one who desires the hymns looks down like a man upon the waters;
having taken pleasure in the Soma-presser’s skill, he makes him his friend and ally—blessed are Indra’s gifts!
O Indra, all the gods have yielded to your heroic power and your will.
O much-praised one, you have become the lord of the universe; auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
I praise that supreme power of yours, O Indra, for the assembly of the gods, when you slay Vṛtra with your might, O Lord of Might; auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
As if making human generations appear beautiful as one, Indra—famed for this—has attained that consciousness; indeed, the gifts of Indra are auspicious.
O Indra, your might has been raised up, and so too have you and your wisdom.
O possessor of much wealth, they have increased greatly under your protection, O Maghavan; auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
O slayer of Vṛtra, both I and you shall join together for the sake of winning booty. Even the ill-disposed, O wielder of the stone, will acknowledge us, O Hero; auspicious are the gifts of Indra.

Truly, we shall praise that Indra with truth and not with falsehood. Great is the destruction for the one who does not press the soma; abundant light belongs to the one who presses it. Blessed are the gifts of Indra.
He, the ancient one, the seer among the great, has been anointed by sacred rites.
Through whose doors Manu’s father anointed the prayers among the gods;
like the measure of heaven is their seat, the stones that bear the Soma on their backs;
there, the hymns and the sacred formulations are to be recited.
Knowing this, Indra opened up the cattle for the Aṅgirases;
I praise that manly deed of his.
Like of old, he is the increaser of the seers, Indra, the carrier of the word.
May the auspicious one, who is worthy of praise at the oblation, come to us for our protection.
Now, O sacrificers, according to your will, [offer] the Svāhā-call to the desirable one.
The singers have sung their strengthening hymns for Indra, so that he may grant the wealth of the herd.
In Indra are all heroic deeds, both those already accomplished and those yet to be done— he whom the *ṛks* know as the sacrifice,
when the shouts of the five tribes have been released toward Indra.
By his own power he has spread out the inspired hymns; he is the lord of the noble man’s thought. This is your praise; you have performed these heroic deeds;
you have furthered the path of the wheel.
At the libation of this bull, he has strode out widely for us to live;
he has taken [us] as cattle take barley.
Receiving that, seeking aid, we—whose father is Dakṣa—[are sustained] by you.
May we be for the strengthening of the Lord of the Maruts.
O Hero, with our hymns we praise you, who abide in the eternal law at the appointed time;
with you as our ally, O Indra, may we be victorious.
RV 8.63.12: May the Rudras, the liberal ones, and the mountains be united with us in the slaying of Vṛtra when the call is raised for booty.
May the gods, with Indra as their chief, protect us—those who have been established as a firm support for him who recites and praises.
RV 8.64.1: May the hymns of praise gladden you; bestow bounty, O wielder of the stone!
Strike down those who hate sacred prayer;
trample with your foot the stingy Paṇis. You are great;
indeed, no one can withstand you.
You, O Indra, rule over the pressed juices; you, Indra, rule over the unpressed.
You are the king of the people.
Come hither! Depart! You are the dwelling place of the divine roar of the peoples.
You fill both the worlds, heaven and earth.
Even that mountain, the peak with its hundreds and thousands [of treasures],
you shattered for the sake of your worshippers.
We call upon you by day at the pressing, and we call upon you by night;
fulfill our desire. Where is that bull, the youth, with his powerful neck, who is unbowed?
Which priest honors him?
To whose libation does the bull come, having taken pleasure in it? Who indeed has longed for Indra?
Whom have thy gifts reached, O Vṛtra-slayer? Whom thy great heroic powers?
And who indeed is most near to thee at our hymn of praise?
This Soma is pressed for thee among the human folk, among the Pūrus.
Come hither; run forth and drink! This [Soma] of yours is dear at Śaryaṇāvat, at Suṣomā, and most intoxicating at Ārjīkīya.
Him, the lovely one, for great bounty and for exhilarating joy, for the impetuous one—
come here, O Indra, run hither, and drink! O Indra, when you are invoked by men from the east, from the west, from above, or from below, [come to us].
Come quickly with your swift steeds!
Whether you delight yourself at the flowing spring of heaven, O Svarṇara,
or in the ocean of the soma-juice.
I call upon you, the great and vast one, with songs of praise, as one calls a cow for nourishment,
O Indra, so that you may drink the soma.
O Indra, O God, your horses bring forth your majesty and your greatness.
Let them carry you on the chariot, bearing you along.
O Indra, you who are praised and extolled as the great one who acts with favor and exercises lordship— come and drink our pressed soma.
We, possessing pressed juices and offering oblations, invoke you so that you may sit upon this sacred grass of ours.
For indeed, O Indra, you are the common lord of all people throughout eternity.
As such, we invoke you.
The men have pressed this Soma-mead for you with the stones;
O Indra, being pleased, drink it.
O Viśvānara, you who are wise, look beyond and come to us; bestow upon us great renown.
The King has granted me spotted deer adorned with gold.
O gods, may the liberal patron not come to harm.
From the thousand spotted deer, I have received a great, broad, bright,
and shining piece of gold.
The grandsons of Durgaha, who are most bountiful, have by their thousandfold gifts established a glorious fame among the gods.
With your aids, O you who find wealth, we implore Indra with earnest prayers for our protection.
Singing the great hymn at the sacrifice where the soma is pressed, I call upon him as a craftsman calls for his wage.
Him whom the fierce ones do not restrain, nor the firm destroyers—him who is well-guided by the exhilarating draught in his rapture.
He who, taking heed, bestows upon the one who exerts himself and presses the juice, a praiseworthy gift for the singer.
Whether it be Śakra, the one who cleanses the horses, or the golden Kīja, he, Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, stirs open the enclosure of the stall of cattle.
He who scatters even that which is buried and heaped up by many as wealth for the donor.
May Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt with beautiful jaws and bay horses, act according to his will as he desires.
O much-praised hero, whatever you have favored among men even in the past, that very thing, O Indra, we now bring together for you: the sacrifice, the hymn of praise, and the swift word.
O much-invoked wielder of the thunderbolt, drinker of the celestial soma, come with the soma-juices for exhilaration, O heavenly lord of the soma-drinkers!
For you indeed are the most generous giver of desirable wealth to the one who prepares the sacred prayer and presses the juice.
We have truly satiated this wielder of the thunderbolt here even yesterday.
Therefore, bring today the pressed juice to him in equal measure; now indeed, attend upon the famous one.
Even the wolf, the wild beast that crushes sheep, attends to his ordinances.
So, O Indra, having taken pleasure in this our hymn of praise, come hither with wondrous thought.
What manly deed of this Indra remains yet unaccomplished?
By what glorious fame has the slayer of Vṛtra not already become renowned from his very birth? What indeed are his great, unassailable powers? And what is invincible in the Vṛtra-slayer?
Indra [overcame] all the Bekanāṭas, visible by day, and he surpassed the Paṇis in wisdom.
O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, much-invoked wielder of the thunderbolt, we indeed bring to you these most numerous, unprecedented prayers of ours, as one brings a tribute.
For many indeed are the desires for aid that call upon you, O Indra of mighty deeds; even past the offerings of the enemy, O Vasu, come hither, O most powerful one, and hear my invocation.
We, the sages, truly belong to you alone, O Indra.
For there is no one other than you, O Much-invoked Maghavan, who is a comforter.
You alone deliver us from this lack of understanding, from hunger, and from reproach.
As your helper, with your wondrous wisdom, O Most Mighty One, grant us aid, for you are the finder of the path.
RV 8.66.15: Let this Soma be pressed for you; O Kaliyas, do not be afraid. He here is fleeing from the destroyer; he shall surely flee away by himself.
RV 8.67.1: Now we pray to those Kṣatriyas, the Ādityas, for protection.
For our protection, may they who are most gracious come to our aid; may Mitra, Varuṇa, and Aryaman carry us across every distress, as the Ādityas know best how to do.
For theirs is a wondrous, praiseworthy protection for the donor,
when they have honored the Ādityas. Great is the aid of you, the great ones— O Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman.
We choose for ourselves those protections; O Ādityas, preserve us alive before the blow of death! When indeed will you hear our invocation?
Whatever protection you have for the weary one who presses the soma, whatever shelter there is—by that, speak in our favor.
O gods, there is wide release from distress; there is treasure for the sinless.
O Ādityas, you whose offenses are wondrously absent—let not this bond bind us; may it release us for our great welfare.
For Indra alone is renowned as the sovereign controller.
O gods who desire to help us, do not let us be struck down by the weapon of our treacherous enemies.
And I, O Aditi, address you, the great goddess.

For our protection, [we call upon] the one who is most gracious. Carry us across the deep abyss when we are distressed; O compassionate one, protect us from him who seeks to slay our sons. May no harm come to our offspring.
O sinless one, wide-pastured and far-reaching, grant us space to spread abroad;
provide for our offspring that they may live.
They who are the heads of the people, undeceived and self-glorious—
They, free from malice, guard the sacred laws.
O Ādityas, release us from the jaws of the wolves,
like a thief bound, O Aditi.
O Ādityas, may this arrow of ours go into the waters, and may this ill-will depart from us without striking us.
For evermore, O bounteous Ādityas, we [rely] upon your aids.
Of old we have surely enjoyed [your favor]. O wise ones, O gods, you grant life even to him who returns from sin, so that he may live.
O Ādityas, may that new favor of yours be even better than the old, which shall release us like one bound from his bonds, O Aditi.
O Ādityas, there is nothing for us to leap over; [may you deliver us].
Be gracious unto us;
O Ādityas, let not the weapon of Vivasvat, nor the artificial arrow, strike us before old age has come upon us.
O Ādityas, drive away our hatred, drive away our assault, and drive away all hostility in every direction. We turn you hither like a chariot for our protection and for our well-being.
O most powerful Indra, Lord of the virtuous, you who possess great power and overcome the assailants.
O you of many powers, of many wills, possessor of might, with your all-pervading thought, you have filled [the world] with your greatness.
By whose greatness your two hands, O Great One, reached around the thunderbolt of gold as it moved across the earth.
I call with my courses for aid the Lord of all men, the master of unyielding power, and the protector of the people and of chariots.
For our assistance, we call upon him who ever prospers, whom men invoke from various sides for aid in the battles for the light of heaven.
Indra, who is beyond measure, worthy of praise, fierce, most bountiful,
and even the lord of all riches.
I urge that very Indra on for great bounty and for the drinking [of Soma]—
he who, as the dancer of the people, rules over ancient praise.
O powerful one, no mortal has ever attained your friendship; no one can reach the full extent of your might.
Aided by you, with you as our ally, may we win great wealth in the waters and in the sun, and conquer in battles, O wielder of the thunderbolt.
We seek you with sacrifices, we seek you with songs, O you who most delight in song;
O Indra, just as you have protected Purumīḷha in the battles for booty.
O wielder of the stone, your friendship is sweet, your guidance is sweet; for you, the sacrifice is one that must be spread out.
Make wide space for our bodies, and make wide space for our dwelling;
grant us wide space that we may live.
We contemplate a wide path for the men, a wide one for the cattle, and a wide one for the chariot— a feast for the gods.
Six men, two by two, stand near me, exhilarated by Soma; they are givers of sweet gifts.
Indrota received from the son of Ṛkṣa two bay horses, and from the son of Aśvamedha, two ruddy ones.
To Ātithigva, [grant] excellent chariots; to Arkṣa, [grant] those with beautiful reins; to Aśvamedha, [grant] those that are well-adorned.
Six horses with mares did Ātithigva win from Indrota at the sacrifice of Pūtakratu.
Among these ruddy steeds, the dappled mare, accompanied by stallions, stands conspicuous; she is well-reined and equipped with a whip.
O you who are bound by the prize, not even a mortal man wishing to find fault could ever attribute blame to you.
Forth, forth [I sing] the Triṣṭubh hymn as food for the exhilarating Soma-drop, O heroes.
With prayer and inspired thought, he seeks to win you for the attainment of wisdom.
I seek you as the lord of the lowing cows, the lord of the restless ones,
the master of your inviolable milch-kine.
These spotted cows, yielding milk from their udders, mix the Soma;
they are the clans at the birth of the gods, in the three bright realms of heaven.
Sing forth with song to Indra, the lord of cattle, as he is known—
to the Son of Truth, the protector of the righteous.
The bay horses have been let loose upon the ruddy dawns on the sacrificial grass,
where we raise our voices together in song.
For Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the cows have yielded the milk-mixture, the honeyed draught,
when he found them in the secret place.
When we two, Indra and I, go up to the dwelling-place, the home of the ruddy sun,
having drunk of the honeyed draught, let us both attend upon him in the thrice-seven places of our friend.
Sing praise! Sing forth in praise! O Priyamedhas, sing praise!
Let the sons also sing; and boldly sing praise as if to a fortress.
The gargara-shell resounds; the lizard has cried out all around.
The frog croaks from every side for Indra; the prayer is raised up.
When the dappled cows, easy to milk and unflinching,
hasten hither, seize the unflinching Soma for Indra to drink.
Indra has drunk, Agni has drunk; all the gods have become exhilarated.
Varuṇa indeed dwells here; to him the waters have cried out in unison, like mother cows lowing toward their calf.
You are a good god, O Varuṇa, you whose throat the seven rivers flow over,
like a hollow pipe.
He who has made the swift steeds, well-yoked, spring forth for the donor—he, the leader, is like a fleet-footed courser; he who was released is a wondrous sight to behold.
Truly, O Śakra, Indra has carried himself beyond all enemies;
he, the young one, split apart the porridge being cooked on the far side of the mountain with his song.
Like a small child, he has mounted the new chariot;
he has brought the mighty buffalo-deer for his father and mother, he whose will is all-pervading.
O fair-cheeked lord of the house, mount upon your golden chariot!
Then let us two accompany the celestial, thousand-footed, ruddy, well-faring, and peerless steed.
To him indeed, the self-radiant one, the worshipful ones sit down in this manner;
for they turn toward his well-placed purpose so that he may come to bestow gifts.
The Priyamedhas have followed the ancient dwelling of these [gods]; following their former impulse, those who have spread the sacrificial grass and prepared the offerings have attained [their favor].
He who is the king of the peoples, who moves with his chariots unrestrained,
the overcomer of all hostile armies, the eldest, the slayer of Vṛtra— he is praised.
O Puruhanman, glorify that Indra for protection,
he whose thunderbolt was placed in his hand from of old by the Ordainer, beautiful to behold like the great sun in the sky.
No one can equal him in deed who has made him ever-increasing—
Indra, whom all praise, the skillful, the unassailable, the bold conqueror, as if with sacrifices.
The invincible, fierce one, the conqueror in battles, at whose birth the great, far-reaching ones lowed together—
the milch-cows lowed, and the heavens and the earths lowed.
O Indra, even if there were a hundred heavens and a hundred earths belonging to you,
O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, neither the thousand suns nor the two worlds could equal you at your birth.
O Bull, most powerful one, you have filled all things with your greatness, your manly vigor, and your might.
O Maghavan, wielder of the thunderbolt, protect us with your wondrous aids in the cattle-pen.
O long-lived one, no godless mortal shall obtain food from her;
even he who yokes the swift-moving Etaśas, Indra indeed yokes his two bay steeds.
For your sake, bring that great Indra, the powerful one, for the granting of gifts—
he who is to be invoked in shallow waters and he who is to be invoked in the deep, who is to be invoked in the contests for booty.
O Vasu, O Hero, raise up for us greatly for the sake of bounty;
raise us up, O Maghavan, for the great gift of wealth, and raise us up, O Indra, for great renown.
O Indra, you who seek the Truth, you satisfy yourself with us who are free from reproach;
clothe yourself in the midst of our two arms, O you of many heroic powers, and strike down the Dāsa with your blows.
May the mountain, our own kinsman, shake down the one who follows another's law, the non-human, the non-sacrificer, the godless; may the mountain shake down the Dasyu for easy slaughter.
O most powerful Indra, do you take hold of these in our hands for our gift;
like roasted grains, gather them up for us—twice gather them up, being well-disposed toward us.
O friends, seek out his resolve: how may we accomplish the praise of Śara, the liberal patron and wise lord who is free from shame?
You shall indeed be praised by many seers who have spread the sacrificial grass,
when you thus bestow the calves one by one as you go along.
Maghavan, son of Śūradeva, having seized him by the ear, brought back our calf from the three [rivers],
just as a wise patron brings back a goat to be milked.
O Agni, protect us with your great powers from every hostile force, and also from the enmity of mortal man.
For human wrath has no power over you, O you who are born of love;
you alone, O Lord, are the master of the night.
O Son of Strength, with your auspicious flame, together with all the gods,
grant us wealth that contains every boon.
O Agni, the enemies do not deprive that mortal of wealth whom you protect as a donor.
O wise Agni, that inspired singer whom you urge toward the winning of wealth in the contest for prizes— he, through your protection, shall attain cattle.
O Agni, you bestow wealth consisting of many heroes upon the mortal who offers oblations; lead us forward toward what is better.
Protect us, O Jātavedas; do not deliver us over to the one who intends evil, nor to the mortal of wicked intent.
O Agni, let no godless man ward off the bounty of you, the god;
for you alone are the lord of riches.
As such, O Son of Strength, bestow upon us of your abundant wealth;
O Friend, O Vasu, grant it to those who sing your praise.
May our songs go forth toward him of the sharp flame, the beautiful one to be beheld;
may our sacrifices with homage go toward the possessor of many riches, the one praised by many, for his protection.
Agni, the son of strength, Jātavedas, for the giving of desirable boons—
him who has from of old become the immortal among mortals, the most delightful invoker in the clan.
I invoke Agni for you with the sacrifice to the gods; I invoke Agni as the rite proceeds.
I invoke Agni first among inspired thoughts; I invoke Agni for the swift steed and for the successful attainment of landed property.

May Agni, who is the lord of desirable things, grant us nourishment in his friendship. We constantly implore Agni for our offspring and progeny—he who is the possessor of wealth and the protector of our bodies.
Pray to Agni for protection with songs of praise—the one of piercing luster.
O Purumīḷha, men have praised Agni for wealth; they have praised Agni for a well-shining dwelling.
We praise Agni so that he may ward off hatred from us; we praise Agni so that he may grant us well-being and prosperity.
Like a protector, he is to be invoked among all the people; he becomes the illuminator of the flames.
Prepare the oblation; let the Adhvaryu come again;
he, the wise one, follows his instruction.
The Hotṛ has sat down at the mind, toward the sharp, swift arrow.
Delighting in his friendship,
they seek him within the people with their highest wisdom;
they seize the essence with their tongue.
The giver of strength has strung his bow against the sister; he has climbed the forest and struck the rock with his tongue.
Moving here as a radiant calf, he finds no one to bind him.
He seeks the one worthy of praise; and indeed, his great and vast chariot-yoke, harnessed with horses, has been seen as a bond for the chariot.
Seven milk the one; two and five set her in motion at the ford of the river, above the roar.
With ten hands, Indra has drawn down the bucket of Vivasvat.
With threefold heat from heaven,
the newest flame goes around the three-layered sacrifice;
the Hotṛ-priests anoint it with honey.
With reverence they pour out the water from the high, circling vessel—
downward-flowing, inexhaustible.
The Adityas have taken up the honey that was poured into the lotus-leaf.
At the release of the well,
the cows have come down to the well; great are the two overflowing vessels of the sacrifice, both their handles are made of gold.
Pour the glory upon the pressed juice, the glory that overspreads both heaven and earth;
let the flowing stream take up the Bull. They recognize their own dwelling place, as calves do with their mothers.
They meet together with their kin; devouring in the caverns, they establish a support in heaven—
homage to Indra and Agni, the light of heaven.
The enemy has milked out swelling nourishment and strength that extends over seven steps,
by means of the seven rays of the sun. O Mitra and Varuṇa, the risen sun has taken up the soma.
That is the medicine for the sick man; and indeed, that which is the place of his, the desirable one, the repository—
there he has extended across the sky with his tongue.
Arise for the one who follows the *ṛta*; yoke your chariot, O Aśvins! Let your aid be near at hand.
Come hither, O Aśvins, on your chariot that is swifter than even a blink of an eye.
Sitting nearby... RV_08.073.03.1: O Aśvins, spread out the heat with cold for Atri.
RV_08.073.03.2: Sitting nearby...
Where are you? Whither have you gone? Whither have you flown like two hawks?
You are near at hand... If today, at whatever time, you should hear this invocation.
Sitting nearby...
O Aśvins, most swift to hear the call at the journey’s start, I go to you who are closest; sitting nearby...
O Aśvins, you two have made a home for Atraya near at hand; you dwell in his presence.
O Agni, you choose the heat for Atraya, who speaks beautifully.
He sits near... RV_08.073.09.1: Saptavadhri, through his prayerful hope, has directed the stream of Agni forward.
RV_08.073.09.2: He sits near...
Come here, O possessors of abundant wealth; hear this my invocation.
You are seated nearby. What is this that is being proclaimed to you, as if to two ancient ones who have grown old?
RV_08.073.11.2: Sitting near you... RV_08.073.12.1: Common is your kinship, common is your bond, O Aśvins; sitting near you... RV_08.073.12.2: Sitting near you...
O Aśvins, that chariot of yours which traverses the realms and the two worlds, being near at hand...
[may it come] to us with thousands of cattle and horses. Come hither to us.
RV_08.073.14.2: Sitting nearby... RV_08.073.15.1: Do not overlook us with respect to our herds of cattle and horses, nor with thousands [of wealth].
RV_08.073.15.2: Sitting nearby...
The ruddy one has appeared; light has been made by the follower of Truth.
Sitting nearby...
[the Aśvins] have looked out clearly, like a man with an axe at a tree.
Sit near us... O bold one, shatter him like a fortress, for he is oppressed by the black host.
Sit near us...
Seeking strength, we people of every tribe praise Agni, your much-beloved guest and the lord of the house, with words and hymns of exultation.
Him whom men, bearing oblations, honor like Mitra, whose draught is clarified butter.
They praise with hymns of praise Jātavedas, the most praiseworthy one, who, exalted among the gods,
has conveyed the oblations to heaven.
We have come to Agni, the best slayer of Vṛtra, the eldest, the descendant of Manu,
whose face Śrutarvan and Bṛhan-Ārkṣa cause to prosper.
[We come] to the immortal Jātavedas, visible even through the darkness.
To Agni, who is to be praised when offered clarified butter, whom these people here, striving together, worship with oblations,
pouring from their extended ladles.
RV_08.074.07.1 This newest hymn has been offered to you, O Agni, by us. RV_08.074.07.2 O delightful one, well-born, of noble will, unerring, wondrous guest!
RV_08.074.08.1 May this [hymn] be most peaceful, most pleasing, and dear to you, O Agni.
Grow strong through that [praise], being well-extolled. She, radiant with splendors, shall bestow great fame upon us in the slaying of Vṛtra.
Like a horse, like a cow that fills the chariot, like the brilliant Indra, the lord of the good—
him whose glories you celebrate, O people, and who is praised again and again;
you, O Agni Aṅgiras, whom Gopavana has delighted with his song.
O Purifier, hear our call—
you whom people invoke with urgency for the winning of booty; be mindful of us in the conquest of Vṛtra.

Invoked by Śrutarvan, the son of Ṛkṣa, who pours forth the intoxicating draught, I shall stroke the heads of his four steeds, as one strokes the herds of woolly rams. May the four swift and fleet-footed horses of the most powerful one carry me.
Like well-guided chariots, they shall carry the offerings to the feast, as birds carry the son of Tugra.
Truly, O great river Paruṣṇī, I have pointed you out;
there is no mortal other than the most powerful one who bestows horses upon these waters.
Yoke, O Agni, like a charioteer, your horses that best summon the gods; sit down as the ancient Hotṛ-priest.
And do you, O god, who are most wise, speak here for us to the gods.
Grant us faith and all desirable things.
For you, O youngest one, son of strength,
when invoked with oblations, have become the observer of Truth and worthy of sacrifice.
This Agni is the lord of thousandfold and hundredfold booty; he is the sage, the head of riches.
As the *Ṛbhus* bend the felly [of the wheel], so do you bend him with our joint invocations.
Come closer to the sacrifice, O Aṅgiras!
Now, O Virūpa, with an eternal voice, urge forth this excellent hymn of praise for that bull-like one who looks toward heaven.
Who indeed can withstand the onset of this Agni, whose eye looks backward?
Let us strike down the Pani in the struggle for the cattle. Let not the hosts of the gods overlook us, like cows wallowing in water.
May the cows not let us waste away; may the distress of the malicious one who hates us all not strike us down,
as a wave strikes a ship.
Homage to you, O Agni; the peoples sing praise to your might, O God. With your missiles, crush the adversary.
Will you not, O Agni, truly provide us with wealth for the quest for cattle? Envelop us in riches.
O maker of wide space, make wide space for us!
Do not abandon us in this great contest, like one who carries a burden; win the prize, win the wealth!
O Agni, let this distress, born of fear, pursue someone other than us; increase our impetuous might.
[He is] the one whose reverent service or the labor of the pious man you have accepted with joy.
Agni indeed protects him;
from the highest distance, cross over toward those who are nearer,
to those whom I am here to protect.
For we have known you, O Agni, from of old, as one who provides aid like a father; therefore, we now implore your favor.
Now I invoke this Indra, the master of wondrous power, who rules by his might.
You do not withhold [the gift] from him who is accompanied by the Maruts.
This Indra, with the Maruts as his companions, split asunder the head of Vṛtra with his hundred-knotted thunderbolt.
Growing strong with the Maruts as his allies, Indra drove Vṛtra away,
releasing the waters of the ocean. Indeed, by him— accompanied by the Maruts— this light of heaven was won.
With Indra, for the drinking of Soma;
we invoke with songs Indra, who is accompanied by the Maruts, the consumer of the dregs, the powerful, and the exuberant.
We invoke Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, with an ancient hymn,
for the drinking of this Soma.
O bounteous Indra, lord of a hundred powers, accompanied by the Maruts, drink the Soma!
At this sacrifice, O you who are praised by many men!
For you, O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, O wielder of the stone, these pressed Soma juices are offered with the heart by those who recite hymns.
O Indra, friend of the Maruts, drink the pressed Soma during the celestial rites,
whetting your thunderbolt with might.
Rising up with power, having drunk, you shook your jaws.
O Indra, [drink] the pressed Soma in the vessel;
both heaven and earth cried out after you as you roared,
O Indra, when you became the slayer of the Dasyus.

I have measured out my body from Indra—the speech that has eight feet, nine corners, and touches the Eternal Order (Ṛta). As soon as he was born, the Lord of a Hundred Powers (Śatakratu) asked his mother thus: "Who am I?"
Who are the fierce ones? Who indeed are renowned?
He has proclaimed them as the powerful: Aurṇavābha and Ahīśuva;
let these be your sons, O Niṣṭhura.
The Vṛtra-slayer crushed them together with his bolt, as one forces out the spokes from the holes; he grew strong as the slayer of the Dasyus. With a single draught, he drank up thirty lakes at once.
Indra, through his longing for Soma,
struck down the Gandharva in the unfathomable depths of the mid-air;
Indra [did this] indeed for the increase of those who offer sacred prayer.
He pierced [the demon] from the mountains and held the cooked rice;
Indra drew his well-strung bow.
Your arrow has a hundred barbs, and it alone has a thousand feathers.
O Indra, with that [friend] whom you have made your ally— bring that for the sake of the singers, for the men and for the women, so that they may eat;
O you who are firm from birth, [you who are] Ribhu-like as soon as born.
These most exalted deeds of yours have been performed with fullness;
you, whose resolve is firm, have sustained them with your heart.
All these things Viṣṇu, the wide-strider, brought hither when impelled by you.
A hundred buffaloes, rice cooked with milk, a boar, and a ram—these, O Indra, [I offer].
Powerful is your well-fashioned, pleasant bow; excellent is your golden arrow. Both your arms are worthy of battle, well-prepared, increasing even the soft with their softness.
O Indra, bring us a thousandfold portions of the pressed juice and the sacrificial cake;
O Hero, bring us hundreds of cattle. Bring us the distinguishing mark: cattle, horses, and ointment.
Together with golden neck-ornaments,
O bold one, bring us many ear-ornaments as well;
for you, O Vasu, are renowned as the one who hears us.
No one, O Indra, can surpass you in growth, nor in the giving of good gifts, nor in the granting of wealth; no other, O Hero, can do so for the one who offers worship.
Indra cannot be brought low, nor can the powerful Śakra be overcome.
He hears all; he sees all. He, the undeceived, seeks out the wrath of mortals;
before reproach comes, he seeks to act.
Truly, by his power, the belly of the swift ordainer is full—
the slayer of Vṛtra, the drinker of Soma.
In you, O Soma, all treasures and all blessings are gathered together.
O bounteous giver, never to be surpassed!
My desire for you seeks after you— desiring cattle, desiring gold, and desiring horses.
O Indra, through hope in you, I have taken a sickle in my hand.
O Maghavan, fill me with a handful of barley, whether it be that which is being harvested or that which has already been gathered.
This Soma is the doer, ungraspable, all-conquering, and the piercer.
The seer, inspired by poetic wisdom, covers what was naked; he heals everything that is afflicted.
He has manifested light for the blind, and the lame have been set free.
O Soma, you who provide wide protection as a shield against the hostilities that pierce our bodies and those wrought by others;
O impetuous one, through your wisdom and your powers, you extend from heaven to earth.
Even the enmity of one who eats heroes [is overcome].
When those seeking their goal go for their purpose, may they reach the gift of the giver; may they satisfy the desire of the thirsty.
He who provided what was lost of old, he raised up the one who lives by the *ṛta*; he extended that life which had not yet been crossed.
May he, who is most gracious, the compassionate one whose will is undaunted and who is unassailed, be merciful to us.
O Soma, be a blessing to our heart. O Soma, do not make us tremble; do not terrify us, O King. Do not strike down our heart with your brilliance.
When I behold the ill-will of the gods in my own dwelling, O King, drive away our enemies; O Bounteous One, drive away those who seek to harm us.
For there is no other, O Śatakratu, who can so effectively grant us comfort.
O Indra, have mercy on us!
O Indra, you who have ever before protected us unceasingly for the winning of booty— do you, O Indra, have mercy on us!
Why indeed, O impeller of the weak, do you not aid the one who presses the soma? Surely, O Indra, you are capable of helping us.
O wielder of the stone, O Indra, protect our chariot even if it be far behind.
Place him before me! Come now, why do you sit still? Make our chariot foremost, a preeminent glory that seeks the prize!
Help our prize-seeking chariot; it is easy for you to do. What can hold us back? Make us thoroughly victorious.
O Indra, be firm; you are full. Your auspicious [chariot] comes to the appointed place.
This prayer is timely;
let it not be deficient, for the broad course is set, the prize is placed,
and the obstacles have been removed.
We desire that fourth name worthy of sacrifice which you have made yours; from the beginning, O Lord, you have been mindful of us.
He has increased you, O immortals; he has gladdened you, O gods who dwell in heaven, and those who are goddesses.
Therefore, bestow upon him excellent wealth; may he who is rich in inspired thought come quickly in the morning. O Indra, seize for us a wonderful, food-filled prize with your great right hand.
For we know you, O performer of many deeds, of many gifts, and of great wealth—
of vast measure through your aids.
For neither the gods nor mortals can restrain you, O Hero, when you desire to give.
As one restrains a bull when it is fierce, they do not hold him back.
Come now, let us praise Indra, the lord of wealth, the self-ruling king;
may he not neglect us with his bounty.
Let him praise; let him sing near; let him hear the *sāman* being sung. May he respond with a gift of wealth.
Bring to us with your right hand; touch [us] with your left.
O Indra, do not exclude us from wealth. Come hither, O bold one; with courage, bring the riches of the people who are most liberal in giving.
O Indra, whatever prize-winning strength you possess that is to be won by the inspired poets— win that well for us!
May those strengths of yours, swift as lightning and all-gladdening, come to us instantly.
And by their will, they quickly grow old.
Run forth from afar and from near at hand, O slayer of Vṛtra,
for the pouring out of the honeyed draught!
The Soma juices are strong; come hither! They have been pressed, they are exhilarating.
Drink, O steadfast one, as you desire! Rejoice in the food; it is sufficient for your choice and your will.
May it be well with your heart, O Indra.
Come hither, O you who have no enemy; you are invoked by our hymns in the highest luminous realm of heaven.
For you this [Soma] has been pressed with stones and purified with milk for exhilaration;
O Indra, Soma is offered to you.
O Indra, hear my call well; [hear it] from us regarding this pressed juice mixed with milk.
Attain full satisfaction from the draught!
O Indra, that Soma which has been pressed for you in the cups and in the vats—drink of it; you are its lord.
Soma, who is seen in the vats like the moon in the waters—of this you are the master; drink of it!
That which the falcon brought to you with his foot, across the regions, untouched.
Drink of this; you are its lord.
We choose for ourselves that great exhilaration of the gods, for our protection, from those who are powerful.
May they— Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman— be our constant allies, as well as the wise ones who increase our prosperity.
Carry us across many perils, as one crosses waters with ships.
You are the charioteers of the cosmic order (*ṛta*). O Aryaman, may we have desirable wealth; O Varuṇa, may we have desirable wealth worthy of praise; for we choose desirable wealth.
For you, O wise ones, are the lords of desirable wealth, O destroyers of enemies;
O Ādityas, you do not grant a portion of evil. O bounteous givers, whether we dwell at home or travel upon the road, [we depend on you].
O Gods, we invoke you for our prosperity. O Indra and Viṣṇu, look upon these kinsmen of ours;
O Maruts and Aśvins, come hither!
O bounteous ones, we indeed maintain our brotherhood from of old, even in the common womb of our mother.
For you, O bounteous ones, with Indra as your eldest, are directed toward heaven.
And now I speak to you once more;
I praise Agni, your dearest guest, like a beloved friend, as one who knows the way, like a chariot.
Like a seer of profound wisdom, whom the gods have established once again among mortals;
O youngest one, protect the men who offer oblations and hear our songs.
Protect our offspring and ourselves.
With what [hymn], O Agni Aṅgiras, son of strength, may we offer praise to you, O God, according to your desire and your will?
With what intention shall we serve the sacrifice, O Son of Strength?
What word of homage shall we now speak?
For you indeed shall grant us all secure dwellings.
O Lord of the House, whose songs of praise, seeking prize-winning wealth, do you now quicken? Whose prayers, seeking to win cattle, do you favor?
They groom him, the one of excellent wisdom, the one who goes at the head in battles, the vigorous one in his own dwellings.
He dwells with secure and perfect peace; no one slays him, but he slays those who would strike him.
O Agni, he prospers with excellent heroes.
O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, come to my invocation, you two,
for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
O Aśvins, hear this hymn of mine, hear this my invocation,
for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
O Aśvins, possessors of abundant wealth, this Kṛṣṇa here invokes you.
To drink the sweet Soma. Hear the call of the singer, of Kṛṣṇa who praises you, O Heroes,
to drink the sweet Soma.
O heroes, come to the dwelling of the donor who praises you, O Aśvins, for the drinking of the sweet Soma— [you who provide] inviolable protection for the inspired singer who offers praise.
For the drinking of the sweet Soma.
Yoke the donkey to the chariot with its strong-limbed frame, O possessors of bovine wealth,
for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
Come, O Aśvins, on your three-seated, triple-wheeled chariot,
for the drinking of the sweet Soma. Now, O Nāsatyas, O Aśvins, further my songs.
For the drinking of the sweet Soma. For you both are the wonder-workers, the physicians who bring delight; you both have become the masters of skillful speech.
Viśvaka invokes you both for the protection of his body; do not sever our friendship, but release us from our bonds.
How indeed shall I now praise you two when my mind is troubled? You two bestowed the prayer for the attainment of wealth.
Viśvaka [praised] you two...
For you two indeed bestowed upon Purubhū and Medhatithi the power for the attainment of wealth.
RV_08.086.03.2 {09} Viśvaka [praises] you two...
RV_08.086.04.1 {09} And that hero, the winner of wealth, who drinks the dregs of the soma—though he be far away, we call upon him for protection.
RV_08.086.04.2 {09} He whose most sweet favor is like that of a father—do not sever our friendship; release us!
By the *ṛta* (Cosmic Order), the god Savitṛ has brought peace; the horn of *ṛta* has spread itself far and wide.
*Ṛta* has conquered even those who fiercely attack us. Do not sever our friendship; release us!
O Aśvins, glorious is your hymn of praise; like a pouring cloud, come hither!
O Heroes, drink of the pressed honey-sweet mead; you are beloved in heaven, like two bulls for the one who offers the oblation.
O Aśvins, drink the honeyed *gharma* offering; sit upon the sacred grass, O Heroes.
Rejoicing in the dwelling of man, protect us with your wisdom and grant us vital strength.
The Priyamedhas have invoked you both with all your aids;
come to the dwelling of him who has trimmed the sacrificial grass, to the beloved sacrifice during the rites of the seekers of heaven.
O Aśvins, drink the honeyed Soma; sit upon the sacrificial grass with favor.
Growing strong, come to our fair praise from heaven like two bulls to the pasture.
Now come, O Aśvins, with your dappled horses! O wonder-workers on golden paths, lords of splendor, increase of Truth, drink the Soma!
For we, the inspired singers seeking praise, invoke you both for the winning of the prize.
O wondrous Aśvins, performers of many deeds, come with your wisdom and readiness to hear us.
I [praise] that wondrous one of yours, the subduer of the assaulters, who rejoices in the exhilarating soma-juice of wealth.

Like milch-cows lowing toward their calves in the stalls, we celebrate Indra with our songs— him who dwells in heaven, the bounteous giver, encompassed by powers, and like a mountain rich in many enjoyments. We implore him for food, for booty in hundreds and thousands, and swiftly for wealth consisting of cattle.
The great, solid mountains do not obstruct you, O Indra, when you wish to bestow wealth upon a praiser like me; no one can diminish that of yours.
You are a warrior by your will, your power, and your wondrous deeds, surpassing all created beings in your majesty.
May this hymn turn you hither for our protection, it which the Gotamas have generated.
For you have indeed extended yourself beyond the ends of heaven by your might;
no one has encompassed you, O Indra, for you have grown great according to your own self-sustaining power.
O Maghavan, there is no one who can obstruct your bounty when you bestow it upon the worshipper. Be the inspirer of our hymn, most generous one, for the winning of the prize.
O Maruts, sing a lofty song to Indra, the greatest slayer of Vṛtra.

By which [strength] the upholders of *ṛta*, the gods, generated light—the god who is watchful for the sake of the gods—Indra blew away the curses, the slayer of the revilers; then Indra became resplendent in glory.
O you of great luster, the Marut-host, those gods strove for your friendship, O Indra.
Sing forth a prayer to the great Indra, O Maruts!
Let the Vṛtra-slayer, the lord of a hundred powers, slay Vṛtra with his hundred-knotted thunderbolt. Boldly strike out against him, O you of bold mind; even your fame shall become vast.

Let the waters flow forth with speed like mothers; slay Vṛtra and win the light of heaven! When you were born, O matchless Maghavan, for the slaughter of Vṛtra, then you spread out the earth and propped up the sky.
From that your sacrifice was born; from that the hymn and the joyful song.
Therefore you surpass all that is born and all that is to be born. You have placed the cooked within the raw; you have made the sun ascend in heaven.

Like the heat of the sacrificial vessel, heat yourselves with well-fashioned hymns—[O Maruts], beloved by the lover of songs—with a lofty [chant]. May Indra, who is to be invoked in all battles, attend to us; may the slayer of Vṛtra, the supreme victor worthy of praise, come to our prayers and libations.
You are the first giver of riches; you are the true lord who acts with sovereign power.
We choose the alliance of the mighty Tuvidyumna, the son of great strength.
O Indra, lover of songs, these unsurpassed prayers are being fashioned for you.
O Indra, Lord of the Bay Horses, take pleasure in these [songs], which we have meditated upon for you as a *yojana* (a distance/journey).
For you, O Maghavan, are the true one, never bowed down; you strike down many Vṛtras.
O Most Powerful One, wielder of the thunderbolt, bring wealth toward us for the donor.
O Indra, you are glorious, the drinker of the *ṛjīṣa*, O Lord of Might.
You alone, the sustainer of the people, slay the irresistible Vṛtras, having conquered them.
Therefore, O Asura, we now entreat you, the wise one, for wealth as our allotted share.
Like a great skin, O Indra, you are our refuge; may your favors reach us.
A maiden, seeking a suitor, found the Soma flowing through the strainer. As she brought it home, she said: "I shall press you for Indra; I shall press you for Śakra."
O hero, you who go there, looking out from house to house—
drink this juice pressed by the jaws, accompanied by parched grain,
by groats, by cakes, and by hymns of praise! We cannot discern you, nor do we grasp you.
Flow around for Indra, O Indu, as it were softly, as it were gently.
Will he not heal? Will he not act? Will he not make us better?
Will we, who have been hostile to our husband, now find union with Indra?
O Indra, cause these three regions to sprout anew:
that head of mine, this fertile field, and this [portion] here within my belly. And that fertile field which is there, let it be this very body of mine.

And as for that head of the stretched-out [hide], make all those parts hairy. O Śatakratu, having thrice cleansed Apālā in the hole of the chariot, the hole of the cart, and the hole of the yoke, you made her sun-skin.
Sing forth to Indra for the drinking of your soma-juice—
he who is the all-conquering lord of a hundred powers, the most generous among the people,
invoked by many, praised by many, the leader of songs, and renowned from of old.
"Indra!"—thus you should say.
Indra is indeed the giver of great spoils to us, the dancer; he, the mighty one, shall lead us forward with his jaws.
The broad-chinned Indra has drunk of the soma-juice, of the well-prepared, offered libation;
of the drop mixed with barley, O Indra.
Sing forth to that Indra so that he may drink of the soma.
For this indeed was his means of strengthening;
having drunk of these exhilarations, the god, by the might of the god,
has surpassed all worlds.
Bring hither for our protection that ever-conquering one of yours, who is extended across all songs;
bring him down for our aid—
the warrior, the unassailable, the drinker of Soma, the immovable.
The man of irresistible will— O Indra, you who know much, O R̥cīṣama, bestow wealth upon us;
help us in the decisive contest for booty.
From there, O Indra, come to us with food that brings a hundredfold strength,
with food that brings a thousandfold strength. O Śakra, finder of cattle, may we, through our inspired thoughts, direct our prayers toward you with swift steeds.
May we conquer in battles, O wielder of the thunderbolt! We, O Lord of a hundred powers, cause you to take delight in our hymns, as cattle do in pastures.
For all desires of mortal man, O Śatakratu, have come to you, O wielder of the thunderbolt; we have come with our hopes set upon you.
In you alone, O son of strength, those who yearn for their desires have found fulfillment.
Nothing surpasses you, O Indra. As such, O bull, favor us with your most bountiful, formidable, and swift-moving wisdom, accompanied by abundant prosperity.
O Śatakratu Indra, that exhilaration of yours which is now most glorious—
by that very exhilaration, do you now rejoice.
O Indra, that exhilaration of yours which is most renowned and the greatest slayer of Vṛtra.
He who bestows vigor and gladdens with Soma—
O wielder of the stone, O true drinker of Soma, we know indeed that which you have bestowed upon all the people, O wonder-worker.

For Indra, who delights in the intoxicating drink, let our songs resound around the pressed soma; let the poets sing the hymn of praise. In him all glories rejoice, in whom the seven assemblies take their delight.
We invoke Indra when the Soma is pressed.
At the Trikadruka rites, the gods performed the sacrifice that brings consciousness; may our songs of praise increase him.
Let the drops enter into you, as rivers flow into the ocean;
O Indra, nothing exceeds you.
You have encompassed with your greatness, O mighty and watchful one, the draught of Soma.
O Indra, that [Soma] which is within your bellies— O Vṛtra-slayer, let the Soma be sufficient for your belly, O Indra; let the drops be sufficient for your powers.
Śrutakakṣa sings sufficiently for the swift horse, sufficiently for the cow,
and sufficiently for the domain of Indra.
For you, O Indra, do indeed attend to us when the Soma juices are pressed.
O Śakra, you are ready to grant [our desires].
Even from afar, O wielder of the thunderbolt, let our songs reach you;
may we come readily before you.
For thus indeed you are one who seeks heroes, thus a hero, and thus steadfast.
Thus indeed is your mind to be won over.
Thus, O possessor of abundant wealth, has your gift been established by all the ordainers.
And so, O Indra, be with me;
do not be sluggish like a priest, O Lord of spoils!
Rejoice in the pressed juice mixed with milk.
O Indra, let not the sun’s rays reach us with their threatening glances;
with you as our ally, may we win that.
With you as our ally, O Indra, may we answer back against our rivals.
You are ours; we are yours.
For you indeed do the Indra-loving singers, your friends, O Indra, follow after you as they move along.
O Sūrya, you indeed rise up toward the bull of renowned bounty, the performer of manly deeds, the archer. He who by the strength of his arms shattered ninety-nine fortresses.
And he, the slayer of Vṛtra, slew the serpent.
That Indra is our auspicious friend; may he milk for us wealth in horses, cattle, and barley, like a wide-streaming cow.
O Vṛtra-slayer, whatever the sun has risen over today,
all that, O Indra, is under your control. Or rather, O exalted Lord of Beings, if you think, "I shall not die."
And this is truly yours:
O Indra, you go to all those Soma juices that are pressed, whether they be in the distance or nearby.
We incite that Indra for the sake of great victory, to slay Vṛtra;
may he become the bull, the showerer of blessings.
That Indra has been made ready for the gift; he is the most powerful, established for the exhilaration of the soma-draught.
Resplendent and renowned is that Soma;
like a thunderbolt fashioned by song, he is powerful and unshakable. Sublime and unconquered, he has grown great.
Even in a difficult place, O Indra, lover of songs, being praised, make for us an easy path;
and you, O Maghavan, have the power to do so. You, whose command and sovereignty no one at all disregards.
Neither god nor man, however diligent, can surpass thee.
Thus the two goddesses, Heaven and Earth, O fair-cheeked one, revere thy irresistible might.
You have established this bright milk in the dark cows and in the ruddy ones, and in the *paruṣṇī* rivers.
When he released it, then all the gods stepped forth from their brilliance.
They have found the track of the wild beast.
May the Vṛtra-slayer come to me as my protector; he has displayed his manly power—he who is without an enemy and unsubdued.
I have heard of you as the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, the bold host of the peoples; I call upon you for great and heroic bounty.
O you of many names, much-praised one, come through this prayer that seeks cattle.
When you become present at every Soma-pressing,
may the Vṛtra-slayer, who is rich in libations, be mindful of us; may the powerful one hear our prayer.
With what aid will you gladden us, O Bull? With what [aid] will you bring [wealth] to those who praise you?
With whose pressed juice does the Bull, accompanied by his teams, take delight?
The slayer of Vṛtra [comes] for the drinking of the Soma.
Being exhilarated, do thou indeed bestow upon us thousandfold wealth; be the giver to the worshipper.
These pressed juices, accompanied by their consorts, go eagerly to the feast;
the dweller in the waters, the silent one, has arrived. The offered oblations have been poured forth, strengthening Indra at the sacrifice.
Perform the final purificatory bath with power here. Bring hither those two bay steeds, companions at the feast, with golden manes,
to the prepared food-offering.
For you, O Radiant One, these Soma juices have been pressed; the sacrificial grass is strewn.
Bring Indra hither for the sake of those who offer praise. May he bestow upon you skill and splendor, and grant treasures to the donor.
Sing praises to Indra for the sake of the singers! O Śatakratu, I bestow all power and hymns upon you;
O Indra, be gracious to the singers!
Bring us what is auspicious after auspiciousness— food and vigor, O Śatakratu—
when you, O Indra, show us mercy. Bring to us all prosperity, O Śatakratu.
O Indra, when you show us mercy...
We who have pressed the soma call upon you alone, O greatest slayer of Vṛtra...
O Indra, when you show us mercy...
Come to our pressed juice with your bay horses, O Lord of exhilarations;
come to our pressed juice with your bay horses.
He who is doubly the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, Indra, the lord of a hundred powers, has been found.
Come to our pressed [juice] with your bay steeds;
for you, O slayer of Vṛtra, are the drinker of these Soma juices.
Come to our pressed [juice] with your bay steeds.
May Indra grant us nourishment, the wealth of the *Ṛbhus* and the lord of the *Ṛbhus*;
may the prize-winner grant us the prize itself.
The lowing cow, seeking glory, the mother of the bounteous Maruts, yields her milk.
The two steeds of the chariots are yoked;
in her lap all the gods maintain their sacred laws,
as they gaze upon the sun and moon.
All noble poets ever sing that well of ours for the sake of drinking Soma, O Maruts.
This Soma has been pressed; the Maruts drink of it.
And the self-ruling Aśvins drink, as do Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa, from the stream of the purified juice that dwells in three places and is full of life.
And may Indra, taking pleasure in this pressed juice mixed with milk,
exhilarate himself like the Hotṛ-priest at dawn.
What will our wise patrons do when they blaze forth, crossing over their enemies as if across waters?
They flow forth, possessing purified skill.
Whom among you, O great gods, do I choose today for protection— you who are wondrous in splendor by your very nature?
Those Maruts who have spread out all the earthly realms and the luminous spheres of heaven—
them I call hither for the drinking of Soma. O Maruts, I invoke you from heaven, you whose strength is purified.
For the drinking of this Soma;
Those Maruts who have propped apart the two worlds, them indeed I invoke for the drinking of this Soma.
I now call upon that host of Maruts, dwelling on the mountains, the bull-like troop,
for the drinking of this Soma.
O lover of songs, may my hymns rise up to you when the juices are pressed, like a charioteer.
RV 8.95.1: O Indra, they have lowed toward you in unison, as mother cows toward their calf.
RV 8.95.2: O Indra, lover of songs, the bright pressed juices have drawn you hither;
drink of this food, O Indra, for it is prepared for you in all [the vessels].
Drink the Soma for exhilaration, O Indra— the pressed juice brought by the falcon—
for you are the Lord and King of all the eternal tribes. Hear the call of Tiraścī, O Indra, who serves you.
Fill me with wealth consisting of heroic sons and cattle; you are great.
O Indra, he has generated for you a new song, delightful to hear—a prayer from one whose mind is discerning, an ancient thought that swells with the Truth (ṛta).
Let us praise that Indra whom songs and hymns have strengthened;
desiring to win his many manly deeds, we shall conquer.
Come now, let us praise the pure Indra with a pure *sāman*.
May he who has grown strong through pure hymns be exhilarated by the pure, well-aimed draught.
O Indra, come to us pure, pure with your pure aids;
being pure, bestow wealth upon us; being pure and worthy of Soma, be exhilarated.
O Indra, as one pure, bestow wealth upon us; as one pure, grant treasures to the donor.
As one pure, you slay the Vṛtras; as one pure, you seek to win the prize.
For him, the Dawns have lengthened their course; for Indra, the nights with their fair voices have extended their flow.
For him, the seven rivers, the mothers, stood still—those easy-to-cross streams—for the men to ford.
Though pierced through by that which was even unsteady, the weapon, he joined together the thrice-seven ridges of the mountains.
Neither god nor mortal could surpass those deeds which the grown bull performed.
The iron thunderbolt of Indra is firmly joined; in the two arms of Indra is the greatest might.
In the head of Indra, his powers are uniquely concentrated; they have settled near him to be heard close at hand.
I deem you the most worthy of sacrifice among those worthy of sacrifice; I deem you the shaker of even the unshakable.
I reckon thee, O Indra, as the banner of heroes; I reckon thee as the bull of the peoples.

When thou, O Indra, dost take the mace that distills exhilaration into thy arms for the sake of glory and for slaying, then the mountains resounded, the cattle lowed, and the priests drew near to Indra.
Let us praise him who brought forth all these creatures that are younger than he;
through our songs may we win Mitra with Indra, and may we approach the Bull with prostrations.
Fleeing from the snort of Vṛtra, all the gods who were his friends abandoned him.
O Indra, let there be friendship between you and the Maruts; then shall you conquer all these hostile armies.
The sixty-three Maruts, worthy of sacrifice, have increased in strength like heaps of dawn-rays;
we approach them. Grant us our portion; we shall honor your might with this oblation.
The host of the Maruts bears sharp weapons; who, O Indra, has dared to withstand your thunderbolt?
O impetuous one, with your wheel, strip away those weaponless Asuras and godless ones.
Send forth a well-fashioned hymn to the great, fierce, and powerful one, most auspicious for our cattle.
Offer many songs to Indra, who is borne by songs; bestow them upon his body, for will he not surely take notice?
Send forth your inspired thought to the mighty one who is borne by hymns, as one crosses to the further shore of rivers with a boat.
Touch the body of the famous one, who is most dear to you, through your devotion; for will he not surely take notice?
Perform that for which Indra will take pleasure; praise him with a beautiful hymn and seek to win him with homage.
Draw near, O singer; do not cry out [in vain]; let your voice be heard—surely he knows, does he not? The drop descended into the *Aṃśumatī*, moving along as a black one with ten thousand [followers].
Indra helped him with his power as he blew; the hero-minded one laid aside the female serpents.
I saw the drop moving in various directions in the secret place by the river Aṃśumatī.
Like a black cloud, he has taken his stand; I shall send you forth, O heroes, to fight in battle.
Then the Drop, flashing forth, assumed his body in the lap of Aṃśumatī.
With Bṛhaspati as his ally, Indra overcame the godless tribes that were attacking us.
At your birth, O Indra, you became the enemy of those seven who had no enemies.
You found heaven and earth when they were hidden; you bestowed joy upon the mighty worlds.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, with your fearless bolt you struck down that peerless power. With your weapons you overcame Śuṣṇa; O Indra, by your skillful might you found the cattle.
O Bull among the people, you have indeed become the mighty slayer of Vṛtras;
you released the obstructed rivers and you won back the waters whose lord was the Dāsa.
He is the one of excellent wisdom who rejoices in the pressed juices, he whose fury is unsurpassed, and who is wealthy as the day itself.
He who alone performs manly deeds, he is the slayer of Vṛtra; others they call his counterpart.
That Indra is the slayer of Vṛtra, the sustainer of the people; him we shall invoke with fair praise as one to be called upon.
He, the bounteous Maghavan, is our protector and advocate; he is the giver of strength and glorious fame.
That Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, the lord of the Ṛbhus, as soon as he was born, became one to be invoked;
performing many manly deeds, like Soma when drunk, he is to be invoked by his friends.
O Indra, those enjoyments which you, possessing the light of heaven, brought from the Asuras—
O Maghavan, prosper the singer of this hymn and those who have trimmed the sacred grass for you.
O Indra, whatever horse, cow, or imperishable portion you have ordained as your share,
bestow that upon the sacrificer who presses the soma and gives the sacrificial fee, not upon the usurer.
O Indra, that one who is lawless, who follows his own sleep, and who is godless—may he perish by his own ways;
deprive him of nourishing wealth and keep him far away from it.
O Śakra, slayer of Vṛtra, whether you are in the distance or nearby.
Therefore, O Indra, the one who has pressed the soma seeks to win you over with songs that reach to heaven like long-maned locks.
Whether you are in the luminous realm of heaven, upon the surface of the ocean,
in a terrestrial dwelling, O greatest slayer of Vṛtra, or in the intermediate space— come hither!
O Soma-drinker, Lord of Might, rejoice among our pressed soma juices with your bounty, O Indra, with wealth full of truth and abundance.
O Indra, do not cast us away; be our companion at the feast.
You are our aid; you are our kinship. O Indra, do not turn us away.
O Indra, sit with us by the pressed juice to drink the honeyed mead.
O Maghavan, grant new and great favor to the singer; O Indra, be with us by the pressed juice.
Neither gods nor mortals have attained thee, O wielder of the stone;

thou surpassest all created beings in thy might—neither the gods have attained thee. For the sake of sovereignty, they have fashioned and begotten Indra together, the hero who overcomes all hostile armies.
By his wisdom, he is most excellent, the best subduer of enemies, fierce, most powerful, mighty, and swift.
The singers have raised their voices together to Indra for the drinking of the Soma—
him who is the lord of heaven, so that he may increase [our strength], for he, whose vows are firm, is united with power and with his aids.
The inspired singers bow to the rim [of the wheel] with their vision, chanting toward the ram.
Your well-shining, guileless, and impetuous ones are close to the ear along with the chanters. I repeatedly invoke that Indra, the bounteous and fierce one, who truly possesses irresistible powers.
May the most generous one, worthy of sacrifice, turn toward us with our songs; may the wielder of the thunderbolt make all paths easy for us to reach wealth.
O Indra, you have always known how to shatter those fortresses with your might, O strongest and most powerful Śakra.
At your fear, O wielder of the thunderbolt, all beings, heaven and earth, tremble.
O Indra, O hero, O wonderful one, may that truth protect me; O wielder of the thunderbolt, ferry me across many difficulties as if across waters.
O King Indra, when will you grant us wealth—wealth that is all-sustaining and worthy of longing?
Sing forth a lofty *sāman* for Indra, the inspired singer, the great one—the great [song].
To the one who acts according to dharma, the wise, the praiseworthy—O Indra, you are the conqueror; you caused the sun to shine. You are the maker of all, the god of all, and you are great.
Shining with light, you have gone to the sun, to the luminous realm of heaven;
O Indra, the gods have striven for your friendship.
Come to us, O Indra, as our beloved, the ever-conquering one who cannot be hidden.
Like a mountain broad on all sides, he is the Lord of Heaven.
For you, O true Soma-drinker, have surpassed both worlds, O Indra; you are the strengthener of the one who presses the juice, the Lord of Heaven.

For you, O Indra, are the shatterer of eternal fortresses; you are the slayer of the Dasyus, the prosperer of Manu, and the Lord of Heaven. Therefore, O Indra, lover of songs, we have released our great longings toward you.
Rising up with the waters,
O Hero, the prayers increase you with their fresh offerings, O Indra,
even as you grow day by day, O wielder of the thunderbolt.
They yoke the two bay steeds with song to the broad-yoked chariot of the impetuous one, the bearers of Indra, harnessed by the word.
O Indra, bring us strength and manly vigor, O Śatakratu, O far-seeing one!
[Bring] the hero who conquers in battle.
For you indeed, O Vasu, have become our father and our mother, O Śatakratu; therefore, we pray for your favor.
O impetuous one, much-invoked, you who are eager for booty, I address you, O Śatakratu;
grant us heroic strength in our battles.
For indeed, yesterday and today, the zealous men have made you swell with draughts, O wielder of the thunderbolt.
O Indra, hear us here, you who are borne by our hymns; come to our dwelling place.
O fair-cheeked one, lord of the bay steeds, rejoice; we implore this of you. The wise ones wait upon you;
O Indra, lover of songs, your glories are supreme and worthy of praise when the soma is pressed.
Turning toward him as if toward the sun, may all partake of Indra’s riches;
at his birth and at every new birth by his might, we look toward his portion as our own.
Praise the giver of wealth whose gifts are never-failing; auspicious indeed are the gifts of Indra.
Thus, he is not angry with the one who fulfills his desire, as he impels the mind toward giving.
O Indra, you are superior to all rival hosts in the battles; you are the slayer of the malevolent, the progenitor, and the conqueror of all. Do you overcome those who seek to overcome us.
The two worlds have followed after your surging strength, as two mothers follow their young.
All your rivals submit to your wrath when you, O Indra, strike down Vṛtra.
From here, for your aid, [I call] the ageless one, the hurler who is never sent forth.

We invoke for protection the common Indra, the possessor of wealth, who bestows riches— the swift victor, the striker, the best of charioteers, the unconquered, the strengthener of Tugra’s son; the restorer of what was unmade, the one made by might, the one with a hundred aids and a hundred powers.
Here I come before you in person; all the gods follow behind me.
When you, O Indra, have assigned a portion for me, then through me you shall perform heroic deeds.
I place for you first a draught of honey; let the pressed Soma be your allotted portion.
And you, my friend, are on my right; then let us two slay many Vṛtras together.
Bring forth a true hymn of praise to Indra, seeking strength, if indeed truth exists.
"Indra does not exist"—so says some one; who has seen him? Whom then shall we praise?
Here I am, O singer; behold me here! By my greatness, I surpass all created beings.
The quarters of Truth increase me; bursting asunder, I rend the worlds apart.
When the longing ones have ascended toward me, who sit alone upon the back of the beloved Truth.
My mind, fashioned by thought, has spoken back to my heart; my friends, possessing young offspring, have cried out in joy.
All those deeds of yours are to be proclaimed at the Soma-pressings, O Maghavan Indra, which you performed for the one who presses the juice.
When you opened the treasure brought from afar, heaped up in abundance, for Śarabha, the kinsman of the seer.
Run forth now toward Pṛthu; let him not hold you back here.
Indra has hurled his thunderbolt down upon the vital organ of Vṛtra. Moving with the speed of thought, he rushed forward and shattered the iron fortress.
Having gone to heaven as a fair-winged bird, he brought the Soma for the wielder of the thunderbolt.
Within the ocean lies the thunderbolt, completely enveloped by the waters.
To him, they bring tribute from the front, flowing together in a continuous stream.
When Vāk, the queen of the gods, the delightful one, sat down speaking words that lack consciousness;
when she milked out the fourfold vigor and the waters—where indeed has her highest part gone?
The gods generated the goddess Vāk; cattle of every form speak her.
May she, the cow, the Speech, yielding for us pleasant refreshment and vigor, come to us with fair praise.
O friend Viṣṇu, stride out further; O Heaven, grant space for the hurling of the thunderbolt.
Let us two slay Vṛtra and release the rivers; let them flow forth, set free at Indra’s impulse.
Truly, that mortal has succeeded in his service to the gods,
who now brings Mitra and Varuṇa for his aid and for the offering of oblations. O kings of most exalted dominion, far-seeing heroes, you are the ones most renowned for your hearing.
Those two, through their wondrous power, move like arms upon the chariot together with the rays of the sun.
O Mitra and Varuna, the swift messenger who ran before you—
iron-headed and eager for exhilaration— has sped forth.
