He who does not mingle with us, nor delights in being invoked again, nor in conversation—protect us from him today through our union; protect us with your arms!
O you who abide by the *ṛta*, offer a helpful song to Mitra and Aryaman.
Sing a protective, pleasing word of praise to Varuṇa, a hymn to the kings.
They have sent forth the ruddy, noble one, the sole son of the three.
Those immortal ones, undeceived, look down upon the domains of mortals.
Take heed of my uplifted words, most splendid deeds to be performed;
come both of you, O Nāsatyas, in harmony, to enjoy the oblations. Since we invoke your non-demonic bounty, O you who possess the wealth of horses, for your sake.
O Heroes, being praised by Jamadagni, extend the eastern oblation.
O Vāyu, come to our heaven-touching sacrifice with benevolent thoughts.
This bright, purified [Soma], being mixed above the filter, is offered to you.
The Adhvaryu priest comes by the straightest paths to receive the oblations for their enjoyment.
Therefore, O Lord of the teams of horses, drink of both: the pure Soma and that mixed with milk. Truly, O Sūrya, you are great; truly, O Āditya, you are great.
The greatness of you, who are great, is celebrated; truly, O God, you are great. Truly, O Sūrya, you are great in glory; altogether, O God, you are great.
By your greatness, you are the divine Asura, the domestic priest of the gods, the pervasive and invincible light.
This [cow], which was lowly and lacking luster, has been made beautiful by Rohiṇī;
like a marvel, she is seen approaching within the ten arms.
Three generations have indeed passed away; others have entered into the light on every side.
Great indeed he has stood within the worlds; as Pavamāna, he has entered the golden rays.
Mother of the Rudras, daughter of the Vasus, sister of the Ādityas, navel of immortality— I shall now proclaim this to the discerning people: do not slay the cow, the sinless Aditi!
The mortal of feeble intellect has not seized the cow— the goddess who knows speech, who utters her voice, who stands near with all sacred thoughts, and who has come forth from the gods.
O Agni, you, a god, bestow great vital strength upon the one who offers oblations.
The sage, the master of the house, the youth— O Agni, together with that *īḷā* which honors the gods,
bring them hither, O radiant one, you who are full of knowledge.
With you indeed as our ally, O most youthful one, who are the best at impelling, may we prevail for the winning of booty.
Like Aurva, Bhr̥gu, and Apnavāna, I call upon the pure one.
I invoke Agni, whose garment is the ocean, the sage who sounds like the wind, the power that roars like Parjanya—
Agni, whose garment is the ocean.
I call upon Agni, who is clothed in the ocean, as I call for the impulse of Savitṛ and the enjoyment of Bhaga;
I call upon Agni, the most frequent guest at our sacrifices, who causes them to prosper.
Toward the powerful grandson [of the gods],
so that this Tvaṣṭṛ may come to us like a form to be fashioned,
through the will of this glorious one.
This Agni, who rules over all splendors among the gods,
may he come to us with strengths.
Praise here the most glorious one among all the Hotṛ-priests.
Agni, the foremost in sacrifices, sharp and with purifying luster, who is the eldest dwelling within the homes,
has shone forth as the one most widely renowned.
O sage, praise him who is like a prize-winning steed, the powerful one, who stirs men like Mitra.
Toward you, the sisters— the voices of those who have prepared the oblation— reach out with their instructions.
They have taken their stand in the presence of Vāyu; he for whom the threefold, unobstructed, and secure sacrificial grass has been spread— he has established his footstep.
The station of the bounteous god, with his unassailable protections,
is auspicious to behold like the sun.
O Agni, God, glowing with your flame through the offerings of clarified butter!
Bring the gods here and offer sacrifice to them.
The gods, the mothers, have generated you as a sage, O Aṅgiras—
the immortal bearer of oblations.
Thee, O Agni, the wise one, the excellent messenger, the bearer of oblations, they have established here, O Seer.
For I possess neither a cow that should not be slain, nor an axe for felling the forest.
Now I bring such [an offering] to you:
O Agni, whatever pieces of wood we place upon you,
enjoy them, O youngest one!
Whatever the woodlouse eats, whatever the ant crawls over— may all that become ghee for you.
Kindling Agni with his mind, let the mortal man attend to his prayer.
To Agni, kindled with the rays of light— He, the best finder of the path, in whom men have established their sacred vows, has been made manifest.
May our songs of praise reach Agni, the strengthener of the noble one, as soon as he is born.
Agni, the son of Divodāsa, has gone forth toward the gods with his might;
he has spread himself across the mother earth and stands upon the summit of the firmament.
Before him the people tremble as he performs deeds worthy of praise.
Worship Agni with your prayers, as if for the winning of a thousandfold booty at the sacrifice itself. O Vasu, the mortal who offers gifts to you— whomsoever you wish to lead toward wealth—
that man, O Agni, gains by himself a hero who recites hymns and brings a thousandfold prosperity.
He pierces even that which is firm; with his steed he wins booty, and he acquires imperishable fame.
O Lord of many riches, we ever place all desirable things within you among the gods.
He who distributes all wealth is the joyous invoker of men.
Like the first vessels of honey for him, hymns go forth toward this Agni.
Like a chariot-horse, the bounteous ones, seeking the gods, polish him with their songs.
O wondrous Lord of the People, protect both our children and our progeny; bring us the wealth of the generous patrons.
Sing forth to the most generous one, the observer of cosmic order (*ṛtāvan*), the great one with brilliant luster—
to Agni, you who offer praise! May the bountiful lord, kindled and invoked with splendor, win for us glory accompanied by heroic sons.
Will his most recent benevolence surely come toward us with spoils of war?
Praise Agni, the most beloved of the beloved, the guest of this world, the driver of chariots.
He who, being praised, knows both what is proclaimed and what is hidden, and brings forth wealth worthy of sacrifice;
he whose waves are difficult to overcome as they flow down the slope, seeking to win the prize through inspired thought—
may that guest Agni, the Vasu, highly extolled by many, not be angry with us.
He who is the excellent invoker and the master of the sacrifice—
let none of those who address you with their prayers, O Vasu Agni, nor any others, come to harm through any divine powers. For even the lowly man,
having offered oblations and being skilled in the ritual, seeks you for the office of messenger.
O Agni, come as a friend of the Maruts with the Rudras to drink the Soma;
rejoice in the excellent praise of Sobhari, O giver of light.
